[2025-04-14T06:20:15.767Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1361224519456522422
Hi! I am the technical lead for this project, tasked with guiding and assisting our team of researcher-programmers in building the τaos decentralized simulation framework  I will also be available to answer questions you may have related to the technical function, and to investigate and assist with any problems faced by miners and validators in setup and operation once the codebase is finally shared and the experiment begins 

Was hoping to introduce myself with a link to the Github repo for our automated trading subnet, but we have unfortunately encountered a couple delays resulting from problems uncovered during final detailed testing in preparation for the release  
These relate primarily to the properties of the generated "background market" on top of which miners will operate, which requires careful selection of parameters and tuning of agent logic to produce stable and realistic order-book dynamics.  Although all components are in place and we have been running τaos simulations in our test environment already for some time, it is important that issues with the background model be resolved prior to release as this affects several aspects which are key to the proper and useful function of the subnet:


If the market is not well-structured, miners may not be able to achieve meaningful results with otherwise well-designed strategies.  This may also create a route for exploitative techniques to be applied.
,
Improper parameter selection can lead to inefficiencies in the function of the simulator, and result in wasted computation by participants.
,
The integrity and realism of the simulation data produced is of course important to attract institutions and researchers in the financial space to apply our system for their investigations.
,

We realise this has been much delayed, and thank you again for your patience - we're pushing hard to get our vision finally manifested within a week or less, and this is an unfortunate but critical distraction which we need to deal with in order to launch into a healthy subnet.

We have started setting weights from our owner key to this end, and are requesting all validators to kindly either childkey our owner hotkey 5EWwdZB7qCCMaAso5Mzcks4UUcPxKYvpAj32t5Mg1v6HSxoF, or if you are validating already in the subnet (or prefer to register your own validator), then to deploy the attached temporary validator code which assigns all weight to the burn UID.

If you need any assistance in deploying the temporary logic, please reach out to us, but should be just a matter of saving the script to your machine and launching via:

[2025-05-08T23:03:24.687Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1370174278858838069
@mvtrx・79  Have just published an update which addresses the issue of inactive miners earning rewards - miners must now maintain their trading volumes over a rolling window of 24 hours of simulation time at or above the value of the initial capital allocated at the start of simulation in order to receive the full rewards calculated on their risk-adjusted performance.

We have deployed this change to our validator, and reset all scores so that miners that do not execute any trades will receive 0 weight.  The scores of active miners will rise over time as their cumulative trading volumes increase.

This update also includes a fix for an issue occurring in the simulator during handling of agent deregistration under certain circumstances.

Validators : Please delete the running validator and simulator processes and execute the run_validator.sh script to deploy the update.
Miners : No action necessary, except to get those trading volumes up

[2025-05-11T14:29:29.120Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1371132108713492583
Got it – but the application is financial market context, to develop better risk managed algorithms; these algorithms not only try to maximize profit-n-loss, but do this with very good inventory controlling in mind

Financial markets is one of the biggest areas of application of many human made methods, ranging from physics to economics and beyond, and financial markets are important for most fields we know today

Those include, say, agriculture and resources, commodities, etc. Understanding the risk in trading them, or holding on to them, is something that is especially underdeveloped in cryptocurrency markets

So essentially, if you have in mind everyday-use, it would be the application of AI-methods to control risk related to their wealth and investments, actively (dynamically) managed, rather than long-term passively

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-05-11T14:33:31.346Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1371133124682973285
We will surely start to make more effort to build a better understanding of all this to a wider public, at this stage most likely traders, finance professionals, academians, and other industry related people will get it why it is important. But risk itself is very poorly understood concept in the world by ordinary folks. They would rather place everything on bad luck (or good fortune), than believe they could have actually controlled the risk they have taken. Risk is very hard to understand because if a bad event does not happen, the you might think you don't have to account for that. But that's obviously the wrong conclusion. And when you manage risk very well, then you don't see the bad outcome happening, which may make you wonder you have just spent countless hours and money to manage risk that never happens. Again the wrong conclusion. People don't think risk management is relevant, because they think it is out of their control, and people tend to underestimate risks to stay positive

[2025-05-12T14:35:45.922Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1371496077001490533
Each trade price series represents the evolution of one simulated market; each market consists of a set of "background agents" which we configure to produce a realistic price path and orderbook dynamics, together with the miners which seek to maximize their risk-adjusted performance across all markets.
You can click the links under "Book" column in the Trades table to inspect a particular book in more detail.
You can also examine the performance of a particular miner by clicking a link under the "Agent" column in Trades or Agents table (note that only agents with positive ID will display data - these are the miners, negative IDs are the background agents). (edited)

[2025-05-12T17:33:12.883Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1371540733592473642
The Bittensor protocol models key registration as a dynamic market expected to be related to the value of UID ownership - this is a competition by design.  The entities which aggressively register into the subnet are willing and have tools which enable them to acquire a substantial quantity of UIDs, and they are able to maintain their registration by acting in line with the requirements of the subnet incentive mechanism.

The price of registration will steadily increase as they continue this behaviour, until reaching a point where they either are no longer willing to pay the cost for registration, or they can no longer maintain their registrations as other more successful miners enter and overtake them in terms of incentive.  We will of course monitor the situation, and will be regularly tuning and refining the simulations and incentive mechanism in a manner that provides opportunities for intelligent agents to distinguish themselves.

We can increase the rate of registration cost increase as suggested, but this will still only allow others to register at higher price than this entity is willing to expend unless developing equivalent or more powerful registration tooling; the market will decide this threshold more precisely with the current lower (default) rate of increase.

[2025-05-12T18:09:20.257Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1371549824218042510
True that the range of incentives is currently very low, this is one of the parameters that can be tuned - miners that perform consistently better than others are though anyway still able to maintain higher placements in the subnet. As stated by @7/., only very good algorithms will measure consistently significantly higher than the rest in terms of the metrics employed - currently we do not see (you can confirm at our dashboard) any agents achieving results that distinguish them substantially from others, the distribution of incentives is thus as should be expected.

The registration component will diminish over time as "fair value" for registration is reached; then other miners can more easily enter and, if performing better than the status quo, all the keys acquired by this entity will ultimately be replaced.  We cannot do anything to prevent aggressive registration as this is a protocol-level consideration, which has existed in competition-driven form for most of the history of BT.

[2025-05-13T09:31:26.421Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1371781878968877056
This was also planned to be written soon, but let me give a quick introduction in very "conceptual manner" of what the monitor shows. For those with "quant" background, it is obvious, with their experience with similar, or more complicated Bloomberg terminals, etc, but here the key is just the concept of running multiple simulations at the same time. Further info to monitor will be coming up, and it may end up looking like a Bloomberg monitor, tbh. 

Anyhow, you know the movie Matrix? Your life if a realization, it does not have to be a real one. It is one out of thousands simulated ones. You do not even know if you live in a simulated one, because it is so real. One "path realization" in our framework is just like that. But we run multiple ones at the same time to understand what kind of behavioral patterns are possible, since your life may consist of different choices, and the others can react differently to yours.

So, running multiple "life scenarios" simultaneously and taking an average of them does give your "expected behavior" and "expected performance," rather than just one out of thousands, which could be marked by luck or un-luck. This position is made typically in finance, and in mathematical finance regularly, especially in option pricing. But why it matters here is that we understand the probabilities better, the risk better, while allowing the freedom to act in each of the "realizations" (lives).

@mvtrx・79 I do see that new miners are largely not reaching the incentive level of established miners within immunity; as an immediate step to allow new miners some additional time to set up and establish their strategy we have increased immunity period to 7200 blocks (~1 day) (from 5000).

We will continue to monitor the situation, and assess in more detail up to and following tomorrow's update, since this will reveal additional details of the score calculation introduced in the previous update which are not yet readily observed at the dashboard.

We do however also observe some discrepancies in weights assigned to new miners between validators; notably R21 seem to have zero weight set on a number of new miners which are weighted comparably to the older registrations by our own vali.   This is evident also in the fact that while incentives of new miners are lower than established UIDs, consensus values are more closely aligned.

We will be in touch with other validators in order to ensure they are able to operate successfully and are receiving miner responses, as well as to request details allowing us to display their validation data at the dashboard.  Miners should also check that they are receiving and responding to requests from all validators.

@mvtrx・79  Updates listed below will be deployed shortly (in the next ~2 hours):


Refinements and additions to monitoring via [taos.simulate.trading](https://taos.simulate.trading/), notably illustrating the trading volume requirement imposed on miners and improving transparency on miner activity.  Note the addition of 24H volume statistic to agent table and dashboard; the "Activity" column indicates the factor by which Sharpe-based score is multiplied to ensure continuous active trading by miners.
,
Non-uniform initial capital allocation between cash and asset to miner agents; this is only one of several updates designed to motivate miners to place more attention on smart inventory control.  The immediate effect is not expected to be major due to selection of conservative parameters for the distribution, but miners should make extra sure to account for their inventory position in their trading strategy.
,
A first optimization to the simulator computational performance, aimed at accelerating simulation progression and preparing for larger experiments.  We expect a modest improvement in the rate at which simulation time progresses relative to real time, such that miners may receive requests from validators more frequently than before.
,
Revisions and improvements to state management for handling of persistent scoring across simulation configurations; this ensures that scoring data from previous simulations is more completely carried over when a new simulation begins, and prepares the system for more significant updates to the simulation configuration (expect book count to increase at the next update ).
,
Tweaks and refinement to simulation configuration, background agent logic and scoring parameters.  No major adjustments made in this version, but should observe some subtle changes in the structure of the simulated markets.
,

Required Actions (when the changes are pushed - we will make another announcement when this happens):

Validators 
We request to execute in the repo directory a git pull, and then execute the run_validator.sh script - have made a change to the script which removes the previous processes and session before updating (hence the pull needed), and would be ideal to have the next simulation runs started around the same time for easier comparisons and investigations; there are also some updates to the reporting which are needed for proper display of all data at the updated dashboard (we will be in touch shortly to request details so you can be added here).  Otherwise, the auto-update should take care of things once your current simulation run ends.
Miners 
You will just need to pull the latest changes to accommodate some revisions to the structures contained in the state synapse, and restart your miner.  Also of course make sure to check that your inventory control is in order for the new capital distributions! (edited)

[2025-05-20T09:13:20.258Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1374314038330392686
Either you have not done enough trading volume, or only have momentarily high Sharpe.  Rewards are calculated based on a moving average of Sharpe observations, you have to maintain consistently high Sharpe over a longer time period.  You can check out your traded volume and performance history at [taos.simulate.trading/agents](https://taos.simulate.trading/d/edy6vxytuud4wd/agents)
Link: https://taos.simulate.trading/d/edy6vxytuud4wd/agents

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-05-20T10:11:35.093Z] L‘assaymphonie
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1374328696730554398
What's the shifting window

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-05-20T11:29:20.748Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1374348265906110515
The instantaneous Sharpe ratio at each update is calculated using the configured number of previous observations set via scoring.sharpe.lookback at validator side (currently set to 100).
The final score which becomes miner weight is obtained as a moving average of previous scores according to the formula at https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/5f57a452e413e7eb7fd92ca02a2a79d8f8c0f089/taos/common/neurons/validator.py#L375
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/5f57a452e413e7eb7fd92ca02a2a79d8f8c0f089/taos/common/neurons/validator.py#L375
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/5f57a452e413e7eb7fd92ca02a2a79d8f8c0f089/taos/common/neurons/validator.py
Link: https://opengraph.githubassets.com/1f00bee36f8f14a661fc7acd379d4e22ea647450039bf2e09b18b575a7f0098c/taos-im/sn-79

https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1374722901600632832
@mvtrx・79    Updates being deployed later today:


Trading Fees : Miner agents will incur transaction costs for their trading activities; this is implemented using a tiered structure where higher daily trading volumes will result in lower fee rates.  The schedule of fees will be seen in the new [simulation config](https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/main/simulate/trading/run/config/simulation_0.xml) once the update is pushed.  This creates better alignment with real-world trading considerations, requires agents to account for transaction costs in their decision making and further encourages active trading.
,
Price Jumps : The price generation process will be modified to include a jump diffusion component which produces sudden changes in the underlying value of assets in the simulation.  Although parameters are conservatively set in order to allow careful observation of the effects, this represents a step towards incorporating more robust "news-like" events into the simulation, improving realism and illustrating the first of two major classes of "price shocks" that influence real market behaviour.
,
More Books : The total number of concurrent simulations will be increased from 10 to 20, providing better statistical significance for the results.
,
Increased Miner Capital : The initial capital allocated to miner agents will be increased in value from 60000 to 100000, allowing greater impact on the market and more weight with which to capitalize on profitable opportunities.
,
Validator Updates : Various optimizations to improve running performance on validator side and increase rate of simulation progress, and updates for handling of data and configuration related to new features.
,
Monitoring : A couple of refinements and additions to metrics and [taos.simulate.trading](https://taos.simulate.trading/), including breakdown of traded volume in terms of role at agents dashboard.
,

We will post an announcement here again once the updates have been pushed (~16:00 UTC)
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/main/simulate/trading/run/config/simulation_0.xml
Link: https://taos.simulate.trading/

Validators

Miners

[2025-05-23T08:53:27.288Z] 7/.

This is just for the Level 1, which is "mandatory" for all, after that it drops by half (for maker, a bit less for taker), and then further. So essentially, as everybody starts with that level, it does not pose a real concern when you compare the performance to others. Those that would however continue to execute more, will get them cheaper. Since the principle is the equal for both making and taking, at level 1, it is rather innocent assumption and done to give enough space for the other levels to drop close to zero. Later, some of them will turn into rebates (negative costs), that is the plan. (edited)

Then, there are also smaller exchanges, which the wider public might not be aware of, with even more intense schedules (see e.g. https://www.northcrypto.com/fees). The trading fees can naturally be adjusted, but the main motivation has been to allow those with active trading profile to have the possibility to gain some edge within a "single day trading," while also allowing us to do relatively "simple schedule" that can turn into negative costs as mentioned.
Link: https://www.northcrypto.com/fees

@mvtrx・79    This week's updates:


Self Trade Prevention : This is an important function which exists at real exchanges to facilitate order management for traders by preventing an account from trading against its own positions, which can also be enforced by the exchange to help mitigate certain types of price manipulation.
,
Simulation Parameter & Agent Logic Updates : Several refinements to the parameterization and behaviour of the background agents are employed to improve the statistical realism of the market.  The most important characteristics introduced in this update are the generation of additional "shocks" creating more dynamic and unpredictable price fluctuations.
,
Monitoring Improvements : Several refinements and additions to the reported metrics and dashboard will be deployed to help clarify certain concerns and visualize additional data allowing to better understand the behaviour of miners.
,

A number of other feature-related tasks are in planning and development, including updating of simulation checkpointing functionality, further profiling and optimization projects, enablement of quote-denominated order sizes, support for additional order and agent types, incorporation of real-world signals to the simulation, and more - these will be released in subsequent updates as they are completed and tested.

We will post an announcement here again once the current updates have been pushed (~16:00 UTC) (edited)

[2025-05-28T16:42:18.455Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1377326128242622585
@mvtrx・79   The updates described earlier ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠ have been pushed, and deployed at our vali  

Validators
If having availability to do so, please execute the run_validator script to pull and apply the latest changes immediately - otherwise will be auto-updated at the end of your current simulation run.

Miners
Please pull the latest changes and restart your miner; no other technical requirements, but if you wish to apply self-trade prevention options on your orders please see the example RandomMaker and RandomTaker implementations for illustrations of the usage.  There are 5 options for handling of self-trade scenarios:

NO_STP : No self-trade prevention, you will be able to match against your own orders.
,
CANCEL_OLDEST : If a self-trade would occur when placing an order, cancel the passive order and proceed to place the new order. [This is applied by default if no STP method explicitly specified]
,
CANCEL_NEWEST : If a self-trade would occur when placing an order, cancel the incoming order and leave the passive order in the book.
,
CANCEL_BOTH : If a self-trade would occur when placing an order, cancel both the incoming order and the passive order.
,
DECREASE_CANCEL : If a self-trade would occur when placing an order, the smaller of the passive and incoming orders will be canceled and the larger order will be decremented by the size of the smaller order. If the two orders are the same size, both will be canceled.
,
Also be aware that only the taker order STP rule is active.

Note that we have registered testnet netuid 366 and deployed a validator here, for miners who would like to make use of this facility.  Dashboard for testnet will be available soon. (edited)
Thursday, May 29, 2025 at 12:44 AM

[2025-06-03T10:23:06.303Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1379405025993949265
FYI. I will be explaining this out more in future blog posts too…

One thing to note is that risk can and will change over time. And then a system like here can come to rescue. AI will need a lot of data, and it cannot get that from history alone, because things change.

You can see some thoughts on this by, say, Myron Scholes (Nobel Prize winner):


”Even if you’re in a long run horizon, phase transitions are very important in risk. And what the data shows is that’s what we should be looking at. Not necessarily the level of risk today, but how it is changing. How to get information about changing risk to enhance our rates of return.”


It is really just a more general thinking than we apply here, but emphases  the nature of risk being time dependent.

https://www.top1000funds.com/2024/09/nobel-laureate-advises-a-different-focus-on-risk-to-enhance-returns/ (edited)

Indeed, we continually push to produce features and define configurations that move us closer to the big goals of the project, namely the creation and application of massive, high resolution, quality simulated datasets which allow traders, researchers, institutions and regulators to conduct novel studies of financial markets and carry out more robust analysis of risk factors than currently possible anywhere else.

Much of the involved workload does take place "behind the scenes" in the form of research, data analysis, profiling and testing to inform the decision making on market configurations and development planning.  This work enables our attempt to maintain a steady flow of visible updates which drive the simulated markets to create a more realistic and challenging environment for miners, encouraging application of the best risk management practices.

We are still in the early days of the project, so that addressing scaling considerations and tackling unpredictable issues that arise in the live operation also tends to feature in the timeline, but have seen overall a good level of stability interrupted only by technical glitches which were quite quickly resolved.

[2025-06-03T12:06:37.254Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1379431076610572408
In terms of the upcoming releases:


The first point of focus for June is on optimization; with several revisions on validator side applied this week, next goal is to upgrade the simulator - we expect to achieve at least 10-20x speedup with reduction in memory requirements over the next couple weeks, which enables to run many more concurrent simulations and thus simulate more "paths" to better understand risk in financial markets.  Increasing the simulation count is central to the value of the generated data, and these optimizations will allow us to reach the first milestone where we are able to claim statistical significance of the outcomes.
,
We plan to make more advanced order options available in stages, including quote-denominated size specification, additional timing strategy options (IOC, FOK, GTT), stop orders and potentially even hidden and iceberg orders.  This provides more flexibility for miners to dictate how they interact with the market in handling latencies and other considerations, allowing for even more intricate and realistic risk management strategies to be deployed.  We also already have functionality in the simulator enabling leveraged (margin) trading by agents which will be enabled for use by miners in future runs.
,
An expansion to the suite of background agent types is on the cards for this week, being part of the broader, ongoing task to continually direct the logic and parameterization of background agents to more accurately reflect real-world markets.  The current inclusion aims to create an additional source of "shocks" which trigger sudden moves in market price, creating a more dynamic, unpredictable and realistic simulation environment.
,
Real-world connections will be made in the simulator by incorporating signals from live markets, social media and other influential sources as inputs to modify the behaviour of our simulated markets.  This will require miners to expand their risk management to account also for unexpected events arising outside of the synthetic dynamics.
,
Visualization and analysis tools for detailed, high-resolution simulation outputs which allow to inspect the properties and behaviour of simulated markets are undergoing testing and refinement; results of these will be published once we have collected suitable datasets, and will allow to see concretely the effect of the incentivized participants and compare statistically to real markets.  This development forms part of the project to better explain and motivate the goals and purpose of the subnet, together with further extension and refinement to monitoring tools, documentation and marketing material.
,
 (edited)
Tuesday, June 3, 2025 at 8:08 PM

[2025-06-03T12:07:10.899Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1379431217727803392
As mentioned, several of these represent steps in continuously ongoing processes which will allow us to expand and refine the system to model real-world markets of all types ever more accurately, with increasing number of runs providing both statistical significance and generating vast quantities of data which can be used for analysis and the development of trading tools, including data-driven and AI-centric approaches which cannot be properly realised without this type of system in place.

The above compiles a small selection of the shortly upcoming releases that are necessary to reach the level of technical operation required for the application of data to become feasible, and only scratches the surface of what we intend to make possible through this system.

Once able to fully demonstrate the superiority of an incentivized, distributed simulation in producing meaningful data, ongoing marketing and discussions with relevant parties are hoped to lead into collaborations where the subnet will host simulations specified so as to hold immediate real-world practical applicability in the study of risk management, market microstructure, exchange mechanism design, and more.

For example:

I can say what we will be covering in a blog-post, or one of them. This is called the Hurst exponent and it is most typically related to long-memory characteristics and fractal properties. The Hurst exponent is typically over 0.5 (=H) in real markets, and the price series produced in the simulations also reach such numbers, around range 0.5 < H < 0.6. This means there is certain (long term) "predictability" in there, and certain range of time-scale that fractal properties in terms of self-similarity in statistical sense hold.

The fact that such match with the real time series is already a good and solid indicator that the roughness of the simulated paths are in par with real ones (again generally speaking). Of course, this in itself does not yet however indicate that the LOB dynamics are matching or aligning with real ones, so underneath the best prices and trade price (or mid-quote), the dynamics are being better matched in every upgrade we do. There are several ways to achieve this and we are investigating many approaches. The Hurst exponent, and the fractal "roughness" in itself is very interesting and warrants a blog-post.

As this may sound a bit academic, it does indicate that statistically speaking we are on the right "path" of roughness that matches the most financial time series. The fine-tuning to specific LOBs and assets is more time consuming but there again we follow general principles that span decades of research, and where we have both worked scientifically and in trading (practice). These all are mostly related to risk management, and the features we will be deploying both from the research angle and technical computational angles support each other in that we want to bring about the right measures of risk.

There are multitude of other statistical properties we already match well, reported also in literature.

And as we integrate real market data, like direction or sentiment of markets, into the simulations, the more it will get also in touch with the actual market data. The development is that we first put in the general characteristics, that we already match well, and then we go about the fine-tuning process, whereby we dig in deeper and deeper into the dynamics of the LOB, and how actually those characteristics are formed, not only as a black-box, but being able to explain them. This part is done by the "background agents," while the AI Agents (miners) are able to affect the dynamics themselves.

Hope this helps for now.

@mvtrx・79   First few updates for this week already released today:


Advanced Order Options : Miner agents will be able to submit [Immediate-Or-Cancel](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/i/immediateorcancel.asp) limit orders as well as specifying for their limit orders to be processed with Post-Only enforcement.  This provides intelligent agents with better control over their market impact and trading role.
,
Incentive Mechanism Update : The period over which Sharpe ratios are calculated is increased to 1 hour of simulation time, and the calculation is taken as the average over all books rather than using the change in total inventory value across all books.  This is a minor first step of several upcoming revisions to the incentive mechanism which aim to better reward intelligent active trading and penalize those who do not participate meaningfully in the simulated market.
,
Miner Trade Reporting : Miners' latest 5 trades on each book will be retained for display at the dashboard to improve visibility of behaviour.
,
Simulation Outputs Management : (Validators) Previous simulation outputs will be automatically compressed, and oldest archives cleaned up if disk space crosses critical threshold.
,

We will release latest on Wednesday some additional order options as well as more significant revisions to the incentive mechanism.  Stay tuned!

These updates were already pushed and deployed at our validator

Validators
If having availability to do so, please execute the run_validator script to pull and apply the latest changes.

Miners
Update should not be immediately required, but recommended to pull the latest changes to access the new order type options.  Illustration of how these are specified is given in an [example agent](https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/main/agents/OrderOptionAgent.py). (edited)

To give some fore sight to you. What can we expect from the newest package coming out more explicitly:


There will be a much-awaited connection to the real world market,  which can provide signals and help to make better and more nuanced trading strategies and especially risk management, and while this will be a bit experimental setting at first, we have a clear theoretical (proven) path to follow in the upgrades;
,


On Monday, we already released new more advanced order types (e.g. IOC), which can be used especially in these circumstances, and more order types will be made available in the new package upgrade, and we believe they should also affect the performance, so we recommend looking into them;
,


The direction of development is, as mentioned for 1-2 weeks, is to make things more non-random, with more signals to follow, and speed will be becoming more relevant now and in the future, with crashes and bubbles forming, with or without the AI Agents involvement – interactions will be left to be seen;
,


Since this is an exercise and practice of risk management tools, with maximal Sharpe in the process, we recommend paying attention to this development line, which we likely continue to the foreseeable future, suggesting that the value of the multiple price paths (LOBs, really) will become more prevalent;
,


For the aforementioned reasons, we will also be starting to give certain penalty on bad performance on the Sharpe Ratio, more than previously (more maybe after this), this being motivated by the fact that we want to incentivize more careful risk management and avoidance of "blunders" or "fat finger errors";
,


We will be dropping the requirement of trading capital per simulation ("24 hours"), and instead there will be an incentive to trade more actively throughout the day, and finding signals that actually matter, and optimize for the times to do so – this is also motivated by our desire to go more into the HFT realms;
,


Multiple other (smaller) features that are supportive will be announced, and their end-effect should be a positive one by expectation, and if we see improvements to be made, or surprising twists of nature, we shall be acting on those  in order to regain stability of the process and more meaningful incentives given.
,

Again, this is a package. We had to collect many of them together before releasing, and we are still working on to hone some of them. We believe this direction is both necessary and desirable to do. We have to put some restrictions on certain matters. They may be lifted also in the next versions, hereafter.

More details coming up! Thanks for your interest, and it has been useful to be in Paris Proof of Talk!

[2025-06-12T15:41:46.454Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1382746712510173194
@mvtrx・79  The next round of updates is now prepared for release in a short while:


More Advanced Order Options : Extending the IOC and Post-Only options deployed on Monday, miner agents will be able to specify [Fill-Or-Kill](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/f/fok.asp) and [Good-Til-Time](https://www.coinapi.io/learn/glossary/good-till-time-gtt) time-in-force options for their limit orders, as well as placing market orders with size denominated in quote currency.  This provides intelligent agents with additional options to better control their market impact and trading role, and enables to more accurately manage aggressive trading activity in volatile periods.
,
Real-World Data Integration : The evolution of the simulated market will now be influenced by data collected from the real market, specifically the trade price of the TAO perpetual futures contract on Coinbase.  A new agent type monitors the stream of prices from this source at a specified sampling interval (60 secs), and triggers a period of buying or selling dependent on the sign of the most recent return.  This update creates a source of predictability in terms of the market direction to provide an obvious means by which attentive agents are able to outperform idle competitors, while also enforcing a need for careful risk assessment paired with speedy reaction to beat others to the rewards.
,
Miner Testing Tools : Instructions and tools to enable miners to test their agents against the latest simulated background offline at their own machines will be added to the repo.
,
Incentive Mechanism Revision : Several innovations will be applied to improve the utility of the incentive mechanism with the goal of rewarding intelligent, informed and active traders while penalizing those who take excessive risks or remain inactive for significant periods.  We recommend to review the code once pushed in order to fully understand the changes, but will describe the key points below:
,


There is no longer a minimum volume requirement to receive full inventory-based scoring; rather, rewards are calculated using Sharpe values weighted by the volume traded during the assessment period.  This incentivizes active trading without setting specific arbitrary thresholds.
,
Inactivity is punished by decaying the activity factor which is multiplied onto the Sharpe values for each book - for each assessment period (currently 1H) where a miner remains inactive, their total score will be halved.  This decay resets whenever trading activity is detected.
,
A cap on the total volume allowed to be traded by a miner in any 24H simulation period is enforced.  If the miner trades more than 10x their initial capital, no orders will be accepted until 24H volume decreases below this threshold.  The volume weighting on the Sharpe ratio is also capped to provide no additional benefit to trading more than this volume.  This works with the volume-weighting of scores to prevent from creating a race only to achieve high trading volume.
,
A penalty is applied if a significantly lower performance is achieved on one book as compared to the others, this ensures that miners must manage risk well in all realizations.
,
STP now cannot be disabled, this is to avoid manipulations of the trading volume by matching against one's own orders.   If sending instructions with the NO_STP option specified, these will be rejected by the validator.
,
Miner capital is reduced from 120,000 to 100,000, to slightly reduce their possible impact while these changes are being monitored.
,

These updates will be pushed and deployed to our validator in the next couple hours (~17:00 UTC) (edited)
Thursday, June 12, 2025 at 11:43 PM
Link: https://www.investopedia.com/terms/f/fok.asp
Link: https://www.coinapi.io/learn/glossary/good-till-time-gtt

Now, we have taken many efficiences away, and also first introduction of real markets, becoming a hybrid simulation.

[2025-06-13T14:47:09.466Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1383095355691896874
The idea here is explicitly to optimize trading activity throughout the day especially with regards to the use of trading volume, or rather how it relates to the initial capital given at the start of the simulation challenge. One of the indicated problems in the previous setup was that the trader entities did a lot of trading volume sporadically, even carelessly, but now rather the way is to optimize a "budget" to trade during the day. One can imagine that these restrictions are placed by a (trading house) "manager" on the trader side, in order to keep the risk of the trader at check. In this case, the restriction is 10x, which may be edited in the next Wednesday's update, either to be smaller or bigger.  In this sense, we "simulate" the situation where there is a manager with control over the used capital, while the actual trading logic is up to the trader. There are multiple chances to find inefficiencies, but they are now in need of optimal use.

[2025-06-13T19:58:25.785Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1383173689851248713
Note taken. There is always some losers and winners, whatever we would do. Back in the day, we were mining, and we have a lot of first-hand experience gained from that. However, we had to act on this occasion quite seriously and develop an extended package that would put some cap on playing with volumes without any sense, as this would not be practical in real markets either. And we are going to push this into more realistic direction with more market impact, like in the real markets (if not considering the highest liquidity pairs). It was always the intent that high volumes have to be executed smartly, and that will also be playing a role in how different algorithms are going to compare. The only reason why that has not really happened yet is that it does require more in depth time with the LOB dynamics creation. But we also advise to look into that. We have also advised to look into the special order types that we have been pushing out lately, they can (or not) give an edge, when used well. Those would not expose to the same kind of risks as, say, the simplest order types. Also, previously, we had a requirement that you must trade a certain amount, but that was played away by just mindless volume. 

The only way we think is suitable, and is consistent with real markets if the description I gave above. 

And overall, although some have lost "unfairly," we feel the advantage from now is definitely in the corner of those that spend the time and energy to really try to compete well, and not, say, just play a registering game. As this was brought to our attention already some weeks ago, we started to design a system that would help to prevent that. If we were to announce such much before, those actors might as well just prepare accordingly, and the registering game would continue more easily. In essense, we have tried our best to protect the best miners, or those with intent to do really great stuff in this subnet. We value those entities, and would of course like to hear their feedback on the current situation.

Estimated next Wednesday, we may release other updates on these things, but if things do not progress badly, we would not expect any critical changes, more like fine-tuning of things. But please always be a bit prepared, especially if you already are aware that criticism has been expressed, and changes have been requested. We take those quite seriously, and the only reason why this took so much time from our side was that we started to do a big package and not small steps, in particular because we wanted to have a full-blown "better incentive scheme" that has features that all support the best miners, or those that want to be such. We know this may in some cases drop the ball from those that already try to do that, we have experienced the same back in the day, but like then, we feel it was quite necessary. In the bit longer run, there is no question in our view that it is in the best interest of the best miners to do this.

Also note that some of the changes, in such a big package, had to be planned and decided very late in the game, because the complexity is already quite high, with C++ also being slower to develop than Py.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-06-13T20:38:19.808Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1383183731111493632
Notice that there is one crucial bit of specialty in our system. This is that when the incentive mechanism has been fine-tuned to be good and working, and we have reached a level of practical relevance with our research related upgrades, including the already launched futures market integration – making it a hybrid simulation – the number of simultaneous simulations will work towards the actually best miners and algorithms. Why is this so? Because it will make the results more reliable, statistically speaking, and while we now provide 20 such simulations, I can already say the next upgrades will be taking this north, much north of that number. We have also intentionally wanted to make the incentive upgrades before such technolical leaps, because otherwise it would not create the desired effect. That means that "luck" plays less and less of a role. We would think this is in the advantage of the best of the best. To get to this point, we are working hard every week to think about the actual execution of the schemes, their potential weaknesses and strenghts. Still, much of the time also goes into technical implementation of efficiency, as it is not an easy thing to do work in C++. This has also caused us longer development cycles in the past, but once we get into the really good stuff, then we promise this will start to bring the fruit. While this technical thing may not yet be apparent to the miners, this should not go unnoticed either. Also there is a bag of tricks we have not used yet, perhaps only hinted at, and we want to use those feats somewhat sparingly to make this one of the best Sns out there. Patience, a bit, we ask — we are on a path that can be a significant one. We ourselves have had the patience of one year in the making from a technological perspective, and over 20 years in the research realm. Being of this level of complexity, with deadlines that matter, this is no easy feat, and we are gaining experience by monitoring and through your valuable feedback. (edited)
Saturday, June 14, 2025 at 5:47 AM

[2025-06-13T20:54:15.451Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1383187739369013348
To ”protect" those with good intentions but accidentally hitting their own orders, we now in the latest upgrade enforced the STP functionality, which is in practice enforced in all regulated exchanges, but not "mandatorily" so as one would expect the trader side to make sure they do not wash trade themselves. Here, we wanted to turn it on by default, and enforce, so that unexpectedly high trading volumes would not occur accidentally, and therefore hit the limit earlier. Those that still trade a lot, without hitting their own orders, yes they would be affected. I can say we are monitoring matters in this regard, and planning for different routes to be taken in different scenarios. If you have been given capital of, say, "100,000" then turning that imes over 10x is quite significant, at least we would regard so, as we are not yet in the ”HFT realm” of market making where very significant trading volumes can be created in a day. This and risk-averseness, as stated in our "subtitle of the subnet," lead us also into this. Once the market impact will be more significant, the best algorithms will, in our research agenda at least, float to the top and stay there. (edited)

This lead to a situation that nearly everybody got similar results, and this was reported, and since we could not start to see a spread between the performances, we started to build a package with many interconnected incentives and mechanisms (some of them punishing). In such a big package, some things will have to be going live without weeks of testing, simply because some of the matters depend on how the AI Agents perform – we do not know a prior what the miners will be doing. [2025-06-16T08:02:03.183Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1384080571348811916
We have stated what we will be doing this week, last week's package was big as was mentioned, also a few days earlier – and it was clear the incentive mechanism was going to be changed. Whether we change something dramatically this week or not, no, do not see any evidence from incentive scheme perspective that would require massive overhaul, but there will be incentive scheme parameter changes likely, which we are reviewing currently, and started to do immediately after the last version went out, when we saw the AI Agents (miners) reactions and potential strategy classes used. Our reactions are always partly dependent on what is going on from the miner side, as we cannot possibly know what they will be doing before release.

Secondly, real markets are dynamic. We have done both HFT, market-making, and speculative trading. This would span decades already in some format or another, and in the crypto realm also since 2015. These markets are extremely volatile and dangerous to trade in. Although our intent is not to create such hassle here, it is a fact that markets are dynamic and the game also changes over time, with institutions and funds entering and withdrawing from the markets. So, dynamic adjustment will anyhow be necessary, and we are getting only started to get to the real problems of the markets, including the deep LOB dynamics, gaps in the LOB, resiliency problems, and bubbles and bursts. These will all require to some extent "live testing."

It is basically a laboratory setting. We started (the subnet) 1-2 months ago in a field that is extremely challenging to model the whole structure of the market. This has never been done, anywhere, academically, and if privately done by some entity or company, it has not been revealed. Although we have about 10 people onboard, and years of experience in trading and also in Bittensor for a significant amount of time, from different perspectives, it remains a challenge to push realistic and yet correctly incentivizing features into such space, because we are giving "initial capital" to use, for free basically (you can count in the registration fee by the protocol) and the incentivize correctly agents that do not behave necessarily in the fashion like they would in real markets. This then requires another layer of thinking how the agents possibly will be behaving, to a large degree.

And that, those reactions, plus the technical difficulty level we do this all at, with C++ programming that seems to be totally unique in this chain to this date, means that we have many things to consider, and cannot proceed with just Python logic and testing into live. The learning curve is longer and steeper, and slowed down because of the technical limitations of the chain, which we will be testing to the limit, so in that sense yes I do believe this subnet is taking risks and chances with those who are onboard whether they want to partake in a subnet pushing boundaries, or whether they just remain relatively stagnant in some other subnet of easier entry barrier. But of course, if we make a mistake, which is possible in some pushes, we try our best to correct for them if we just see the evidence of that and can clearly identify the reason. So, feedback is valuable. (edited)

[2025-06-16T16:54:54.296Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1384214667915690004
@mvtrx・79    After much digging, we eventually isolated the reason for higher-than-expected timeout rates by miners to an apparent problem in handling simultaneous connection to all axons in a single call via the usual bittensor package query mechanism - in this case, long delays arise during forming of a connection to miners; this phase of the communication is also included in the timeout enforcement, leading to inaccurate measurements of the response times.

The exact reason for the connection delays here is still under investigation (we have tested with changes to networking config and with increases in available resources), and we will be in touch with the developers for a fuller understanding once we have completed our own dive, but have now pushed an update which modifies the manner in which the queries are executed so as to evade this issue and ensure accuracy of response times for each UID.

Since this method does however lead to a longer overall processing time for all queries, we have also made the adjustment that each miner will receive a state update synapse that contains only the accounts and notices data relevant to themselves.

Under this new mechanism, the processing time captured by the validator reflects only the time taken for the miner to respond, and thus the timeout parameter has been significantly reduced to 1.0 second.  This is also necessary to ensure that the total time taken to complete all queries remains reasonable.  We have been testing this at our validator for a short time prior to this announcement, and seeing the majority of miners responding within the timeout at each step.  We will continue to monitor and will adjust this parameter if seen to be necessary.

Validators
The update will be automatically pulled and deployed at start of the next simulation hour; to deploy immediately, please execute git pull && pm2 restart validator

Miners
No changes needed; if you were using account balances or notices from other UIDs than your own in your strategy, you will no longer be able to do so, but the structure of the synapse remains unchanged so that this does not necessitate any updates otherwise.
Please monitor and let us know if you are still experiencing issues with excessive timeouts after confirming your local processing times do not exceed or significantly contribute to your response time. (edited)

@mvtrx・79  Weekly update will be pushed to tomorrow to allow some extra time for finalizing testing on the simulator and validator optimizations; we are also still investigating further refinements to speed up query times as this currently presents somewhat of a bottleneck in enabling to dramatically increase the rate of simulation progression and start to scale up the book count.

This update will not contain any major changes at the level of the incentive mechanism, and only some minor tweaks to the parameters of the background model in the simulation, so should not expect any substantial action to be required in terms of strategy development.  The update does however modify the synapse structure and miners should be aware that they will need to upgrade to the latest version when released.  This does not affect the usage of the synapse data in agent logic, so no other changes are expected to be required.

We will announce more details of the changes during the day tomorrow, and will notify when pushed and deployed (tomorrow ~17:00 UTC).

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-06-19T13:44:22.262Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1385253882086817833
@mvtrx・79   As mentioned, this week's update focuses primarily on optimization with the goal of enabling to speed up simulation progression, and allowing for increases to the book count:


Simulator Optimization : The simulator parallelism implementation have been reworked to make maximal use of the available resources and avoid excessive concurrency overhead present in the previous version; the simulator is now quite capable of maintaining hundreds if not thousands of simulated orderbooks with reasonable speed of progression on the same modest hardware currently in use by our validator.
,
Validator Optimizations : All aspects of the query process have been examined in detail and optimized where possible; this includes networking parameter enhancements, extensive benchmarking and resulting improvements to message compression process, minification of the state update message subfields, as well as refinements to the score calculations.  The query processing still presents a bottleneck in terms of the overall simulation time, but is substantially improved such that overall progression rate will increase while miners and validators should experience significant reduction in network traffic, with faster response times also expected to be possible.  Further improvements are necessary to achieve our ultimate goal of 1000s of books, but this step should already allow for significantly more books to be sufficiently handled.
,
Book Count Increase : The initial increase in book count is a small bump from 20 to 24 books so as to allow to monitor the stability and performance of the enhanced setup and avoid introducing significant extra burdens immediately.  Once we have been able to observe the performance in live environment, decisions will be made as to when and in what amount the count will be increased in subsequent releases.
,
Background Model Tweaks : Just a few minor tweaks to the parameters of the background model are applied with the aim of increasing diversity of behaviour in response to the external signals between different books.
,

These updates will be pushed at ~17:00 UTC today.
Deployment to our validator will be executed ~1H following the push.

[2025-06-24T18:46:09.394Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1387141768230998037
In fact, we are going to update that incentive rewarding system tomorrow on Wednesday. @6/. can give more details otherwise, but from my part I can say that our goal is to start rewarding much more the ones on the top quartile. The exact form of that function will be decided tomorrow around noon UTC, but how this changes from the current one is that those below the average are getting much less than previously, and those at the top much more than previously. The target is to start incentivizing outstanding performance, and we are likely to support this change with other functions as well. The rest of the incentive mechanism is readable in the code, more exactly, but in general this is currently about risk-averse trading, targeting high-volume trading, which resembles high-frequency trading, but currently at lower frequencies. We are going to get faster and faster for the AI Agents ("miners") soon enough, but now there is a limitation on how frequently they can observe the limit-order-book (past orders, trades). The maximization of risk-adjusted returns, better known as Sharpe Ratio (there are also other candidates of course), is the current incentivization variable, and since we have many simultanenous simulations ongoing all the time (see taos.simulate.trading web-page), it is about "the average performance" (roughly speaking) over those simulations, so not only based on one simulation (realization path). This is a bit similar to numerical option pricing techniques. (edited)

[2025-06-25T13:20:46.082Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1387422269390979072
@mvtrx・79    This week's update introduces primarily several changes to the incentive mechanism and simulator agent parameters, aimed as always at better motivating intelligent, risk-averse and active trading strategies:


Reward Distribution : The assignment of scores to miners has been modified to increase the incentive allocated to top performing miners while reducing the rewards earned by average and lower performing UIDs.  This is necessary to foster a more competitive environment and avoid distributing emissions to miners who do not seriously attempt to achieve top performance.
,
Outlier Penalty Reduction : The penalty applied to miner scores where they have very poor performance in one or more books relative to the others is reduced to 67% of the current penalty.
,
FuturesAgent Template : An additional simple agent strategy template is included which incorporates the same external signal used to guide the direction of the simulated markets in its decision-making.  This real-world connection was intended to provide a clear path to making valid price predictions in the simulated market; this template illustrates in a very simple form how this might be achieved.  We encourage all miners to examine and test this strategy, and expect that the competition for top position would be between miners who most cleverly extend this template to maximize their Sharpe ratios and trading volumes, and those who innovate alternate ways to take advantage of this presumed predictability by capitalizing on other miners' movements.
,
Book Count Increase : Number of books will be increased from 24 to 32.
,
Fee Elimination : In this upcoming simulation, fees will be set to zero for all agents in order to eliminate the transaction costs as a potential reason for agents to avoid more active trading strategies, and to reduce the level of difficulty in attaining positive risk adjusted performance.
,
Volume Cap Increase : The maximum volume allowed to be traded in a 24H window is increased from 10x the initial capital to 20x initial capital.
,
Active Order Limitation : The maximum number of orders that an agent may keep open on any given book at one time will be limited to 100.  This is applied initially to ensure that extremely large numbers of open orders are not accumulated as this can affect the perfomance of simulator and increase traffic and processing time for miner queries, and may be decreased further in later releases so as to also encourage more active order management and prevent lazy overly-passive strategies from being deployed.
,
Background Model Tweaks : A few adjustments to the parameters of the background model are applied with the aim of strengthening the market reaction to the external price signal and increasing the likelihood and magnitude of background agents' attempts to take advantage of more volatile market conditions.
,

These updates will be pushed at ~15:00 UTC today.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push. (edited)

[2025-06-25T13:36:54.222Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1387431340022169681
In the description, we will be later this week motivating things more. I did already give a description above (earlier), plus more will be written in July and published in different formats. Finally, we would be getting into the more serious AI development side, first we just need to get certain incentives correct.

At this point, notice that the rewards distribution is actually following a statistical rule known as the Pareto Rule (20-80 Rule). This rule has already been applied in a different context in our codebase, and it is a very well-known statistical finding especially concerning the distribution of wealth in economy.

Pareto Rule is a power-law, with heavy tails. This means that the distribution drops quite quickly, faster than an exponential would, but leaves heavier tails. In fact, these distributions don't have variance defined, and in some cases not even the mean. That means there is a lot of dispersion. That said, 20 % of the people get 80 % of the wealth – here the rewards.

[2025-06-25T20:14:45.292Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1387526452588576798
@mvtrx・79 Some suggestions based on the most recent update:

We have taken out the transaction costs in order to invite more trading volume, which may have been blocked in the fear of making the wrong decision, thus ending up in the red with bad Sharpe, and volume weighting. Therefore, fee structure has been zeroed for now, before AI templates will be available and other common type of approaches are seen to be applied.

Based on our monitoring, we also wanted to lessen the penalty in the "left-hand tail," of Sharpe Ratio, meaning that getting a bad Sharpe would not yet make it impossible to compete with those that are not taking the chances. We may adjust this later on, but for now, we wanted to lessen the impact of those potentially bad Sharpes that occur every now and then.

Thirdly, as we have observed that some of the opportunites in the market have not been attempted to be taken advantage of, we decided to launch a template algorithm that would clearly indicate some statistical arbitrage opportunity, or at least for now such exists, assuming not too many would do exactly the same. This is just a simple template.

Obviously, more templates are in the plans, and we are pushing towards releasing "AI" template that may already come out next week (Wed), and that should allow more and more opportunities to be found. And then, we will concentrate on the market dynamics, and potentially releasing a few more templates if need be. This is to advise on "what potentially to do."

We will also release what you might call "trading README" that concentrates on what the reasoning is behind the incentive scheme, and what type of things could be done, at least from our "generic perspective" (we are not going to give details) – all that would be done to help more diversity to take place and invite more serious competition based on AI.

This week's goal as explained in the messages above is to get those that find edge to gain more rewards, and conversely, those that would not seek such edge not perform as well. This direction was based on several discussions we had also with other people running similar things in the ecosystem – although we took a less radical road in this respect.

The volume weighting has stayed in there, although it could be put even more weight next week, of course depending on what would be observed. The goal of the volume weighting of Sharpe was discussed quite a lot previously already, so not going to go there for now, but the intent is obviously to get the "good volume" to be rewarded, and "bad volume" penalized.

We did not push for the extra weighting yet, since we put out the template for one typical approach, which can clearly change some of the strategies, or hopefully used as a building block, or risk management tool. At the same time, based on monitoring, we changed some of the parameters of the "background agents" (that do part of the LOB) to reflect this change.

The goal is to move towards more AI-dependent algorithms, and we therefore increase the number of LOBs (simulations) prudently, now going just above 30. The next steps may be to go 2* each week up to about 1000, but it will remained to be seen whether there are resource considerations that will put some breaks on this development or not.

Overall, we want to help to build those algorithms to be better, since our analysis suggests that the competition is not out there to the extent we would hope for. Our observations suggest that volume is not yet appreciated enough, and we pumped up the previous 10x (upper limit related to initial capital given) to 20x. This is also to alleviate stress on "trading too much."

Next week may see some corrections to this scheme, based on the evidence we will see, but we simply could not keep the current system intact, since it was not creating quite realistic type of trading scenarios. We try to help to create algorithms that would fit in the longer run goal of the subnet, based on AI and "deep" HFT.

We do review the stuff that is going on, and what we have been seeing in the past is very small trading volumes without genuine attempt to risk manage, except with making almost no sensible actions. This would not be considered to be sound risk management to "lay low" and let others to take the risks. True, if somebody accidentally or by skill hit a good spot, they would be rewarded, and we have to review if this would be too unstable, and then we make it more stable. But stability is about not making trades and attempt to risk manage, at least not in the fashion we have envisioned the long-term goal of this net, which is the "AI advised deep HFT." To that direction, whether it is "deep market making" or "deep statistical arbitrage" we have decided from day zero and beyond go to to. And stability is increased by the simultaneous simulations, so what happens in one simulation is just of the many, and while we can increase these to thousands, we have not yet done so – for the simple reason that was requested to be conversative and not increase any resource side at this point. We are trying to approach it "conservatively" for now, but it is almost impossible to know in advane all the responses from the "AI Agents" outside of the "background agents." At least a priori. Anything you can suggest of course will be evaluated and taken hint at. We are here to do that. This is not a political answer. You can send your proposal say in DM if you prefer. We will consider all such proposals.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-06-25T20:58:53.298Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1387537559130869830
If you have a good signal, you can amplify that by the trading volume. If you believe you have such signals, this is clearly beneficial strategy. But note that there is a risk involved: if that signal turns out to be bad, there is also a penalty that is based on the distribution of those Sharpes (across the simulations). So, a couple of bad mistakes can lead to a penalty, but then again, very good performance with good volume across simulations will take you to 20 % top. To make this stable, in our view, is about having those simultaneous simulations going on, as we of course undertand mistakes happen in risk management and in trading, sometimes PnL goes down, MDD is >10 % and so on. But the point is to try to hit the right spots, and if observing a mistake across the simulations in the strategy, then advised to "manage that risk" either by the advanced order-types we have put in, or take precautions and not run with the herd – the typical stuff that may happen in such complex systems. Sometimes in the real markets somebody hits the jackpot, even by pure luck, but we try to avoid its influence "in continuous rewarding system" by having the simultaneous simulations. True, it might be this is too far taken, and we may take it to evalation over the whole trading day. Has been one of the plans. But, then, this is clearly not rewarding "in continuous time," as our target has been to go into "deep HFT" type of scenario, with continuos inventory control, and careful order placement in the book. And those aggressive orders, we allow them to be taken now even without transaction costs, so those that attempt to leverage on that risk they take, can do so without harmful transaction cost, but at the same time, they will gamble if they do not have a genuine signal behind that. And staying just behind everybody, with limit-orders, well, this is not something that, say, market-makes or active traders would pursue either. They want to actually build up the PnL consistently over the day. One of the things, I can say already, in the preparations, is to move to a bit different calculation method of the PnL. More about that later. It is a process we are doing here, and sometimes have to take some steps into the unknown. We are trying to keep the "continuous rewarding system" because it is in a way much more exciting to succeed in that, rather than wait for the horses to finish in 10,000 mile race.

------------------------------------------------------------

There was no intent to reward old miners, the latest update changed the distribution of rewards so that top performing miners receive a majority of rewards, and average and lower performing UIDs receive substantially less.
We have noted that new registrations typically receive a high score initially, this is just a product of the details of the Sharpe calculation and the effect of having a shorter history of observations on which to assess - the effect dissipates quite quickly, but we will most likely adjust this so that new miners only receive scores once a full window of observations is available. [2025-06-27T16:08:51.148Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1388189344954585178
@mvtrx・79  We have pushed and deployed a minor update in order to start addressing some issues in the incentive distribution; no action needed from miners or validators (will be deployed automatically at the start of the next simulation hour).  The update includes:


Sharpe Assessment Window Fullness Requirement : Newly registered miners will not receive a score until enough observations to amount to 80% of the Sharpe assessment window (currently 1 simulation hour) are available.  This is to prevent unfair assignment of high scores to newly registered miners due to incomplete assessment data.
,
Moving Average Alpha Adjustment : The parameter which determines the period of the EMA applied to miner scores is adjusted so as to amount to ~5 minutes of simulation time.  This is aimed at decreasing the variance of incentives and better rewarding consistency; this slight increase in the period is likely just the first step in this direction, with other modifications and further gradual adjustments to this parameter to be made over the coming weeks.  This is necessary also to attempt to reduce the vTrust gap between ourselves and other validators, which results largely from discrepancies in weight assignment due to highly varying miner performance together with rapid changes in incentive values.
,

Investigation, evaluation and testing ongoing for several other matters related to the simulation model which will be announced next week, and may be other minor adjustments with similar objectives to the above depending on monitoring outcomes.

I don't think AI is yet a pre-requisite here in this subnet, but we are moving into a direction that would most likely benefit from its application and also releasing templates to speeden that progress. Since there is a "latency" (lag) that the AI Agents can now react with, this is well-suited for AI application. If we were to go down to sub-second reaction intervals, optimization of AI would become a harder task in terms of speed. On the other hand, there are market inefficiencies here that we have deliberately not attempted to directly take away, and other miners can create or take way such opportunities, we would expect things in that respect to get a bit more competetitive. Agents can also create new opportunities like in real markets.

@mvtrx・79  This week's update:


Incentive Adjustment : Scoring parameters are further adjusted to decrease volatility of incentives and better reward consistent performance.  EMA for score calculation is increased to 20 minutes and Sharpe assessment window is expanded to 2 hours (both in simulation time).  To avoid zeroing all scores until new Sharpe window is filled, scores will still be assigned once 1 hour of data is available.
,
Book Count Increase : Number of books will be increased from 32 to 40.
,
Taker Fee Re-Introduced : A 0.023% fee will be applied on taker trades executed by miners.  This is aimed at discouraging careless aggression and motivating provision of liquidity within the simulated markets.
,
Background Model Stability : Having observed some undesirable market conditions arising as a result of particular behaviour of miner agents, the background model parameters and logic have been refined so as to improve the stability of the simulated book state under extreme conditions.  This involves an increase in the reaction speed of HFT agents such that they are able to change their position more rapidly while also dynamically adjusting order sizes, especially during periods with particularly low liquidity, as well as improvements to the intelligence of Futures agents in terms of their application of the signal when calculating next actions.
,
Memory Allocation & Usage Optimization : An upgraded allocator is applied to the system, allowing to further accelerate the computations involved in simulation management, alongside a couple of additional refinements to reduce the amount of memory accumulated over long simulation runs.
,
Data-Intensive Agent Preparations : Tools and a preliminary example agent illustrating the use of the full resolution of available data provided through the L3 record attached to the state update are currently in testing; only some preparations for this are included in the update today while finalizing and verifying these elements, expect to publish the example agent and first tools later this week.  This represents a necessary step towards facilitating the deployment of miners utilizing data-driven strategies which demand access to the highest available granularity of data, of which AI-based strategies are a key example - framework and example for application of AI in agent logic is also in the works.
,

These updates will be pushed at ~15:00 UTC today.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push. (edited)
