[2025-07-03T13:57:00.437Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1390330492221521990
Further explanations for those wanting to read more about it:

Recall that you have 20x "cap" (wrt the intial capital given at the start of the simulation) on how much volume you can create before your orders will be stopped from entering the exchange. So, optimally, you would like to place your orders with highest possible volume in cases where you see the most benefit and possibility of reaching high Sharpe, and on the other hand, if you are very uncertain, use low volumes. But overall making sure you would use "maximal" amount of volume, because if you would not, you might not be taking advantage of the best opportunities and you would likely lose to others.

You can think of this as being controlled by a manager at a trading desk: you can take certain risks, but must remain within certain capital use limits. We do not currently enforce minimum amount of trading volume, like we did in the past, we rather now control the maximum, as per this risk management "exercise" or optimization scheme. Clearly keeping things in control while using the maximal available trading volumes, without going further, is a difficult optimization problem. This is where we believe AI methods are useful, it is not only about the signal extraction, but also how much you should weight it.

The current implementation does give a penalty if doing bad mistakes. But we have increased the calculation window further in this latest version to two hours (see above). This penalty is "asymmetric," that is, you can have a great overall performance of Sharpes, but then destroy that by having a few bad mistakes, This reflect the real-world risk taking in a way that a few bad mistakes can wipe you out from the business, in the extreme cases like Knight Capital did (https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/admin/2013/34-70694.pdf). So we think such penalty must exist for making bad decisions.


While processing 212 small retail orders that Knight had received from its customers,
SMARS routed millions of orders into the market over a 45-minute period, and obtained over 4
million executions in 154 stocks for more than 397 million shares. By the time that Knight
stopped sending the orders, Knight had assumed a net long position in 80 stocks of approximately
$3.5 billion and a net short position in 74 stocks of approximately $3.15 billion. Ultimately,
Knight lost over $460 million from these unwanted positions.
 (edited)
Thursday, July 3, 2025 at 10:04 PM
Link: https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/admin/2013/34-70694.pdf

[2025-07-03T15:44:15.478Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1390357482739863602
The limit is on total traded volume in terms of QUOTE value, not sure what you mean "buying and selling the same amount", assets are fungible, any amount executed in a trade contributes to your total trading volume.
,
The limit is on total traded volume over the previous 24 hours of simulation time (rolling window); this is carried over between simulations i.e. if simulation is reset, or a new simulation starts, the volumes used to determine if you have exceeded the cap are carried over.
,
A penalty is applied on outliers, so if you have mostly Sharpe values in a range of say 0.5-0.7 on each book, and then on one book you have -1.0, this will incur a penalty.
,

Would encourage you to study [the code](https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/f7cacecf15552f8f052c3d9fff9aea14ab0d9c60/taos/im/validator/reward.py#L175) if you wish to fully understand the mechanism.
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/f7cacecf15552f8f052c3d9fff9aea14ab0d9c60/taos/im/validator/reward.py#L175

[2025-07-04T14:50:44.686Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1390706403567730820
Ah, ok -  the Sharpe window is 2 simulation hours, but this is a rolling window so new performance observations from the updated miner will enter the window immediately, although the overall performance will include observations from prior to the update as well until 2 simulation hours have passed.  Also should note that the EMA for the miner score (from which weights are obtained) is 20 simulation minutes, so that there is a smoothing effect on the change in incentive relative to rewards, meaning that it will take a bit of time for increases in miner performance over the Sharpe window to reflect in the incentive.  Quite difficult to say exactly how long you might need to wait to see clearly the effect on performance of the new agent, but after 2 simulation hours the Sharpe assessment will be entirely on the new agent. [2025-07-06T17:05:38.635Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1391465127781470218
To be clear, we have released basically every week (significant) improvements, sometimes two per week. We have increased from 10 simultaneous simulations to 40, and can do much more, if we just want to (hundreds, or even thousands). The actual limit-order book "modeling" challenge is just about getting started as the technical setup is ready for that, and the few issues we have had have been resolved, or we know how to resolve them. Since the incentive mechanism change, we observe much more dispersion between the miners, which is something we consider much more interesting (and hopefully, also the miners would do) than the earlier one that had very "stable" but rather unrealistic scenario compared to real-world algorithms that actually take risk and have to resolve risk management. Whether we are now at an "ideal" setup in terms of the incentives, wouldn not yet say so, but we observe a disteibution of incentives that reward the top 20 % more than the rest (80 %), and more competitive environment as a consequence – and this, gives a much better chance of real-world applications.

Secondly, we have laid out at least 6 to 12 months plan already before, and that includes especially "HFT" capable simulation system with special focus on AI. This is what we call deep HFT. Technically, we can reach this even sooner, but since we know we will also want to do other improvements along the way, it is rather safe to say we are in the track of long-term commitment. Personally, having been in this kind of field for 20+ years, and don't think I can ever change that to something else. Also, we have background in HFT market making, which makes it even more seriuosly involved business proposal, as we know we are interested in taking this to its logical theoretical limit in speed and in intelligence building. This includes major innovations in the science side as well, mainly meaning how to model the limit-order book dynamically in real-time conditions, with the help from AI and decentralized computing. We are just getting started, like Bittensor is getting started in real applications.

[2025-07-09T13:58:03.090Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1392505082200719410
@mvtrx・79  This week's update is fairly light, but includes a couple of important refinements and additions:


Query Process Optimization : Computationally time-intensive processes involved in handling preparation of miner queries have been optimized to reduce the time spent in this aspect of the simulation management; this is aimed at increasing the rate of simulation time progression relative to real-world time and prepares for further increases in book count.  Book count is not being increased this week as we focus on first improving stability and efficiency.  Miners, note that you will need to update at latest when deployed to validators as this includes changes to the message compression handling
,
Data Management Tools : Tools providing a simple mechanism by which miners are able to process state updates in order to construct a detailed history of the book state at each event occurrence (order placement, cancellation or trade) are included, along with a new example agent implementation which utilizes this in a straightforward way, are included in this update.  This represents the first step towards supporting the development of data-intensive trading strategies, of which AI-based methods are of course an important sub-class.  Note that the example strategy is not currently intended to work easily straight out of the box on minimal hardware due to the volume of data and complexity of the state reconstruction process; rather this illustrates the usage of the history management class and provides guidance as to how this might be applied.  Explicitly, with the current timeout setting, completing the history reconstruction for the latest state within the timeout is not expected to be feasible without some serious hardware.  More efficient implementations are being explored and will be included if successfully tested, but we expect miners who wish to make use of the higher-frequency, "deep" data to build on top of the basic tools to construct a system that enables to achieve their specific goals.  We of course welcome any queries, feedback, requests and suggestions that would enable us to assist in this endeavour!
,
Reward Distribution Adjustment : No changes to the incentive mechanism this week, but a small adjustment to the distribution of rewards.  This change reduces the difference in incentive between the top and average miners, and is necessary currently to try and improve validator weights agreement while we still do not observe any miners remaining consistently among the top 20%.
,

We will also upgrade our validator instance to provide more of a buffer against spikes in memory consumption, as well as to better leverage the latest optimizations.

As mentioned in an earlier message ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠, several substantial updates are in the works and planned for release over the next couple of weeks, including margin trading capability, revamped dashboard and full AI-based strategy template and example.  Also remains to apply some adjustments to the current dashboard in order to better reflect the relevant data in agent assessment, this will most likely only be completed later in the week.

The listed updates will be pushed at ~15:00 UTC today.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push.

Correct, note that in this case you must specify timeInForce=TimeInForce.GTT, and that the expiryPeriod must be set in simulation timesteps (nanoseconds) i.e. limit_order(...,timeInForce=TimeInForce.GTT, expiryPeriod=60_000_000_000) will specify that the limit order is to be cancelled after 1 minute in simulation time if not executed. [2025-07-10T13:27:38.194Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1392859815897858250
In short, agents need to maximize average risk adjusted performance (Sharpe ratio being the relevant metric) over all books, with preference given to agents who do so while actively trading (i.e. with higher traded volume).

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-07-10T13:29:16.475Z] Kaiming - Liam
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1392860228118249593
So there should not be failed trades and the bigger the trade amount, the bigger alpha token I could take.
Right?

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-07-10T13:32:47.703Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1392861114072830023
"Failed" trades? You mean producing negative profit (loss)? Yes, you want to avoid that. You want to maximize the correct hits, and do that with "max volume," but you need to be aware that 20x the intial capital given is the max you are allowed to do, otherwise you are being blocked from putting new orders/trade again. This is important. Another important thing is that if you get negative profits (loss), then those are penalized more strongly; that is, if you get a good average positive Sharpe, but have big negative ones as well, they will penalize the average. So, this penalty, and the max allowed trade (20x) you have to take into account. Those have been discussed here on this channel quite a bit before, you can scroll to see those discussions.

------------------------------------------------------------

@mvtrx・79  Will be pushing and deploying a minor update a bit later today; back-compatibility was tested so should not require immediate update by miners or validators, but recommended as always to deploy the latest version ASAP:


Response Timeout Increase : Since continuing to see low average successful response rate from miners, the response timeout will be increase from 2.0 to 3.0 seconds to provide more time for miners to download, decompress and process state updates.
,
Further Query Process Optimization : Additional investigation and testing revealed a more performant method for state deserialization by validator, which should further reduce the time taken in handling the miner query process.
,
Miner Response Compression : A bug in the routine handling compression of miner responses before return to validator was patched; this involves some changes to the message handling, but have designed and tested for back-compatibility so should not affect ability to communicate with validators running either the latest or previous version of the code.
,
General Maintenance : A few minor additional updates also applied, including a change in the miner logging to more clearly indicate their role in trades, more complete documentation for the response methods (limit_order, market_order, cancel_order), and a fix to restore function of the agent testing proxy.
,

The code will be pushed and deployed to our validator at ~15:00 UTC today.

There is a Testnet available #366

You will have to take into account certain matters in order to stay alive

More volume traded gives a bigger weight to Sharpe, but obviously if you get bad Sharpe, you will get then also worse volume-weighted result, which will penalize you

So you want to spread traded volume over time, and you do not want to exceed 20x of your initial capital, because after that the system blocks your orders and your performance will automatically decline

This prepares us for further increases to book count and clarifies the path to take in further upgrading the system to address aspects which still run slower than we would like.
,

Commentary has also been added and updated in the code itself to facilitate comprehension of the role and attributes of classes involved in the protocol definitions.
,
Dashboard Update : Minor adjustments to the metrics and dashboard have been made in order to better provide for monitoring under the latest incentive mechanism; more thorough overhaul of the dashboard is in the works, and content-wise the most important next steps will revolve around the inclusion of data relevant to margin trading enablement.
,

Additional steps have been taken towards providing AI-capable agent templates, but further development is required to collect this into a release-ready package.

[2025-07-21T13:47:18.516Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1396851033048617000
@mvtrx・79 Hello all, we do not expect much new things released this week, as we are deeply involved in developing two big "next things," or rather currently testing them out and developing the last bits them:


short-selling and margin-buying features are going to be enabled for the AI Agents as soon as possible (unlikely this week, though) – this means that one could develop strategies that take bigger positions even in the case the asset owned are not enough currently, being able to leverage rather;
,


"AI template(s)" to go with this kind of development of "riskier position building" and covering quickly for those positions using AI approaches – recall that since our initial launch, we have stated that ML/DL approaches could and should be considered in combination with "speed" and this remains our main goal.
,

The AI template(s) are intended to become the mainstay of the approaches taken, since the markets are inherently dynamic and the real applications to real data will warrant such. But we do not want to throw just plan "AI algorithms" at you, though, as you can easily find them online yourself. We want to build a road that could be taken to its logical end, which is "deep HFT," which is intelligence + speed.

More technical details of the progressions will be released this week as per @6/. , as then our internal tests are expected to be completed. Releasing the short-selling etc features prematurely could do some unwanted damage. In the right knowing hands, such positions can do a lot of good to the market, as most academic evidenec suggests these advanced features do stabilize rather than instabiliize.

Also, we should note that this week we can provide further graphical evidence of the status of the network, how different keys are performing with the said tools above, and help newcomers to become more prominent in mining. These tools would help to adapt the right AI tools as well. We expect more collaborations to happen and will leverage even to academic institutions we are connected to.

[2025-07-21T14:28:56.160Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1396861508927094986
To expand technically a little (though the above message already covers most of the critical information):


Margin trading capability has been available in simulator, being employed by at least one of the background agent types in certain scenarios; we aim now to make this functionality available to miners.  Most of the pieces are in place, remains currently to ensure that convenient access is provided to all the data and functions necessary to manage leveraged positions, to expand the dashboard metrics to include monitoring data relevant to margin orders, then to finalize testing and documentation to ensure that this can be smoothly adopted.
,
AI trading templates will be based around a framework targeting to simplify the process of applying models for inference on the τaos data format , with a focus on identifying and exemplifying an approach which follows some established literature while being tractable for execution in the limited time available for state processing.  Once we are able to demonstrate the applicability of AI approaches in decision making, the next stage will involve the development of a pipeline to facilitate continuous training of models on the published state data (for which the previously released high-frequency state reconstruction and history management tools are expected to be put into more meaningful action).
,

These two updates together will create the basis on which we hope deeply intelligent and adaptive strategies with complex risk management will be built and deployed, so we can leverage the full power and expertise of the Bittensor network and community

[2025-07-22T17:10:24.135Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1397264531104989458
We are always happy to welcome new miners, diversity of strategies is a desirable feature within our design and miners contributions are a vital and valuable component of the system.

We do not currently burn any emissions, and do not have any plans to do so.  I do believe there are certain scenarios in which burning may make sense for subnets with a particular model, but this is not something we foresee to be necessary in our case, and would certainly not implement unilaterally without open discussion and careful consideration of the impact on all participants.

I hope this addresses your concerns.

[2025-07-22T18:14:11.462Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1397280584077934612
Yeah so first of all, we have templates in design that precisely plan to attract more miners. These miners would come from several backgrounds, but especially those that have some, or a lot, of financial trading experience, or even HFT background. Definitely people interested in AI application with real financial context. We have not even started this "marketing" since we need those AI templates first, we have taken steps to describe more precisely how to build such algorithms. So I would say we take this side very seriously. We are not interested in homogenous setting. The whole setup was made for a heterogenous setting – indeed if one would just use the same algorithm logic and scale that, it would likely fail in our future settings since it will have market impact that will eat into the homogenously acting miners. So, from side as well, heterogenuity and many different miners is intended to be the status quo. We cannot of course stop actors that would perform extremely well with scaled up processes, but as mentioned, it would get increasingly more difficult with more market impact.

[2025-07-23T14:09:46.599Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1397581463049863168
@mvtrx・79 Hello all, to confirm, we are still working on the short-selling and margin-buying features, to confirm they work well. These are done to the level of detail of most exchanges in crypto, but we start with a bit "limited" feature stack in that our system will not allow "two directions" taken at the same time, you cannot go margin-buying while in short-selling position, or vice versa – your order is blocked. Later, we may consider relaxing this a bit to be consistent with some exchanges.

There are couple of more more nuanced things in check, and @6/. can maybe make further comments on those.

Then, we are also working on the new dashboard, so we expect there to be 2-3 major things coming out next week, or the week after at the latest. These are done to set the stage for newcomers to the network, and improve advanced guys' chances to be more profitable. Essentially to give different variations to exist. Plus we want to incentivize true AI algorithm building. We will keep you guys posted here. We will also post some figures of the tools you could also use to analyze this Sn, and others.

[2025-07-24T13:47:48.563Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1397938322671931392
Note to all here. This selection of five keys is based on the maximum performance over the time period. This is not totally satisfactory as can be seen with those keys that most of their incentives at lower levels. Better definition of super performance would be based on more consistent behavior and this will be applied soon I am confident of that.

The point is to showcase that some miners have found some consistency in their performance, using the trading volume weighting to their favour to get into the top 30 % that are more incentivized. So, the goal of the miners is still the same, to learn how to use trading volume to weight their best performance, and avoid weighting bad performances.

Naturally, as can be seen also, there is a lot of variability here, but it is certainly more interesting and realistic that avoiding risk and trading with minimal volumes. We will be posting this kind of analyses here weekly to help out especially the more new-comers to undertand what is going on. Also more seasoned guys should find these somewhat useful.

If you are interested in these tools mining, as per subnet, let us know here. Our goal is to help access to the most interesting subnets and of course make subnet 79 in particular more accessible. We do understand modeling in financial markets is difficult and one needs several tools and patience to fine-tune the models, with or without AI.

[2025-07-30T14:36:55.625Z] 6/.

@mvtrx・79  This week we release the margin trading capability to miners, alongside some further optimizations and refinements:


Margin Trading : With this update, we enable the use of leverage by miners in placing orders to the simulator.  This allows to implement new classes of strategies which make use of loan facilities offered by the exchange to optimize trading logic and risk management.
,
State Publishing Optimization : The process for construction and publishing of state messages from the simulator side has been reviewed and refined to exclude extraneous data and provide more configurability to prepare for handling of increased order books.  This should result in some improvement in overall progression rate, while we also work on much more significant improvements to this mechanism so as to eliminate delays resulting from this procedure more conclusively.
,

AI/ML agent example strategy and template production is also progressing, with some preliminary structure and logic already being prepared; this will be released once we are satisfied with the level of generality and the simplicity of customization in order that we can attempt to encourage miners to deploy more diverse and adaptive agents, and thus create even more interesting simulated data. 

Updates will be pushed at ~15:00 UTC today.  Deployment to our validator will be executed 2H following the push.
This release includes a number of changes to the simulator, as well additions and revisions at protocol level, which will require validators to restart simulations and for miners to update their software in order to maintain communication.

Apologies for the somewhat short notice, a few last minute issues together with a couple OOO team members has created some delays.  We are back to full strength today; additionally should note upcoming company meeting, during which focus will shift somewhat towards high level planning and discussions, although we expect in any case to resume production of more comprehensive releases including simulation parameter changes, deeper optimizations and expanded strategy samples and templates. [2025-07-30T15:34:21.216Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1400139462595580047
Note to all. We will be keeping eye on any problems caused by the short-selling / margin-buying feature. This feature has been rather long in the making, and was one of the original "problem points," causing significant delays in production. The accounting side of that is a bit difficult to test and maneuver, so it is fair to say we have to see how it behaves.

But then again, if you are not taking leveraged position, this should not really affect you. The leveraged positions were made available in preparation for more market-making type of actions and efficient inventory controlling. In market making, one typically likes to stay around zero inventory, on either side, long or short, and avoid big risk taking.

Since this has been one of the main agendas we have had with this project, we have put quite a bit of emphasis on this feature. In knowing hands, it can be very handy and powerful, while in more inexperienced hands it can cause havoc. Like in modern exchanges it often is. So you are advised to be careful with it, use testnet, and learn by doing.

The long-term being the "deep HFT" capability, we wish this feature set will lay out more degrees of freedom for the algorithm developers. Now you can then use even more trading volume to gain edge, at the right time. Once the AI Template(s) are available, one can take advantage of this more significantly – that is our expectation anyhow.

In modern market settings, the ability to short-sell and use leverage is wide-spread. Although we are taking somewhat of a gamble here in preparation of the future features, we think it is worth a shot and those seriously interested in building real-world applications and algorithms to real markets and exchanges, should be thrilled!

We will share more information soon, and also provide the "usual" performance diagrams / histograms / CDFs to you.

[2025-08-13T08:39:45.149Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1405108554926395432
@mvtrx・79  We plan to release as usual several updates later today; announcing earlier as this includes quite significant changes to certain parameters, which may require some miners to revise their strategies:


Miner Instruction Distribution : In order to address issues in simulation realism arising due to highly clustered processing of instructions from miners, we have made some modifications to the logic which relates to this aspect.  The first and most significant is a reduction of the publishing interval from 5 simulation seconds to 1 simulation second - this means that miners will receive a new state update every 1 second of simulation time.  The other important component is a change in the mapping of response times to simulation latency; the maximum delay applied will be 1s (if responding just within the timeout), with a distribution applied which results in response times between 0-2s producing latency in range 10-200ms (sim time), while responses received in the last second of the timeout will have latencies betweeen 200 and 1000ms applied.  We will also restrict the maximum count of instructions allowed to be submitted in a single response to contain at most 5 instructions per book (down from 20). Miners, if you expect that these changes will require significant changes to your deployed strategies that cannot be completed before release today, please state your case here or privately so that we can consider if it will be necessary to postpone this change to a release later in the week.  The interval reduction will result also in quite substantially slower simulation time progression, we are working on ways to further optimize the query process to reduce the impact, but is anyway a necessary sacrifice to improve the quality of the data produced by the subnet which also moves us a little closer towards the goal of full HFT trading capability.
,
Simulator Parameter Updates : Simulator parameters simultaneously receive some adjustments to improve the behaviour of the background market, particularly in terms of price stability.  This is aimed at enabling the production of more significant "bubbles" and "bursts" within the simulated market, for which we may also include some local agent logic changes already creating such "shock events" coordinated across all simulated books.  This is an important step towards providing for more meaningful analyses of "flash crashes" and similar events, which are quite central to the utility of the subnet as a powerful risk management analysis tool.  We will confirm if this is included in the release upon pushing of code.
,
Diagnosis Tools & Bugfixes : Some pernicious issues in accounting for margin trading activity arising under very specific conditions have been under deep investigation, resulting in development of new testing tools and extensions to logging mechanisms which enable more convenient diagnosis in general, alongside the fixes themselves.
,
Example Agent Refinements : Several updates to the basic example agents to produce more varied activity as well as a number of optimizations to the AI-based agent introduced last week are included in the release.  We have also updated the run_miner script to select the AI agent by default in order to encourage the exploration of these techniques and push for more intelligent and diverse behaviour by all in the subnet.
,

Code will be pushed to the repository at ~14:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push.

MINERS : Again, please pay special attention to the first item above and let us know if you would find it necessary to request a delay in the release of this change.

[2025-08-14T19:49:05.862Z] 6/.

@mvtrx・79  Miners
You may have noticed that the latest simulation exhibits unusual flat price evolution; after examination this is revealed to be due to miners simply placing large quantities of limit orders at or near the best levels, resulting in an insurmountable "volume wall" which background agents are not able to remove, at least with the current configuration.  This most likely arises due to the reduction in publishing interval, which results in those that simply place orders every round now doing so more often.

We would like to appeal to those miners that seek to find optimized performance in the subnet to recognize this as an opportunity by which to profit from the thoughtless behaviour of other participants - there are several liquidity-taking strategy implementations which would allow to extract profits from the lazy, while also restoring reasonable properties to the market and enabling intelligent algorithms to continue to test and succeed in a dynamic environment.

We are working on providing an example agent to facilitate the elimination of this scenario, and expect also that upcoming further upgrades to the background market will prevent this situation from persisting in future simulations.  We of course develop also modifications specifically to address this issue, but will require careful testing so as not to disturb other sensitive aspects of the simulated markets.

@mvtrx・79 Hello guys! Today on Wednesday, we will be releasing a few things at around the usual time 5pm UTC:


Another bug fix to shortselling / margin-buying accounting side that occur in some corner cases we have analyzed and has created some crashes of the simulation, more details of this will be given by @6/. later today.
,


To help to debug in such accounting matters, we have also developed a replayer that we will be using in the future.
,


We are working and testing to put more intelligence to a special group of background agents mimicing Hedge Fund behavior. This trader type that has already existed, but used pretty simple type of approach previously, and has been an integral part of (my past) quantitative research on things like bubbles, bursts, crashes. And now we have moved into the direction to push that in. For those agents, volatility is one of the key ingredients, among other basic statistical estimates.
,

Incorporating more of this intelligence will lead to wilder performance, the intent is to find the best performing parameter estimates. However, as usual, the AI Agents have a significance say in this, so the end result will also depend on things out of our reach, and we will be fine-tuning things accordingly. The testing we are currently doing and likely deploying today, in some format or another, is to create more dynamic behavior that will also affect the LOB dynamics in a realistic fashion.

I would give more story and motivation behind this new "stylized intelligence" once the new features are released, since the testing is still ongoing in the background and rather would not promise 100 % that it will be released in the desired format now. There is some update in that direction, and more will be coming in any case in the next days and weeks to the extent that more serious AI model approaches would start to gain more ground and we are reaching our goals to simulate and model risks adequately, first to the level of academic precision (meaning, "stylized") and then going into more fine-tuning mode with particular assets in mind. There would be a lot to say here, but rather would not get into that right now since we have taken a deep dive into matters and naturally everything being C++ we are a bit slowed down with that complexity. So, hopefully you guys understand this is a long-term project with equally long-term benefits to it and big goals to reach for.

The above will help us all to better manage risks at high-frequency levels such as in flash crashes, and their mechanisms.

https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1407689252942119003
@mvtrx・79  This week's update already largely described above, and a few of the changes previously planned for inclusion today were deployed in earlier updates, but here a summary and some additional details:


Accounting Bugfix : Another very rare edge case encountered in live simulations which doesn't appear in tests is corrected for; of course we prefer that no such incidents occur, but to put in a positive light, this indicates that miners are deploying real and unique strategies which implement logic outside of the "typical".  We have been working on developing tests and tools to improve detection and expedite diagnosis of such scenarios.
,
Simulator Parameter Updates : Simulator parameters receive some adjustments to improve the behaviour of the background market, this being largely in response to the quite flat price evolution observed in the latest simulations and includes several modifications which are expected to create more "bubbles and bursts".  Occurrence of these type of events in the simulation is vital to the objective of providing data enabling to properly assess and manage risk in the real world.  Again, the live market situation demonstrates clearly that the inclusion of distributed, human-controlled agents in the simulation creates meaningful changes in the orderbook evolution as compared to purely theoretical and controlled experiments; fine-tuning the background market in reaction to newly observed behaviours is an important and expected part of the subnet management, and each update brings us closer to fully realistic market dynamics.
,
Replay Tool : Although not yet ready to be included to the public codebase, it should be noted that we are creating tools which enable to "replay" the exact evolution of simulations having occurred in live so as to facilitate reproduction and diagnosis of errors, more deeply examine miner behaviour and test new updates against a market which accurately reflects the latest dynamics with real miners involved.  This is one of several projects aimed at improving our ability to predict and resolve issues arising due to the behaviour of miner agents.
,

Code will be pushed to the repository at ~17:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~1H following the push.

Further note on the above.

We are likely going to change parameter values in the coming days, or during the week. We will inform of such. This is the first in the series of intelligence building into the background agents, which will be creating LOB dynamics that will then be fine-tuned further into real times series and limit-order-books. This is a long process, and the target is to have several steps in here, as the project serves to understand how crashes happen, how such could be mitigated, and how traders could predict in high volatility environments, hedge against certain risks, and come on top in active crypto trading. The "Hedge Fund" representive actor in the background is one of the main actors in this, as typically crypto and other financial markets are driven mainly by "smart investors" and big investment houses. @mvtrx・79 Hello guys, as usual, today we release updates to the framework. More information coming up soon. Just some notes now: We have been working on (still) some remaining bugs that plague the short-selling / margin-buying side, and are mitigating accounting matters (hopefully the last bits!) today by introducing smallest order-volumes, others being rejected.

We are also increasing some of the "inherent" volatility (uncertainty of price path direction and scale) giving better chances to momentum based trading at certain times, and a wider range of options of trading algorithms. There is going to be a template released that would indicate at least to one possible direction. More about that after the release.

There are bunch of parameter changes how the "background" agents work, and these themselves may affect the volatility of the whole system, to the extent that more drastic up and down movements will be seen, including larger orders being executed over time in steps in either direction.

Bunch of other technical things in the works that can help the system to become more resilient and lean in terms of data. More about that after the release. The direction we want to take this into is larger application space, including but not limited to option pricing.

You would expect the same time of deployment around 5 pm UTC, but more information about that will be released soon, as typically we give a more detailed technical overview closer to the time.

Here attached plots that show the last seven (7) days overall performance of "Dispersion Group." Any questions about that we can do Q/A here, and help the process getting into the game succesfully.

We have lots of things bubbling, including but not limited to collaborations with research institutions / universities / groups.

@mvtrx・79  This week's update includes a few additions, revisions and optimizations, with several other projects currently in the works:


Momentum Example Agent : A new example strategy will be included which uses Hurst exponent estimation to generate trading signals; this is the first in a series of new templates aimed at exemplifying the use of different classes of strategies, which we hope will encourage and assist miners to incorporate new techniques into their operations.
,
Simulator Parameter Updates : Further adjustments to the simulator background to increase volatility and create more dynamic and realistic environment are applied.
,
Reporting Revisions : The reporting process executed by validator to enable monitoring via dashboard has been optimized somewhat to reduce the time taken in this activity, and the handling revised to avoid blocking the query process where the reporting is not completed before the next query round starts.  This does mean that there will be a reduction in the frequency at which the metrics are reported, but also an improvement in the rate of progression of the simulation.
,
Bugfixes : Unfortunately encountering some new issues in accounting handling arising in edge cases following the previous updates, these have been investigated and solutions are produced and in testing.  Note that this includes an update which allows to set a minimum order size that will be accepted by the exchange - the value will be fixed to 0.01 BASE in the release.  The complexity and sensitivity of the simulator accounting is of course necessary to ensure accurate and fair evaluation, but does lead to a lot of these types of concerns when introducing intelligent human agents which execute a wide variety of techniques.  The more of these types of scenarios we encounter and fix, the closer we get to full stability of the simulator under any conditions, a key goal which we are now very close to achieving.
,
Logging Improvements : Logging process for simulation events is being reviewed, refined and expanded to facilitate analysis and investigation, as well to reduce the size of the generated files.  The first of several planned steps towards this goal (minifying L3 log entries) is expected to be included in today's release.
,
Replay Tool : The tool enabling to replay past simulations is still undergoing final refinements and testing, but will be put into use and included to codebase soon.
,

Code will be pushed to the repository at ~17:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~1H following the push.

Miners
Note the new restriction on minimum order size (orders with less than 0.01 BASE quantity will be rejected), you may need to adjust strategy logic to account for this.

[2025-08-28T12:20:38.714Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1410599962391220265
You would need to include these processes in your measurements to fully assess whether responding within the timeout, and also account for latency between sending from validator and arriving at your miner (and vice versa).
Typically you should aim to generate instructions within < 1s and allow ~2s for the base message handling; this is in line with the instruction latency distribution changes described at ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠ and included in release 0.1.25 - since simulation latencies are distributed in the range 10-1000ms in simulation time, you should expect that you must complete calculations and generate instructions within 1s of real time. (edited)

What do you mean by this? Again, we can only discuss matters related to miners, and our project, from technical and conceptual perspective. We have been updating now very important matters related to the "background agents," they have got more intelligence and we are closing in to more realistic time series behavioral patterns. The different actors are next going to be calibrated to their respective realistic range of capital. We are also every week including new stuff. What we have had difficulty with was the short-selling and margin-buying features, since there were many (many!) accounting issues in different corners that have taken a few weeks of our time. Now that we then finally hopefully cleared of that, we are back to focus more on the fine-tuning of the limit-order-book, and the real financial applications.

[2025-08-30T17:42:37.456Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1411405766799265832
I can put up a here the main concept what we want to take further. It is one of a few that are totally doable, and as we are into this for long-term, as long as it takes, as long as BIttensor exists (and longer, we move somewhere else in that case). The main reason we do several simulation is because we want to explore risk management and especially the so-called "black swans" or unusual crashes, bubbles, and associated phenomena that are very costly to investors, traders, and even hedge funds that typically are the best informed of market developments. By repeated trials, and realistic trials in that, we can simiarly to option pricing find out the "price of risk" and take that into account in any trading algorithm development. Furthermore, since we not only repeat several times, but also will be taking in "macro-news" and associated real-world events, like already as an example there is the futures market impact (in simple form, yet), we can calibrate the whole system to reflect some of the most typical assets traded in crypto. Also, we are mostly concerned with a bit less liquid names for the reason of asymmetric information in them, compared to BTC, say, which reflects the opinions and investment strategies of many more than, say, of TAO. The fact that we can do this simulation like we do here with ABM (agent-based models) means that we can also explain "why" certain things happen; why for example crashes happen, and how they could be forecasted better. And once the LOB has been better modeled, it will also include valuable information to allow for better strategies to be tested and taken then into live markets. These questions are so central to finance that the whole field of Monte Carlo -simulations, option pricing by numerical methods, and the most serious backtesters that take into account market impacts, or execution algorithms that necessarily have to do so, have always been wanting to seek out answers to the question mentioned above. But instead of relying on just AI to solve this, we want to also explain and undertand "why." This is also the reason why is takes more time to develop this system since we do not want to just "fix" things quickly, we also want to keep in grasp of the "what is going on" -aspect. Therefore, we do not want the machines to control us, it is the other way around this subnet is intended to work. And we do not only seek to resolve research questions. The value can be directly found in some of the said concepts, including precise "black swan" estimates, better forecasting methods at least when it comes down to volatility and risk management, plus liquidity available. What we cannot guarantee in practice is "would the algorithms make money in real markets." That will hinge on some of the more advanced features we are developing, and also for that reason we resort to C++ in order really crack that on chain.

I have to remind of this because these channels are moderated. That said, Bittensor as protocol is similar to Bitcoin in a way, there is no "controlling body," and we keep developing what we have and building value internally as much as we can, and we know how to build up a great product. For other factors in the world that may matter, well, those are topics outside of this realm here. One could say similar of many quality projects, and claim there is not enough "content" or things are "progressing slowly" (or slower than expected), but that is oftent he case in software production that certain matters in complicated projects take a bit more time than initially envisioned. At the same time, we are learning and seeing new opportunities ahead, with universities and alike, and those do not just suddenly emerge over night, like they would not any startup or new projects taken into live mode in this fashion. Linux was not an overnight success in adoption, neither has been many other open-source projects. What we build up is long term things, and certainly we want things to work as soon as possible. We are increasing our head count in the development side, and also hiring marketing and business development people, but just randomly developing "value" is not possible, it is a long process that applies to all projects, especially if they really try to work on something more unique than the average.

[2025-09-03T14:58:34.793Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1412814035140874361
@mvtrx・79  This week we only deploy a few further adjustments to the simulator parameters; there is though much in the works and going on behind the scenes:


Simulator Model Adjustments : Today we deploy further modifications to the simulator parameters and background agent logic which allow the market to better adjust to different volatility conditions, and intend to create more long term price momentum together with an increased frequency and magnitude of sudden endogenous crashes and spikes.  These adjustments are informed by analysis of the latest live simulation data as well as varied testing under different simulated conditions, and are motivated also as always by comparisons with real markets.  Updates of this type should be expected almost every week as we constantly study the data and tune towards more realistic and interesting market evolution.
,
Replay Tool : The tool enabling to replay past simulations has started to see some use in our diagnosis and testing, but still some minor technical issues to iron out before this is fully completed - we expect to include in next week's release.
,
Simulator<->Validator Communication Optimization : Proof-of-concept for a much more efficient mechanism handling the sharing of state updates and responses locally between simulator and validator has been produced, with the revision of serialization methods throughout the simulator underway to enable this to be applied.  The simulator has seen a number of highly impactful optimizations which allow it to process a large number of books in parallel (as we will showcase soon), but the process involved in dealing with miner queries prevents to fully leverage these advancements - this change represents another step in the project to optimize the state publishing process in order to address the bottleneck which prevents more rapid simulation progression.  We expect to practically eliminate time spent in sharing the state information, preparing us also to handle much larger state messages in future.  This update is planned for release in 2 weeks.
,
Simulation Checkpointing : The ability to resume stopped or failed simulations has been one of the features intended to be included in the simulator for some time already. A version of this was actually already implemented earlier in the development, but due to the scope and extent of other feature updates it was decided to be deferred until reaching a more stable state.  We have now reached the stage where this makes sense, and also designed a better mechanism which can be produced as a sort of "extension" of the state publishing refinement in the previous point.  The ability to resume simulations will allow us to deploy simulator updates without requiring to restart the running simulation, enabling more accurate and stable rewarding, better recovery from failures and a smoother deployment procedure.  We hope to complete this feature in the next 3-4 weeks.
,
Reporting & Analysis : We have also been consistently internally expanding and refining the tools used in the monitoring and analysis of the subnet data to better support the tuning of market parameters, study of AI agent behaviour and detection and diagnosis of issues.
,
Dashboard Upgrade : A completely custom rework of the monitoring dashboard has been in production for some time, with the aim of providing a smoother, more intuitive and interactive experience for those interested in observing our simulated markets and the activities of the agents participating therein.
,

Code will be pushed to the repository at ~16:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~1H following the push.

[2025-09-10T13:18:10.078Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1415325480713850891
@mvtrx・79  This week's updates include some further market adjustments, the first iteration of the replay tool and a couple of functionalities requested by miners:


Simulator Model Adjustments : The update includes further modifications to the simulator parameters and agent logic, aimed as always at approaching more realistic conditions with accounting for the latest state of the live simulation - we have seen some good progress in this regard over recent weeks, and are really only getting started in terms of the detailed tunability of the background.  Specifically, this revision includes most importantly the implementation of a "volatility guard" for the stylized agents, which allows for much more dramatic variations in the aggressiveness of the background traders
,
Replay Tool : The first iteration of the tool which enables to replay past simulations is present in this release; while we immediately intend to use this internally to facilitate diagnosis of issues, enable additional analysis methodologies for the mainnet data and improve predictability of testing outcomes with regard to parameter adjustments, we also expect this to become useful to miners and validators in general as the subnet evolves and matures.
,
Miner Requests : Having received some valuable feedback, a couple of updates to the miner framework have been made - the first is the inclusion of the initial balance in the market state update to enable miners to more easily utilise this in their own calculations.  The second is the addition of a simulation_id field in the state config class to assist in organisation of data recorded by miners for use in more detailed analyses of behaviour.  The utility of this is demonstrated through logging to file of basic miner market events: trades, orders and cancellations are now written to CSV files with organisation by validator and simulation, so that these data can be read and analyzed either within the strategy or during analysis to calculate more advanced metrics.
,

Updating then on some of the ongoing projects:

Simulator<->Validator Communication Optimization : We expect to practically eliminate time spent in sharing the state information from simulator to validator, preparing us also to handle much larger state messages in future.  This update is expected to be completed next week, but may go to the next week's release so that careful testing can be concluded.
,
Simulation Checkpointing : The ability to resume stopped or failed simulations has been one of the features intended to be included in the simulator for some time already; since now at a stage where it makes sense to proceed with this development and given that it can be achieved as an extension of the state communication optimization, the implementation is now underway. We hope to complete this feature in the next 3-4 weeks.
,
Reporting & Analysis : We consistently internally expand and refine the tools used in the monitoring and analysis of the subnet data to better support the tuning of market parameters, study of AI agent behaviour and detection and diagnosis of issues.
,
Dashboard Upgrade : A completely custom rework of the monitoring dashboard has been in production for some time, with the aim of providing a smoother, more intuitive and interactive experience for those interested in observing our simulated markets and the activities of the agents participating therein.  Progress on this continues, more updates to come.
,

Code will be pushed to the repository at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push.

I would like to add perhaps here a bit of larger context on the simulator model adjustments. We are working on a greater feature that is not so much related to the fine-tuning of parameters. The feature under work – which we have been investigating for at least two months already – is related to a new way of bringing about bubbles and crashes formation. Or maybe more accurarately put, a way to merge two types of modeling techniques into one.

This would create a system that has not been reported even in academic literature as such. If we are succesful in this, which we shall see first evidences of in the next 2-3 weeks ETA, then we will be seeking academic collaboration at a deeper level. The reason why this is interesting is that we can begin to understand why certain crashes and bubbles form. This is of greater interest in finance due to the need of better risk management.

Effectively, in trading, you are also interested in making more money. Obviously. This feature stack would allow better forecasts based on limit order book data alone. It could be combined with basically any intraday trading strategy.

[2025-09-17T14:54:53.956Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1417886539001630832
Let me expand on this a bit to those not familiar why "fractional Brownian motion" (with mixture) might matter. First of all, this class of stochastic processes is alrady rather old and much studied, for about 50 years or so. That itself surely lends it  credibility. But mostly we are interested in the long-term memory this process has and its implementation in finance. In "serious" mathematics, it has been applied several times over – the associated (and applied) Hurst ("H") exponent has an interesting story behind it. A long time ago, guy called Hurst wanted to know what kind of cycles the River Nile would have to better design water reservoirs. He designed an approach to estimate the memory characteristics. Since then, the same approach has been applied in financial markets, and the associated "H" parameter makes the typical random walk (in continuous time, known as "Brownian Motion") more general, allowing for different types of behavior to occur. This, and the fact we also incorporate jump into it, which are notoriously themselves hard to estimate from real exchange data, allows us to approach another important strand of research with far reaching consequences on say option pricing. The better one is able to catch those statistical features, with more and more advanced methods, the more precise estimates for valuation of risk one is able to get. We already released one trading template with Hurst exponen in that, so one can see probably now why it might matter and be also valuable in this framework. This was the real short story behind this... More text and explanations are upcoming in blog-posts and articles, and this will likely start our academic collaboration with universities.

Total Traded Volume : By request, the total volume traded over the last 24h of simulation time is now included in the state update; this allows to more easily keep track of how much trade volume you are still allowed to execute before reaching the cap.  The latest total trading volume can be accessed inside agent logic as self.accounts[book_id].traded_volume.
,
Latency Setting in Proxy : For those miners who utilize the proxy setup to test their miners offline, logic to set delays on instructions received to the proxy from agents is now included so as to improve the correspondence of results with those expected in mainnet environment.
,

Miners
Please check out the latest changes; if you are making use of the event history or the regressor agent examples / framework, you likely should apply the new updates to gain access to properly organised history data.

The update has been deployed to testnet, and will be put to mainnet validator in ~1 hour
No simulator changes included so no restart will occur.

Validator Update (Today):

Synapse Compression Refinement : Following further testing and exploration to seek additional optimizations to the state publishing process by validators, the compression mechanism and format is adjusted in order to reduce the time taken in preparation, as well as the size of the published state data.  This change requires all miners to update to the latest package version today between 15:00 UTC (code push) and 17:00 UTC (deployment)
,

Simulator Updates (Friday):

Simulator Model Adjustments : We continue to refine the parameters related to the interaction between the new mixed fractional Brownian motion and the background agents, further improving the realism of the market momentums and other key behavioural matters.
,
Simulator<->Validator Communication Optimization : This update is nearing completion with finalization being the reason for delaying the simulator update deployment; this is targeted at providing a more significant reduction in the time taken at each miner query round by eliminating delays due to GIL locks and state parsing & restructuring.  The expected result is a decent improvement in the simulation progression rate, an important consideration for a number of reasons, chief among which is the ability to produce a larger quantity of data and improve continuity of scoring results.
,

[2025-09-24T14:21:54.658Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1420414952283574433
Updating again on some of the ongoing projects:


Additional Background Agent Types & Models : While the somewhat smaller tweaks and additions to simulator configuration deployed recently bring us closer to more realistic, interesting and tradeable markets, advanced extensions which produce new conditions reflecting the most critical real-world scenarios in terms of risk management have meanwhile been under continuous research and development.  The latest project centres around the use of an established model applying principles from physics to financial markets, and is expected to enable to generate conditions which much more closely simulate the "bubbles" and "bursts" which are so important to the study of risk in real markets.  This research does take time, mostly due to the complex interactions between the different background model agents and the miner agents, but has seen good progress through the use of novel, conceptually consistent mechanisms to coordinate agent behaviour.
,
Simulation Checkpointing : The ability to resume stopped simulations has been one of the features intended to be included in the simulator for some time already as this allows to deploy updates without interruption and recover from failures without requiring to start a new simulation; since now at a stage where it makes sense to proceed with this development and given that it can be achieved as an extension of the state communication optimization, the implementation is now underway. We hope to complete this feature in the next 2-3 weeks.
,
Testing, Reporting & Analysis : We consistently internally expand and refine the tools used in the testing of simulation configurations as well as monitoring and analysis of the subnet data to better support the tuning of market parameters, study of AI agent behaviour and detection and diagnosis of issues.  Several upgrades and refinements enabling more extensive use of the replay tool in creating realistic testing environments are being utilized internally, and some outputs from the reporting and analysis process will start to be shared over the coming weeks.
,
Dashboard Upgrade : A completely custom rework of the monitoring dashboard has been in production for a while, with the aim of providing a smoother, more intuitive and interactive experience for those interested in observing our simulated markets and the activities of the agents participating therein.  Progress on this is ongoing, with the first interactive feature enabling more detailed inspection of historical orderbook states in testing while the next feature is under development.
,

,

,

An additional enhancement to the background model has also been prepared and included; stylized background agents will now leverage a HARA utility function to capture evolving risk preferences, fostering dynamic evolution and emergent complexity beyond traditional models. This is complemented by a more realistic wealth distribution, aligning agent behavior with empirical realities. The aim is to generate more realistic trading volumes from background activity while still producing sensible price evolution.
,

[2025-10-01T18:19:39.393Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1423011497977708544
I should also note here for those interested that typically in economics one uses CARA (constant absolute risk aversion) or CRRA utility functions. However, this is mostly due to convenience rather than actual "realism." It is due to simplicity of finding solutions, not necessarily even according to important researchers originally discussing and proposing different utility functions in economics. In particular, Robert Merton (Nobel Prize Winner), one of the most influential economists ever, used HARA utility function rather than the simpler CARA or CRRA: In our computationally already involved setting, such simplifications are no longer necessary, nor even desirable. We have selected HARA for a number of reasons, first being its more general format, but also because many economic relations are derived with the simpler formats, which cast doubt on several outcomes. The classical "treatment" on HARA is https://www.sfu.ca/~kkasa/Merton_71.pdf (edited)
Thursday, October 2, 2025 at 2:40 AM
Link: https://www.sfu.ca/~kkasa/Merton_71.pdf

@mvtrx・79  This week's update consists mostly of refinements, optimizations and improvements resulting from monitoring and investigation of the simulations following last week's major communications upgrade:


Simulator<->Validator Communication Refinements : A couple of improvements, optimizations and enhancements related to the operation of the new communication mechanism are applied.  This includes updates to the state structure to reduce the size of messages by populating composition data only for a limited number of top levels, improving the rate at which states are parsed by the validator and producing smaller messages for transmission to miners, expected to further reduce the time and resources taken in this step.
,
State Saving Optimization : Following deployment of the new communication mechanism, it has been observed that some time is spent during each state processing round in waiting for simulation state saving to complete; this process has been optimized and re-organised to avoid this and further reduce the delay in processing.
,
Leveraged Order Handling Refinements : A new scenario arising in the live environment over the last week resulted in another detailed inspection of certain order execution logic within the simulator; a few adjustments and refinements which improve the accuracy of calculations and avoid certain rare scenarios leading to unplanned restarts of the simulator are introduced.
,

We expect to push to the repository at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

@mvtrx・79  Have just pushed an additional update:


Accounting Refinements : Additional robustness improvements to the accounting consistency checks aim to eliminate a remaining rounding issue encountered in very rare cases.
,
Simulator Parameters : Updates to the parameters and logic of the background model agents are applied as an immediate attempt to tackle the walls of liquidity entered at the best levels by some miners.  More extensive adjustments to the model as well as the incentive mechanism are being designed and tested to provide a more complete and organic mechanism to disincentivize this type of behaviour.
,
Sharpe Assessment Period Adjustment : The period over which Sharpe ratio is calculated has been further increased to 1 simulation hour, this is intended to reduce the rate of decay of activity score and lessen the volatility of miner evaluations.
,

Would note also that we are investigating approaches to improve the efficiency of simulation state parsing, since it seems this is a major culprit creating delays in the processing of state updates leading to response timeouts on the miner side.  While of course it is ultimately the miners' responsibility to ensure they respond timeously, we seek to facilitate this as much as possible.  Several direct optimizations have been tested without seeing substantial improvements, will next be examining if any structural or content changes are possible without dropping potentially important information from the updates.

Miners

The upcoming changes include modifications to the trading fees parameters and application as well as careful adjustments to the incentive mechanism which will motivate the use of more intelligent, active strategies.
,

Validators

Miners

[2025-10-22T12:47:41.673Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1430538102182645821
@mvtrx・79  This week's update focuses on refinements and optimizations to address issues of simulation stability and progression rate:


Validator State Parsing : Handling of simulation state parsing in the validator is revised to skip class construction and validation and work directly with dictionary representations; this eliminates one fairly significant source of delay in both state processing and synapse preparation, and is expected to provide a moderate boost to the simulation progression rate.
,
Miner State Parsing : Since receiving feedback indicating that state parsing is also significant on the miner side in causing timeouts when responding to validators, an option will now be provided which allows to specify for state updates to be lazy loaded.  If enabled by appending lazy_load=1 to the --agent.params argument when launching a miner, the state is constructed with dictionary-valued fields, and properties are only parsed into classes when accessed.  This allows agents which use only a small subset of the state information in their logic to avoid validating unused data and only pay the time cost for parsing fields which are actually applied.  This is expected to improve the response success rate of miners by reducing the time taken in basic processing, and if we observe a significant decrease in response times will also allow to reduce the timeout and further accelerate the simulation progression.
,
Fixes & Refinements : Still encountering new complex edge cases in the accounting management leading to some rare discrepancies which require the simulator to be restarted, additional fixes for the latest issues are applied to restore simulator stability.  Additional instruction validation necessary to account for type limitations in the C++ message parsing are also included.
,
Replay Function Updates : Not perhaps relevant to others, but this update includes also the latest enhancements to the simulation replay functionality which we use for diagnosis, debugging and testing.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

[2025-10-29T13:56:19.538Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1433092088819617923
@mvtrx・79  This week's update includes only some adjustment to the reward calculation handling to avoid blocking the query process, and a couple minor corrective updates on simulator which were already deployed at our validator for testing at the last restart.  Otherwise, we leave the simulator process to run in order to confirm stability and gather more data to inform the enhancements scheduled for next week's release:


Rewarding Calculation Adjustment : In order to avoid blocking of the query process due to incomplete rewarding calculations between rounds, the handling is modified to implement a queuing structure.  However, due to variations in calculation time and concurrency considerations which may lead to delays in assigning scores, we further modify the logic such that rewards are not calculated at every step, but rather updated only at certain interval.  This interval is specified immediately in simulation time as 5 seconds, i.e. rewards will be calculated at every 5th state update.
,
Simulator Corrections : A couple of minor corrections addressing a rare failure scenarios on simulator side are included; these were already deployed at the last simulation restart on our end, and are provided here to be deployed by other validators.  Our simulation will thus not be restarted at the deployment, in order that the current simulation will have maximal time to run before the next release.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered. (edited)

[2025-10-29T13:56:37.036Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1433092162211549256
Updating then on the ongoing projects:

Dynamic Trading Incentive Structure : The major enhancement currently in testing for next week centres around a novel model for fee and rebate application which aims to motivate participants to take actions which positively influence market quality by adapting the costs and incentives distributed to traders in response to market conditions.  More information including a preliminary article describing the model will be provided by @7/. in the next couple of days.
,
Additional Background Agent Types & Models : While the somewhat smaller tweaks and additions to simulator configuration bring us closer to more realistic, interesting and tradeable markets, advanced extensions which produce new conditions reflecting the most critical real-world scenarios in terms of risk management have meanwhile been under continuous research and development.  The latest project centres around the use of an established model applying principles from physics to financial markets, and is expected to enable to generate conditions which much more closely simulate the "bubbles" and "bursts" which are so important to the study of risk in real markets.  This research does take time, mostly due to the complex interactions between the different background model agents and the miner agents, but has seen good progress through the use of novel, conceptually consistent mechanisms to coordinate agent behaviour.
,
Simulation Checkpointing : The ability to resume stopped simulations has been one of the features intended to be included in the simulator for some time already as this allows to deploy updates without interruption and recover from failures without requiring to start a new simulation; since now at a stage where it makes sense to proceed with this development and given that it can be achieved as an extension of the state communication optimization, the implementation is now underway. We hope to complete this feature in the next 2-3 weeks.
,
Testing, Reporting & Analysis : We consistently internally expand and refine the tools used in the testing of simulation configurations as well as monitoring and analysis of the subnet data to better support the tuning of market parameters, study of AI agent behaviour and detection and diagnosis of issues.  Several upgrades and refinements enabling more extensive use of the replay tool in creating realistic testing environments are being utilized internally, and more outputs from the reporting and analysis process will be shared over the coming weeks.
,
Dashboard Upgrade : A completely custom rework of the monitoring dashboard has been in production for a while, with the aim of providing a smoother, more intuitive and interactive experience for those interested in observing our simulated markets and the activities of the agents participating therein.  Progress on this is ongoing, with the first interactive feature enabling more detailed inspection of historical orderbook states in testing while the next feature is under development.
,

[2025-11-03T22:03:50.986Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1435026717612966030
The visualizations are going to be released on Tue-Wed. The script latest on Wednesday, or upon the release of the new mechanism, but the latest when releasing the code overall. This is because there may still be some changes to how the code is actually implemented. However, you can review the paper we released last Friday no 31st of October, it discusses the motivations and pretty explicitly lays out the principle.

Short description is the visualization will about the Maker-Taker Ratio (MTR); the target is for now considered to be 70-30, meaning 70 % passive 30 % aggressive, and if the AI Agents (miners, here), are together accounting for something different than that "ideal" (optimal) MTR, the other side is taken a fee and given as a rebate to the other party.

This means, if you look at the FIgure 1 in the paper released, that the trading algorithms would like to, overall, converge to 70-30 MTR, but since obviously it is changing over time, it will create some statistical arbitrage opportutinies, a bit similarly to what perps and spots have (as also mentioned in the paper).

Practically speaking, since currently most of the miners are passive, with about 80 to 85 % on passive side, overall, aggressive orders will be incentivized to the point of reaching the 70-30 status quo. We will consider going deeper into 60-40, or even 50-50, to further incentivize those that find signals, and are not merely on the passive side.

The script to calculate the fees and rebates will be released before the actual code. I expect more information on that tomorrow, on Tuesday. Visualizastion the same, but the visualization is basically a GIF version of Figure 1 of the paper, showcasing how the MTR changes over time in some typical scenarios.

But yes, I will be giving more information, as we just get confirmed that the Wednesday is THE release date, as there are some tests going on currently, still. However, you should be prepared to adopt your algorithms to this new intelligence requirement, or at least it may give an edge over others via rebates, or in opposite side, bigger transaction fees.

It is important to note that the exchange does not take this "fee," it is given to the opposite side of the trade.
