[2025-11-03T22:16:15.675Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1435029841064890450
What you therefore should be paying attention to is:


what is the current "MTR"; this will be reported on Dashboard, and the script can be used to calculate it explicitly;
,


what is your algorithm doing, is it mostly just passive, or aggressive, finding the smartest balance is one of the risk management goals;
,


how the others are playing on this, as your options to perform better depend partly on what they do, as they can create statistical arbitrage opportunities based on the transactions fees and rebates.
,

One is also advised to think about the perp versus spot market practice for similar "stability" enhancing practices, although this was not originally the motivator, it is rather a bit analogous.

Also, as we have received feedback from a few miners here, we think this above structure (the "DIS") and its practical implementation of the functional form ("DIF") will be something that will make the Sn perhaps more valuable, and we also seek to understand whether exchanges in the real-world would be interested in such structure application.

This is just the start on that direction though, as we will be releasing more and more features and structures that are novel, and attempt to make the markets overall better performing. By modern technology and automation, it is all possible to do, and one might even wonder why certain incentive schemas haven't been activated.

Finally, we are going to release a quite significant model upgrade, that we have been working for months already, but since we have had other things to take care of, it has been pushed several weeks now. We are very close to release that now however, and we think that in combination with this proposed "DIS" will be a very interesting pair.

@mvtrx・79  This week's update contains a novel implementation of dynamic fees and rebates calculation as described above, as well as a number of refinements and enhancements to the validator operation:


Dynamic Incentive Structure : As described and illustrated above, we deploy today a new mechanism for determining the fees and rebates distributed in trades based on the ratio of the role of miners in recent trades as either maker or taker.  This is intended to improve simulated market quality, incentivize more intelligent application of different order types and strategies dependent on prevailing market conditions, and function as a demonstration of the ability of TAOS to provide insights on the effect of trading rules for exchanges.  For a more detailed explanation of the implementation and intentions for this feature, see the messages above and the preliminary article published at simulate.trading/taos-im-dis-paper.
,
Validator Refinements : Several updates aimed at further improving the speed and timing consistency of the validator query process are applied as well; this is intended to increase the average simulation progression rate by producing more stable overall performance.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

[2025-11-05T13:27:42.474Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1435621601990283396
Once this is complete and working, we expect the next thing to be the inclusion of long-in-wait endogenous bubbles and crashes feature-set, which is a totally novel way of combining two frameworks together to create complexity in trade prices and limit-order book. It would add value in learning how bubbles and crashes form, and although it will be a process to calibrate, we are confident it will be a worthwhile addition to the already elaborate system of decentralized simulation.

There will also be a separate paper on that. It will introduce two main concepts familiar from the physical world, but adapted to the financial market context. The reason we decided to go first to release the "DIS" is that this structure we would like to first work well in a more "stable" environment, as the incentives will be important in a potentially more volatile framework subject to market crashes, and such. Therefore, we decided to spend first the time on this DIS feature.

Due to the complexity of the framework, I think there remains a chance for some simulation crashes, or other hickups, and we will be working quickly to resolve any such. Once it is confirmed to work well, and people have undertood the basic logic and principles of this DIS approach, we are ready then to launch that new "merging of frameworks" to the public. To be fair, that calibration will take some time, but in our tests we are reaching interesting results definitely worth that calibration.

Since this DIS and the next features are paramount to the whole project goal, among increasing the speed then later to "real" high-frequency levels, we will be releasing more papers and blog-posts explaining the motivations. This also will include simulations or examples of crash situations, and among them the latest in October, 2025, obviously. Such events are something that have always been motivating the whole TAOS framework, and the focus on risk management.

That aspect of crash prevention, or hedging, protection from losses is at the core of TAOS. The features we keep rolling out weekly are always targeting, in a way or another, to serve risk management and better quality of markets, among of course the increase of understanding of why things happen the way they do. In practice, we also think it will lead to practically relevant trading algorithms and approaches than provide significant value, in combination with historical data backtesting.

[2025-11-10T20:00:01.596Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1437532271551713503
@mvtrx・79 Hello guys,

this week's main update from the miner perspective (and to be honest, also exchanges') will be that we are changing the 70-30 "tipoff" point we started with in the Maker-Taker Ratio (MTR) to 60-40. The optimal point from transaction cost point of view is 60 % passive, 40 % aggressive. Aggressive behavior will be a bit more rewarded after Wednesday's release, in order to fine-tune the system closer to where we would like to be. The next stages after this are taken into account, which are, as mentioned, the bubbles and crashes adoption via a merge of two "major frameworks" in science. This work is important as discussed previously for the reason that we want not only to provide a good framework for "stress-testing" or sandbox environment for new trading algorithm ideas, but to innovate new market microstructure rules and redefine how exchanges should operate especially in the decentralized finance space. We have taken somewhat conservative approach this far, step by step increasing complexity and features, trying to avoid too much bouncing around, while recognizing that the system is meant for some groundbreaking testing of new theories and approaches. We have a couple of aces in the sleeve, we believe.

What I can say at this stage about the "merging" of frameworks at this stage is that the other force is in play is "gravitation," and the other is "magnetism." I am aware this a bit hazy way to put it, but some mysticism is maybe appropriate in TAOS.  

I am myself thrilled about this development, but it is also complicated and no straight forward way exist in order to do that.

In any case: The above 60-40 % is announced already now in order to give some extra time before Wednesday's second release using the DIS approach for incentivizing optimization of transaction costs.

@mvtrx・79  This week has been focused on monitoring and evaluating the DIS deployed last week, while working on addressing the slow simulation progression rate.  Updates to the simulation background to incorporate the model described by 7/. above are in ongoing research, development and testing, with expectation for release next week.


Dynamic Incentive Structure Parameters : Having monitored and analyzed the outputs since last week's release of this novel rebate mechanism, we are overall happy with the way things are progressing, but will be adjusting some parameters to bring us closer to the desired profiles and refine the setup to better apply the incentivization.  The target ratio between maker and taker trading will be updated to 60/40, and the relationship between dynamic fee rates and the ratio may be modified using a smoothing function to reduce the volatility of the rates over shorter time horizons.
,
Validator Refinements : A number of revisions, optimizations and enhancements have been applied in the validator process in attempts to better manage the concurrent execution of the various processes involved in state handling.  This only affects validators and does not change any of the scoring or other functionality, but results in improved simulation progression rate due to faster average state handling times, being down from ~12s to ~8s.  Further improvements here are still expected to be possible, but becomes increasingly difficult to coordinate while ensuring stability of query process and sufficient time for all processes to complete.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

If, on the other hand, the sample (empirival) MTR goes above or below that, then an opportunity to catch rebates is activated. (edited)

Link: https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1353733356470276096/1438945681778802830/rnf_maker_taker.gif?ex=6ad9a0d8&is=6ad84f58&hm=c66f36a1c808bb7882617910ab5914ebbf23e2f2dbc6e5d937ed59145417ca67&

[2025-11-14T17:39:41.571Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1438946506869702920
So, as you can observe, a couple of new terms have been invented here for this DIS to be understood. Those are


MTR: Maker-Taker Ratio, which is explained in the paper, and based on the activity of the AI Agents (overall)
,


RNF: Rebates and Fees, which is a cumulative function, like Profit and Loss (PNL) is typically presented as
,


DIF: Dynamic Incentive Function, which is currently non-linear, but in the simplest case could be linear
,

We have selected DIF to be of the form stated in the paper for many reasons, but may later use linear function for mathematically optimal derivation of results. The non-linear format is supposed to give more freedom around the "tipoff" point explained and demonstrated in the paper.

@mvtrx・79  This week has included additional evaluation and monitoring of the DIS, and further updates to the validator query process while background projects related to the improvement of the background model testing and tuning are ongoing.  Releasing today:


Validator Refinements : Additional refinements to the validator query process are applied to address some remaining concurrency concerns and ensure timeous state processing with reliable execution of miner queries.  There remain still some further optimizations in development and testing to improve the simulation progression rate, these will be handled over the coming weeks in parallel with background model enhancements.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.



Elaborating on the ongoing background projects and their importance to the overall subnet vision:


Simulation Model Additions : As previously noted, a new type of agent applying physics principles in the context of financial markets has been under development and testing for some time; this is nearing release-readiness and is expected to enable triggering realistic "bubbles" and "bursts" in the simulated market.  The occurrence of these events is critical to the study of risk.
,
Simulation Checkpointing : The ability to resume simulations is key to the ongoing refinement of the background model as it allows for frequent adjustments to the parameters and logic to be deployed without requiring to restart the ongoing simulation - this enables to collect more complete and useful datasets and examine the longer-timescale effects of changes.
,
Replay Functionality : The replay functionality allowing to precisely reproduce the conditions of the mainnet simulation has been invaluable in diagnosis of faults and testing of new features, enabling us to confidently deploy updates to the simulator accounting, matching logic and other critical components without risking breakdowns in live conditions.  The next utility to be derived from this capability involves the use of partial replays to incorporate the effect of AI agent activity into our testing; this aims to provide us with a mechanism by which to estimate the expected effects of simulation model adjustments in mainnet more accurately, providing a solid basis with which to select parameters and adjust logic to reach fully realistic simulated markets which can be tuned to mimic a wide variety of asset classes.
,

These changes, while not flashy and having absorbed quite some time in development, are necessary preparations for the next phase of subnet development - having reached a point of stability in operation, we now seek to tune the simulation model in order to produce fully realistic data reflecting real-world conditions.  Once this is achieved, the value of the subnet will become much more clear, as the superiority of a distributed simulation approach in analyzing the risk inherent in all financial markets can be properly demonstrated.

@mvtrx・79  This week we have continued with monitoring and studies of DIS, while also further examining overall state handling process timing and query stability.  As indicated in previous announcement, we focus on deeper and deeper analysis of the simulation outputs in order to inform decisions related to adjustments in simulator parameters and incentive mechanism.  Scheduled updates for today:


DIS Adjustment : We are with this update going to further reduce the MTR target for DIS to 50%; this means that departure from symmetric distribution between maker and taker role trades by miner agents will result in rebates being available for fulfilling the less common role, further incentivizing liquidity taking by miners under the right conditions and removing the bias towards preferring liquidity providing behaviour.
,
Minimum Order Size Increase : To address concerns surrounding the submission and execution of uninformed instructions by miners in order just to maintain activity factor component of score, we increase the minimum valid order size from 0.01 to 0.1.  Miners should take special note of this, as it implies a need to more carefully consider order placements since the impact of poor trading decisions at the smallest order sizes will be more significant.
,
Validator Refinements : A couple more minor adjustments to the validator query process and concurrency management are included to address remaining issues observed; still more significant architectural revisions that may be attempted in coming weeks to fully isolate processes and avoid any chance of contention, but overall seeing satisfactory handling times and query reliability.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

[2025-11-26T18:03:50.009Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1443301236446072832
Additional notes to all:

The DIS functionality progress has been interesting, and more along these lines will be coming, plus we will be presenting material in relation to this in December, possibly a separate paper, and connections to AMM.

Secondly, note that the idea of being symmetric (DIF being symmetric) is that we would not take stand on whether AI Agents (miners) would be using aggressive or passive orders. By the evidence we have seen, we do feel that a more balanced (50-50) position is currently warranted, but we will be observing things as they progress.

For the Minimum Order Size, this may have several consequences, but fore mostly the idea is to address certain rather undesirable tactics taking place that would not be that realistic to see in real trading. It is possible we will be changing this in the next update, after the experiences from this. Much could be said about this, and discussions with real world exchanges are starting.

All of these changes, and more to come, are intended to address some key concerns reported us, and while the DIS has been successful, we are likely going to make an even more advanced version of that, along the lines outlined in the last paper released. Furthermore, there will be that "bigger" innovation, it has been worked for a long time, since we want to fine-tune it still further.

I can also discuss any of these changes made this week here, and we will be posting more on social media from now on, since visualization has been improved in the backend side, including the "Trading Cards" functionality in collaboration with CryptoQuay (CQ) platform. These visualizations are also taken to a whole another level soon, with our new visualization group, which we have internally started to form, including 2-3 guys with C++ CUDA focus.

[2025-12-03T14:27:21.812Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1445783475058774119
@mvtrx・79  This week we have continued to develop tooling for deeper studies of miner behaviour in the simulation, monitored and tested modifications and application of the DIS, developed adjustments to the background model and revised the architecture of the validation process:


Validator Architecture : The handling of miner querying is now offloaded to a separate process in order to eliminate all possibility of contention with other tasks and ensure fully reliable collection of responses for every published state update.
,
DIS Adjustment : We are with this update going to further reduce the MTR target for DIS to 40%; this is intended to encourage more aggressive trading activity by miners and create a more dynamic market.  The maximum rebates are also increased to provide additional incentive to those who observe and react to the dynamic rates.
,
Background Model Updates : The background agents play a crucial role in maintaining market stability by providing liquidity and facilitating smooth price discovery. To further optimize behavior and strengthen market function, we incorporate the DIS to HFT agents participation logic with small elegant changes. In certain market conditions this will help in price discovery and reduce impact on others. Additionally, ALGOTrader now considers also the cost of trading in deciding when to execute, helping to ensure activation in the most suitable market conditions.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered. (edited)
Wednesday, December 3, 2025 at 10:30 PM

[2025-12-03T14:27:35.374Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1445783531941789748
Updating on the status of ongoing projects:


Simulation Checkpointing : The ability to resume simulations is key to the ongoing refinement of the background model as it allows for frequent adjustments to the parameters and logic to be deployed without requiring to restart the ongoing simulation - this enables to collect more complete and useful datasets and examine the longer-timescale effects of changes.  This feature is nearing completion, but ran into some unforeseen complications which unfortunately will require to push the release to next week so that adequate testing can be performed.
,
Simulation Model Additions : As previously noted, a new type of agent applying physics principles in the context of financial markets has been under development and testing for some time; this is still progressing and is expected to enable triggering realistic "bubbles" and "bursts" in the simulated market.  The occurrence of these events is critical to the study of risk.
,
Replay Functionality : The replay functionality allowing to precisely reproduce the conditions of the mainnet simulation has been invaluable in diagnosis of faults and testing of new features, enabling us to confidently deploy updates to the simulator accounting, matching logic and other critical components without risking breakdowns in live conditions.  The next utility to be derived from this capability involves the use of partial replays to incorporate the effect of AI agent activity into our testing; this aims to provide us with a mechanism by which to estimate the expected effects of simulation model adjustments in mainnet more accurately, providing a solid basis with which to select parameters and adjust logic to reach fully realistic simulated markets which can be tuned to mimic a wide variety of asset classes.
,
Testing, Reporting & Analysis : We consistently internally expand and refine the tools used in the testing of simulation configurations as well as monitoring and analysis of the subnet data to better support the tuning of market parameters, study of AI agent behaviour and detection and diagnosis of issues.
,
Dashboard Upgrade : A completely custom rework of the monitoring dashboard has been in production for a while, with the aim of providing a smoother, more intuitive and interactive experience for those interested in observing our simulated markets and the activities of the agents participating therein.
,

[2025-12-05T02:01:50.746Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1446320635101057216
@mvtrx・79 We have a long list of novel features outlined, some of them in the original white paper, some in the "DIS" paper (and both available at the website of ours). First a note: These new features are somewhat hard to develop. Certainly it is not a benefit (in speed of development) that we do this in C++ but we have to. Py would not be sufficient in terms of the computational requirements. We have had to make a long development cycle due to some of the matters being done for the first time, especially in the decentralized (blockchain) side. We have here wanted to produce a product that will make an impact in the world of (de-)finance, or maybe more generally speaking as well, since some of the concepts are potentially applicable elsewhere, too. In finance, doing this kind of simulation framework we have here is, to our best knowledge, unique in feats, and while we have seen "simulation environments" been done, they have severe restrictions included and would not be able to reach the testable states we are able to do here now. Say, they could be following AI-driven methods on L3 MBO, but we go beyond that: we want us humans to control machines, not the other way around. We want to actually understand what the limit-order book is like and why it behaves how it does.

The complexity of this product is probably a bit overwhelming to many, and getting into algorithm production is not easy feat in real world either. The target of the Sn has been the same all the time: to help to produce better risk management practices for (fast, even high-frequency) trading algorithms combined with (artificial) intelligence, and allow this to be done via L3 MBO level order-book data, which makes this stand out from many other simulation frameworks, alone. The fact that AI algorithms would need a lot of data to produce meaningful results escapes the attention of most people. We have ourselves tested and deployed in real markets several AI methods that have been successful in research, but since most of them are overfitted, and not capable of changing quickly enough to the dynamics of the markets, they stand almost useless. Unless, in our view, with simulated data that are abundant and allow for repeated trials and execution, especially when it comes down to risk management, extreme events, understanding why they happen, and to predict. Undertanding something is different from just "predicting." We actually have done TAOS to understand things better.

We have still a rather long way to go into our ultimate goal to be "indistinguishable" from real market data, but every week we inch closer, in some weeks more than just an inch. We have in our sleeve several aces, which we have been working for a quite a good while, but because of their somewhat "fragile" nature, you cannot just expect to release them in public before they are better tested. For example, primarily, we have a cool system of creating bubbles and crashes, similar to the real world, but since the system of decentralized agents, which we cannot, and should not, control, we have to (for ourselves) simulate things prior to launch. If we fail in some parameter to take into account some issues, this may lead to unwanted results This is not to say it is impossible to do. No. It is totally possible, and we have a road map for it, but since it is still a complex system, one of the most complex systems of human kind – more complex than natural physical systems – and it can create situations similar to deterministic chaos theory where small changes lead to huge consequences ("Butterfly Effect") and forecasting nearly impossible. But this is the beauty of it: within the chaos, therein also lies some structure.

This structure, as introduced in the first blog post of ours, is still a legit goal of ours to create. In TAOS, there already exists hidden fractality. More of it is going to be revealed (maybe for the first time ever). Exciting to be creating all that on Bittensor with you!

It is a simulator of the limit-order book (LOB), including "L3 MBO" (market by order, see e.g. Chicago Mercantile Exchange for the explanation of that). That is, it is much more than transactions. It is all messages. And it is about more than just "TAO" although we can use TAO/USDC, say, as the the goal to fine-tune to. Simply put, yes, it is trying to simulate the LOB of a particular asset (coin, whatever), but as important as that, we innovate on the best incentives schemes of exchanges and market microstructure rules that would be the best for AI algorithms and maximization of market quality.

[2025-12-10T01:55:06.706Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1448130879762337903
Yes, regular interval is every Wednesday, but in some exceptional cases it can be something different. It is a complex system, there are many exciting features coming up, some of them bigger than others, but in a complex system nearly all interrelated.

Shortly, it depends on the update type whether miner code needs updating. Often I would recommend anyhow that since some of the backgorund agent parameters change in order to fine-tune the system and innovate on the whole system of TAOS.

Every upgrade is taking us closer to the ultimate goal, some of which inch forward while some of which are jumps. For example, we have been working on a quite difficult problem to "merge" two modeling frameworks together for some time already, and it may be that we will release a version of that on this Wednesday. Sometimes upgrades are hard to test before live Mainnet well because it is a complex system and its direction is partly affected by the miner themselves.

Upgrades are intended to create more realism, and in our case especially market conditions that resemble important regimes like bubble and crash formations, and other clear regimes in financial markets that create excessive risks to investors and traders unless the trading strategies are taking into account their effect. Basically, trading strategies could be classified (and I am being very rough here) to mean reverting and trend-following strategies and it remains important to be able to use the opportunities wisely, similarly to real markets, when the opportunities open.

To support also aggressive trading strategies we have innovated "Dynamic Incentive Structure" (DIS, explained in a separate paper) that could form the baseline for decentralized finance exchanges of the future (or now already), especially if we think we are heading into AI realm where algorithms decide for themselves how to behave and control themselves – they have to be incentivized correctly to do that. Finding a good balance with different strategies in different conditions is important.

Since we are simulating many limit-order books (LOBs) at the same time, the statistical significance of finding the best strategy is increased (and not based on luck as could be the real life scenario with only one realization, our own reality we live in). There are also other means how we have wanted to emphasize consistent performance.  And yes, we consider making further edits to the current incentive mechanism. Some of the updates may be related to how the miners are rewarded, and not only to the dynamics of the LOB, and these are then more major upgrades.

Hope this helps.

[2025-12-10T14:25:52.269Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1448319814547406870
@mvtrx・79  This week we have incorporated the previously mentioned background model interactions which aim to trigger the formation of bubbles & bursts in simulations via an interesting econophysics model, and validator operation has been further optimized:


Validator Optimization : Metric publishing has now also been offloaded to a separate process and optimized to improve the speed of metric calculation and assignment; this eliminates some remaining instances of contention affecting the state handling time.
,
Simulation Parameter Adjustments : Background market model parameters are adjusted to match the quieter trading activity, as well as to improve the diversity of trading behaviour in order to avoid predictable movements and reduce exaggerated swings in the market.  These changes aim to better align with realistic market behavior while allowing for the natural formation of bubbles and crashes.
,
Ising Model Introduction : We introduce herding behavior into the existing framework, working with basic principles derived from the Game of Life model. More precisely, we are applying Ising Model type of interactions between some of the background agents. In ideal scenarios this can generate unsignaled trends reflecting the bubbles and bursts inherent to real markets.  More details on this will be provided in another post.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

Upcoming Changes
Simulation checkpointing is currently in the final stages of testing, but due to the extent of the update will require still some additional time to complete to state of full confidence in the functionality - we expect to include this in next week's release.
We are simultaneously also exploring and testing updates to the incentive mechanism; an interim addition to address the currently prevalent risk-avoiding strategy is planned to be released as soon as we are satisfied with the implementation, with more extensive additions to refine the allocation of rewards to the most intelligent algorithms also under review.

[2025-12-12T12:30:46.914Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1449028902444994681
As mentioned above, incentive mechanism revisions are currently under discussion, testing and review, but it should be noted that the goal is not raw PnL - agents must maximize their risk-adjusted performance while also actively participating in trading.  An agent which achieves high profits but takes excessive risk in doing so is expected to rank lower than one which achieves more modest profits with proper risk management.  The current mechanism is broadly successful in this, but we aim with the upcoming revisions to further emphasise meaningful trading activity which contributes to market quality, as well as to penalize risk-avoidance.

[2025-12-12T14:41:32.074Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1449048532106481778
@mvtrx・79 Hello guys, several useful features have been deployed in the last weeks. This week's "Ising Model" (Game of Life -type well known especially in physics, or "econophysics" literature) is among the top features we have released along with the "DIS" paper. However, some issues remain that we have wanted to address for a long time, and we are going to give some heads up on that now – although it is yet a bit uncertain if the scheduled released will be next Wednesday or week after, or if the first move will be a "mixture" and not "step," in order to perhaps alleviate any problems in moving into the desired direction. I would like to emphasize that we have been aware of this, and related matters, for some time of course, but have had to focus on other matters preventing us from tackling it/them. I think the time has come to make a change.

Whether or not this would affect your (that is, miner) performance is uncertain, depends highly on the type of activity now done. But what we have had this far is "unrealized" PNL and Sharpe, combined with weighting (volume) and penalty on bad performance. (Details on why to be described closer to Wednesday next week.) Now, we want to finally make the move into realized PNL and Sharpe, which is the industry standard, and the show-stopper has been mostly statistical significance, since we have wanted to evaluate each algorithm on very active basis, in a window that moves across the day, rather than be evaluated at a single time for the whole period. The detailed motivations are also going to be discussed next week. The point is that we are going into realized because we believe it will be giving a "fairer" performance measure of the algorithm performance, while we also want to find a good balance between the window size and potential weights and penalties.

Since we evaluate things as per path, and then average across the LOBs, aligned with Monte Carlo -principles, it is possible that some algorithms would have less roundtrips than others, therefore not producing any Sharpe (Sharpe not being well defined) due to standard deviation being impossible to calculate. While we understand the problem of small sample (bias), and risks associated with that, we think this is the way we should innovate, and there are ways to reduce small sample problems accordingly (in statistical sense) and they are quite well known in the industry, and of course in academia. Since we are simulating one "trading day" obviously strategies are meant to be "actively trading," but not too actively. As you are likely aware, there are hard-caps on the traded volume in a certain time frame that algorithms should not exceed in order to incentivize smart order placement. When introducing realized Sharpe, this will be reviewed again.

While our goal is into the HFT direction, it is not truly intended to be ultra low latency"competition but deep smartness competition between AI agents. There will be several updates in this regard to make the L3 MBO data matter, one of which was introduced just this week, the Ising Model, and its potential to help to create traces of bubbles and crashes before they actually take place. The direction towards "high frequency" actions stands as the main theme, but we are not saying that everybody should use such tactics, but rather optimize risk in terms of expected profit, and take into account the trading volume (aggregate) limitations that we have placed. The motivation of which has been discussed before, and which will be repeated closer to the ETA. As we are running several simulations internally, of various kinds, which various different parametrizations, we cannot definitely say the release time of all the inter-related features yet.

Perhaps this review is in order now and prepare at least partly for the changes. Regarding the "gameability" there will be another post on that, because we have been looking into that lately too. Thank you for paying attention to this matter.:)

[2025-12-12T16:07:35.275Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1449070188141215856
We are producing limit-order-book (LOBs) with L3 MBO, "market by order," see Chicago Mercantile Exchange, with currently 40 LOBs created, with C++, and using agent-based-models (ABMs) to achieve full understanding based on artificial exchange rules how things progress, and why.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-12-12T16:18:42.038Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1449072984747675799
In Synth, the miners are predicting price paths (multiple predictions) and validators score them based on real performance. We, however, produce real synthetic data, L3 MBO level, which is the most advanced data type, basically the "limit order book" and not only price (trade price), or not even BBO (best bid and offer). We do this in an environment mimicking, as closely as possible,  real market exchanges, including but not limited to CEX(es), but also DEX(es). All this done in C++ with the utmost goal of producing thousands LOBs at the same time, with the miners being able to simulate their "HFT" strategies in this setting, and able to leverage that in real market conditions, as well as real exchanges able to develop their market microstructure rules to the best optimal ones. (edited)

So, yeah, this is a complicated system. It is a complex system that is novel in the world, in science we are doing innovations never done. This Ising Model incorporation into this system has not been, ever, to our knowledge, been executed and published. We have scouted for such for a quite lot. There are number of things that are state-of-the-art in both LOB modeling and ABM systems. (edited)

[2025-12-12T17:12:03.167Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1449086411256107201
The reason this is necessary is that one cannot have AI algorithms tuned with limited samples, and snapshots of streams. The streams, like traffic camera streams, are continuous – if your car takes a snapshot, say, every 5 seconds, within that interval it could plunge into depths of a canyon or storm through a supermarket window. By having a view of continuous type, and have the depth of the L3 MBO, provides a fuller understanding what is going on. This type of data sit at the core why we do this, to make AI truly possible. To make it stand on its own feet, and still be humanly controlled, because of the incentive mechanisms built into are intelligent enough to keep the algorithms in check.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-12-12T17:14:02.731Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1449086912743604440
The AI algorithms need to eat in multidimensional data, and make conclusions based on that which truly matters – no data mining, no false predictions based on overfitted models, but truly scalable and well adjusted algorithms that are able to adapt and "understand" what the conditions are and act accordingly. This is the core problem in finance, when it comes down to trading strategies.

No worries, but you should look into www.taos.im page, with white paper, and the "DIS" paper. I can tell from my side that we are at the forefront of "applied science" currently, but it is a complex product, that mostly would resonate with option pricing experts, but there also they typically would not consider LOB level information, just basically the price path. But when you think about it, why would you only look at the surface, when there is much more depth. You do not want to look at the tip of the iceberg, unless you want to end up like Titanic. Titanic thought the tip is just a small floating thing, while in reality, the monster was hiding below the surface. Too late to regret in risk management when you have already hit the iceberg. (No pun intended to Iceberg Orders.:)) AI systems cannot live with that surface level information. If you read AI papers (very scientific ones, even), they commonly make the mistake of using trade or BBO level information, and when finding something of value, report that there is a signal. Try to reproduce yourself, and you will see the truth.

[2025-12-16T14:41:06.260Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1450497975296983100
@mvtrx・79 Hello guys, tomorrow we are switching the Minimum Order Size from 0.1 to 1. This is based on number of things we have observed, not the least that it would motivate to take more relevant risks, but also that the background agents are doing much bigger orders than 0.1. We have been quite conservative on this side to this date, but now would like to move into this direction. It still represents a very tiny portion of the "total wealth" of the given agent.

What this means?

It means your orders below 1 size would not go through, leading to potential inactivity, and failure to keep alive. Also, pay close to attention to the fact that there is still then the maximum volume traded that you should not surpass, in aggregate, this has not changed. It means that if you do the same number of trades, your trading volumes may surpass the limit, and you would need to select more carefully when to trade, or how many open positions you have.

You would have therefore an optimization task to do, since we would keep Volume Weighting, incentivizing making more substantial order sizes to boost up Sharpe, but do it in a way that would not exceed the total aggregate allowed.

This is the first important change on tomorrow's update. More to be announced.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2025-12-16T19:19:01.630Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1450567916868075714
@mvtrx・79 Second main upgrade to incentives mechanism, almost surely now, is the move to realized Sharpe. More details will be given tomorrow, after some final checks, but the reason for moving from unrealized to realized is first of all that we had used the former to guarantee enough observations to be had in a time window of calculation. We have now come to a check point that we feel it would be making most sense to start moving to realized Sharpe, which naturally is the industry standard on that metric. The matter really has been that we have wanted to reward miners "almost continuously" over the simulation run, and not only at the end, say. This has meant that small sample bias will sneak into the calculation, and ever worse, standard deviation might not be even well-defined due to the lack of observations – here, roundtrip FIFO principled transactions.

More information about this very potential move will be announced tomorrow. For most of ou, it should not actually be that dramatic at all, but we think it is a necessary step into finding the actually best performing algorithms. The previuosly announced (see above) change may well be more significant. Together they are intended to provide even a more meaningful racing ground that more and more intelligent trading algorithms can be built, using L3 MBO data and actually then simulate how algorithms would react to algorithms.

[2025-12-17T14:30:33.284Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1450857708268945600
@mvtrx・79  This week the main focus is on the incentive mechanism update to utilize Sharpe calculated on realized profits and losses for the scoring:


Realized Sharpe Scoring : In order to align with industry standards for the evaluation of trading performance, encourage more careful trading activity and reward the most intelligent algorithms more effectively, with this update we shift from utilizing the unrealized profitability data (total inventory values) in calculation of Sharpe ratio for scoring to a mechanism which calculates Sharpe based on the realized profitability.  Realized PnL is calculated using FIFO principle to construct "round-trips" - pairs of trades which buy then sell (or sell then buy) a quantity of asset - and determine the profit or loss realized through trading activity.  Auxiliary scoring machinery (normalization, activity weighting, outlier penalty and median aggregation across books) functions in the same way as before, but now is applied to the realized Sharpe ratio, with the modification that the activity factor is calculated using the total round-tripped volume rather than the overall total traded volume. The realized scoring will be introduced alongside the existing unrealized scoring with 50% contribution from each at the outset, to avoid resetting everyone's scores while realized data is being collected.  After monitoring and confirming that all looks well with the realized scores, we expect to move into 100% realized scoring ASAP.
,
Minimum Order Size Increase : The minimum order size is increased from 0.1 to 1.0; this may seem like a significant minimum, but represents still a very small proportion of the total miner wealth.  This change aims to further ensure that miner algorithms must consider carefully each of their trades as greater risk must be taken with each instruction; together with the realized Sharpe scoring, this should have the effect of rewarding properly risk managed agent logic which trades both actively and sensibly across all books.
,
Minor Optimizations and Corrections : A few minor optimizations in various parts of the validator operation as well as a correction for a bug in the handling of close_positions instructions are also included.  The logging for miner agents is also slightly revised for readability and de-duplication.
,
Simulator Agent Adjustment : Minor adjustments to simulation background agents are also included; this includes most significantly modification to FuturesAgent to better align their activity with other background classes.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~15:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

Upcoming Changes
Finalization and testing of simulation checkpointing is still ongoing, having met with some additional complications and being decided to be separated from the incentive mechanism update to avoid creating unexpected issues. (edited)
Wednesday, December 17, 2025 at 10:32 PM

All it means is that for an initial period, we still calculate your unrealized score as before, and then also calculate the new realized score.  Your final score during this initialization period will be determined as 0.5 * unrealized_score + 0.5 * realized_score.  Once we confirm that there is sufficient data and all is in order with the realized scoring component, the final score will be shifted to 100% realized_score.

[2025-12-19T11:42:48.747Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1451540270272221224
@mvtrx・79 A couple of general remarks that you might already of course know, but to those rather new to this, I will just quickly summarize. There will also be more fine-grained documents like "how to develop algorithms on TAOS" soon.

First each AI Agent (miner) given a certain sum of "wealth" at the start of the simulation. There are currently 40 such simulations concurrently ongoing. The performance is based on (Realized) Sharpe (switch from Unrealized) measure.

The overall performance in this competition is based on average Sharpe over all the "books" ("runs, limit-order books, the LOBs"), but with a certain penalty on performing very badly on some of the runs. This is currently based on what is called the "1.5 Rule," a statistical rule for diagnosing "outliers." Meaning that if the Sharpe falls out of place too much, it will end up in the left-hand tail of that distribution (distribution of statistics over the 40 runs), and those in the far tail of that distribution will be "outliers" that then negatively weigh on Sharpe. We have not wanted to make a lot of ad hoc adjustments here, we use the 1.5 Rule.

The second important thing to keep in mind that is practically quite relevant is the amount of maximum traded volume done in a (full) simulation "day." If you are going to hit the barrier early on in the simulation (read you have done too much volume), then you would be barred the entry to put new orders in – note this. This would mean a hard penalty on it, so avoid this "at all costs," since you are then out of the competition. Rather, optimize your trading behavior in the sense that your algorithm remains viable, signal seeking, and performing well during the day, and finding "alpha" without being restricted on these grounds.

You can think of that "maximum ceiling" (hardcap) as coming from a "fund manager" that would not allow more to be traded in a single (simulation) day. That is, it is a risk management practice put in place to optimize your trading.

Thirdly, what may also be practically relevant – and I will just repeat it here as well – is that the minimum order size was increased to 1 from the previous 0.1. The motivation here as well is that be mindful what to trade and when. Putting things on the book(s) and letting them just stay here has a certain risk, and this risk is associated with market movements to the wrong direction. On the flip side, you want to use aggressive behavior when it is beneficial to do so. The move to minimum of 1 means that if you do not change your algorithm logic from previous, your algorithm may trade too much in a day and hit the hard-cap as discussed above. So, be mindful of this here as well, since it does matter a bit. This does not mean there could not be smaller quantitites done since orders when executed can break into smaller (child) orders, in case you are wondering.

Finally, notice that we have employed a novel Maker-Taker Rebate-Fee system, discussed on a separate paper, which I can also link here again (or find it on www.taos.im), explaining how the new "Dynamic Incentive Structure" (DIS) works and what its motivation is. Basically, by carefully balancing on your taking and making, you can earn rebates (or be subject to fees). This is incentivizing to trade aggressively when need be, or vice versa. There is also a review of this system by another entity, I will give a link below to that if you are interested. I could go on for a long time on the "whys" here, but I suggest having a look at the paper and any reviews on that before asking. We have plans to make it more "intelligent" in a while, here are certainly ways in the plans how to do that.

Just to clarify and specify some details of the current implementations of the matters discussed by 7/. above:


First each AI Agent (miner) given a certain sum of "wealth" at the start of the simulation.

In the current configuration, each miner receives 100,000 QUOTE in wealth at the start of the simulation.  This wealth is allocated between BASE and QUOTE using a value pulled from a distribution to determine the ratio of the total wealth which is given in BASE and that which is given in QUOTE.  For example; when an agent enters the simulation (registers), if the price in book 0 is 300.00 QUOTE/BASE, and the ratio pulled from the distribution for this book is 0.4, then 100,000 * 0.4 = 40,000 worth of BASE = 40,000 / 300 = 133.33 BASE will be given to the miner, and the remainder (100,000 - 40,000 = 60,000) will be given in QUOTE for initial balances of 133.33 BASE and 60,000 QUOTE.  In book 1, the ratio pulled may be 0.6 and the price 200 QUOTE/BASE - in this book the agent would receive 100,000 * 0.6 / 200 = 300 BASE and 40,000 QUOTE.


The overall performance in this competition is based on average Sharpe over all the "books"

Agent scores are determined by applying an "activity factor" (multiplier obtained from the round-tripped trading volume) onto each of the (normalized) per-book Sharpe ratios, with the Sharpe score for the agent being the median over these activity-weighted values.


with a certain penalty on performing very badly on some of the runs.  This is currently based on what is called the "1.5 Rule," a statistical rule for diagnosing "outliers."

After calculating the Sharpe score as median of per-book activity-weighted Sharpes, if any particular book performs much worse than others (as determined using this statistical rule), the lowest outlying per-book Sharpe score is subtracted from the median value.


The second important thing to keep in mind that is practically quite relevant is the amount of maximum traded volume done in a (full) simulation "day."

The maximum volume allowed to be traded in any 24H rolling window of simulation time is set in terms of a multiple of the initial miner wealth - the value in the current configuration is 20x the initial wealth, meaning 20 * 100,000 = 2M QUOTE can be traded in any 24H window.  If an agent exceeds this total trading volume, no further orders submitted by the agent will be accepted - only cancellations will be processed.  This is typically a death sentence for the miner unless only hit near the end of a 24H period with trading evenly distributed over time, as activity factor will decay in every period where no trading takes place.

[2025-12-23T13:15:42.479Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1453013199661039760
@mvtrx・79  This week we have been monitoring the scoring mechanism and will apply a few revisions to the volume-weighting; also further optimizations to the validator process to improve the simulation progression rate:


Volume Weighting Impact : With the incentives now fully determined by realized Sharpe, the volume weighting of scores becomes less relevant and we apply a few adjustments to reduce the incentive for highly active trading and avoid persisting rewards for miners which quickly pump their score.  The first change is a simple "impact" configuration parameter for the activity factor - this effectively sets the maximum bonus that can be achieved by highly active trading, with the initial value chosen as 0.33, meaning that the maximum activity bonus that can be achieved is 33%.
,
Activity Factor Decay : The second change is a revision to the activity factor decay function; previously this dropped off uniformly over time, allowing capped or otherwise inactive miners to hold on to their scores for significant periods.  Under the new function, activity decays slowly for the first 10 minutes of inactivity, and then drops much more quickly if the miner remains inactive beyond this time.  Note that both these changes are intended to reduce the incentive to trade large volumes, so that the focus is more purely on realized Sharpe performance.
,
Validator Optimizations : A number of optimizations and concurrency management revisions are applied in the validator processes to avoid contention and enable the simulation to progress faster.  We expect with these changes that the total state update handling time will be reduced to 6-7s per update, implying that 1 simulation hour will complete in around 7 real-world hours.  This should enable a complete 24 hour simulation to be executed over the course of each week, although this will depend in part on the miner behaviour which is observed over each period.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet TODAY at ~14:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

UPCOMING CHANGES
We may decrease the volume cap in the next update; we suggest that miners assume a new volume cap of 1.5M per book will be implemented next week so that you do not find yourself suddenly capped if and when this is decreased.
,
We are seeing almost all miners now responding in < 2 seconds, so that a timeout reduction is also being considered.  If your response times are currently above 2 seconds, please attempt to optimize in order to respond within 2 seconds.
,
We are also looking into alternate but similar metrics to the current realized Sharpe which would allow to more efficiently and holistically evaluate performance; more on this would be described when research surrounding this is completed.
,

[2025-12-23T13:15:49.345Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1453013228459397230
Updating on the status of ongoing projects:

Checkpointing : Finalization of simulation checkpointing is still ongoing, some optimizations understood to be required to ensure this does not create additional delays in simulation progression.
,
Dashboard Upgrade : A completely custom rework of the monitoring dashboard has been in production for a while, with the aim of providing a smoother, more intuitive and interactive experience for those interested in observing our simulated markets and the activities of the agents participating therein.
,
Visualization Group : We have formed a group within the team having more precise focus on the production of advanced, insightful visualizations enabling to study all the finer details of the LOB structure.  This will allow to generate totally novel visualizations which utilize the ultimate data resolution produced by our simulation to create never-before-seen illustrations of the microstructure dynamics of modern markets.  More information on this will be provided shortly by @7/.
,
Replay Functionality : The replay functionality allowing to precisely reproduce the conditions of the mainnet simulation has been invaluable in diagnosis of faults and testing of new features, enabling us to confidently deploy updates to the simulator accounting, matching logic and other critical components without risking breakdowns in live conditions.  The next utility to be derived from this capability involves the use of partial replays to incorporate the effect of AI agent activity into our testing; this aims to provide us with a mechanism by which to estimate the expected effects of simulation model adjustments in mainnet more accurately, providing a solid basis with which to select parameters and adjust logic to reach fully realistic simulated markets which can be tuned to mimic a wide variety of asset classes.
,
Testing, Reporting & Analysis : We consistently internally expand and refine the tools used in the testing of simulation configurations as well as monitoring and analysis of the subnet data to better support the tuning of market parameters, study of AI agent behaviour and detection and diagnosis of issues.

[2025-12-23T18:44:33.286Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1453095956663767211
This figure here maybe helps to motivate also the trading algorithm development or risk management idea. The green spike formations are what can be indicated to be "bull markets" indicators, while the red are obviously "bears." The greens are when we can get into over-estimated valuations, while the red territory takes into undervaluation. Much of the dynamics is then about the trade price and LOB varying around the "fair valuation." Although you could consider the right-hand scale ranging from about 220 to 500 a co-incidence of $TAO, the point is that drastic changes can happen quite quickly, and one of main goals here is to picture such risks and help in the prediction of such, and the understanding of "why." The picture here is rather conceptual and illustrative than anything else, though it has been drawn from the TAOS mainnet live.
Link: https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1353733356470276096/1453095956273954877/image_60.png?ex=6ad9b0d1&is=6ad85f51&hm=2c33add66b5d09c9b1edabb1512834f121a3bf8742cef1dd721e5b05c9cdeb6f&

https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1454407145444610192
@6/. Incentive Analysis and Proposed "Fair Play" Metric
Subject: Critical Flaws in Scoring Mechanisms and Threats to Long-term Subnet Stability


PROBLEM: "Kamikaze Burners" – Volume Exploitation
,
,
Mechanism: "Burner" miners trade with extreme intensity, consuming their entire 24-hour simulation budget within just 4 to 8 simulation hours.
,
Time-Compression Effect: Since the simulator runs 6x slower than real-time, those 8 simulation hours translate to 48 real-world hours (2 full days).
,
Consequence: By front-loading immense volume, these miners lock their Activity Factor (AF) at the 1.33 ceiling for two consecutive days, dominating the Pareto leaderboard.
,
Economic Impact: For a registration cost of 0.20 TAO, a burner siphons approximately 0.40 - 0.80 TAO in rewards over two days. They then deregister upon hitting the cap, siphoning rewards away from stable, long-term miners.
,


PROBLEM: Lack of "Reward Armor" (The 0.33 Trap)
,
,
The current AF bonus formula is too weak to protect honest miners from natural decay.

Mechanism: For stable miners, the 0.33 multiplier makes the volume bonus negligible (e.g., boosting AF to only 1.002).
,
The Paradox: In a slow or quiet market, missing a trade interval is inevitable. When an interval is missed, the validator applies an exponential decay (*= decay_factor).
,
Outcome: Because the bonus was so small (+0.002), a single decay step instantly pushes the miner below 1.0. Honest miners have no "score buffer" (armor) to survive market lulls, whereas "Burners" starting at a 1.33 AF profile can withstand hours of inactivity and still remain above 1.0.
,
 (edited)
Saturday, December 27, 2025 at 6:53 PM

[2025-12-27T09:35:01.248Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1454407213375291403
PROBLEM: Statistical Fragility (The IQR Trap)
,
,
The outlier detection mechanism (1.5 IQR rule) currently punishes engineering precision.

Mechanism: Top-tier miners maintain highly consistent, high-quality Sharpe ratios across all books (e.g., a tight range of 0.490 - 0.510). This creates an extremely small Interquartile Range (IQR).
,
Consequence: Due to this tightness, even a minor market fluctuation on a single book (e.g., a drop to 0.480) is flagged by the validator as a "catastrophic outlier," triggering drakonian penalties for the entire account.
,
Absurdity: Miners with mediocre, high-variance results are safer because their lack of precision creates a larger IQR buffer, shielding them from outlier penalties.
,


CONCLUSION: High-Quality Mining is Currently Unprofitable
,
,
The current system is inadvertently designed to reward "hit-and-run" exploits over long-term stability:

Consistent trading results in an AF too low to survive natural market lulls (due to the 0.33 impact).
,
High engineering precision increases the risk of massive penalties (due to the small IQR).
,
A "Burner" who exhausts their budget in one day is economically more successful than an engineer who optimizes an algorithm for weeks.
,

[2025-12-27T09:35:23.232Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1454407305582874689
PROPOSED SOLUTION: "Velocity-Capped Uptime" Model
,
,
I propose a metric that values longevity and consistency over volume bursts:


Formula: AF = 1 + (Eff_Vol / Daily_Cap) * Real_Time_Factor
,
Effective Volume (Eff_Vol): Recognizing a maximum of 1/24th of the daily budget per simulation hour. This prevents burners from gaining an advantage through volume front-loading.
,
Real_Time_Factor: A loyalty factor that grows based on the wall clock (uptime).
Competitive Parity: New honest miners reach full competitiveness within exactly 24 hours of real-world time. This ensures that while "hit-and-run" tactics are neutralized, the barrier to entry for genuine participants remains fair.
,
,
Broadened Outlier Buffer: Adjusting the IQR rule to ignore or cap penalties for miners whose total portfolio range is already below a certain "precision threshold."
,

These changes would eliminate exploiters and ensure the subnet finally rewards true algorithmic intelligence and long-term stability. (edited)

[2025-12-29T19:23:50.499Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1455280170725412966
Going to reply here in general to all. There is going to be more detailed reply to each one of the points from @6/. tomorrow. 

Let me just give some notes already. For the statistical 1.5 Rule mentioned, the problem is not entirely a narrow range. I will give an illustrative example and comparison to a shooting range where the shooter is trying to hit the bull's eye obviously. If the shooter shoots consistently in the wrong place not the bull's eye, then a miss and a penalty on that (to the wrong side) will matter a lot, yes. However, if the consistent group is hitting the bull's eye, or close to it, the penalty on a miss would feel less. That said, we are inspecting ways that would alleviate the mentioned problem – there is one rather straightforward way to at least make it less impactful, which would be possible to release on this week's Wednesday, with other upgrades.

Just to elaborate a bit more: 1.5 Rule is detecting a group of outliers. We can do a small adjustment now in order to be on the safer side of things in relation to the bigger update in the works. Note however that we are working on a challenging continuous flow of progress not the "retroperspective" evaluation of performance – here, the sliding window is narrow. We are now working to make the statistics more meaningful with a likely increase of the window of observation from one hour to 2-3 h. That may also go into next week to combine with other features of similar calibre. With this, I want to emphasize that we are aware of the problem mentioned, but really we have wanted to use common statistical laws and put them into a more challenging online environment, where the number of observations may be unconventionally small (with some bias).

What we are seeking to do more generally is to give miners more freedom to develop different type of algoritms, increasing heterogenuity in the process. We can for example see the MTR (maker-taker ratio) varies quite a lot empirically leading to potential stat arbitrage possibilities. We will be considering also the increase of the MTR's significance to those interested in different types of signals related to that. This would also increase the heterogenous nature, hopefully, of the algorithms. 

Notice that one of the designs in this Sn is to make it harder to scale as the market impacts can become more influential. Like in real markets, you are unlikely to trade the same signal with excessive amount of capital unless you are relatively sure of the correctness of that decision. While we do not want to take out of the possibility to leverage your trade, we are going to drop (very likely!) the hard-cap of maximum 24 h sliding trading volume from 2 M to 1.5 M (that is 15x initial wealth, or keep the ratio to 20x).

This drop would likely occur on this week's Wednesday. There are several reasons behind it. We have previously stated that one of the goals is to incentivize and help to produce real-world applicable trading algorithms with great performance statistics. One of the key metrics is now Sharpe, but others include pure PnL, maximum drawndown (MDD), and Hit Ratio. Similar results appear on the Trading Cards (or Trade Cards) available on the cryptoquay.org website for our Sn 79 already. 

Effectively, a Trading Card would be a quick representation of the performance and in addition it to be limited to a certain starting wealth, it is intended to represent the skills of doing well with maximum turnover of the initial wealth (now 100 k). Having the initial wealth being 15x instead of 20x should incentivize to seek out signals to produce PnL mostly due to skill. While this seems to be restricting the actions a bit, it also diminished the need to trade all the time, as referred to above. (edited)

[2025-12-30T12:07:16.352Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1455532692375605384
1.
First, based on observations of the most recent miner activity and scoring, we are not seeing dominance of leaderboard by miners employing this burner strategy.  With the latest optimizations, changes to the activity mechanism and the subsequent fixes in the detection, this strategy appears no longer viable:

The maximum activity factor of 1.33 can be achieved only if burning the entire 24 hour budget in a single assessment window (1 simulation hour); the highest activity factors observed currently are < 1.01 so that this factor now largely only acts to motivate maintaining of consistent trading volume and does not significantly boost rewards for excessive trading activity.
,
The updated, more aggressive decaying of activity factors further disincentivizes this type of "burner" strategy, since once hitting the volume cap and hence being unable to trade, activity factor decays much faster than previously so that "riding" this boost is not viable.  Even if able to achieve high Sharpe score boosted by activity, this will persist only for a short period of simulation time.
,
Since increased trading volume alone does not provide a significant boost to score, and also considering that positive realized trading profits are necessary in order to receive a good score to boost while noting that a single miner does not consistently receive top rewards, so that most time is still spent with small incentive due to Pareto distributed score, recouping reg cost by this strategy is not possible.
,

2.
Indeed, the latest iteration of activity weighting does not provide much leniency for inactivity - this is intentional, since miners are expected to continuously maintain trading to stay in the race.

Since the activity factor decay only starts after 10 minutes of inactivity, this should not affect miners at all so long as they complete a round trip at least every 10 simulation minutes.  Decay is only applied to miners which are totally inactive for longer than this "grace period".
,
The condition which is more likely to create issues is the minimum of 10 round trips per assessment window - if this is not respected, the Sharpe score for that book is zeroed.  This is under review and may be modified or replaced, since requiring to close a round trip on average every 6 minutes may be excessive in some market conditions.
,
Again, no miners currently reach anywhere near the 1.33 cap; in any case the decay is also designed to reduce activity faster from higher levels, and activity will reduce to zero within ~1 simulation hour even from the highest level.
,
We are assessing the option to increase the assessment window for Sharpe calculations in an upcoming release; this will allow to loosen the requirements on continuous trading so that strategies which seek to trade less frequently will become more viable.
,
 (edited)
Tuesday, December 30, 2025 at 8:07 PM

[2025-12-30T12:08:02.684Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1455532886706094130
3.
The penalty mechanism is intended to be thoroughly revised in the next larger mechanism update, but we are observing and considering modifications to avoid this creating negative effects for consistent miners with well-managed risk.  Although we currently do not observe obviously unfair penalties applied, the point regarding the sensitivity of this in cases of tightly clustered Sharpe ratios is duly noted and we are looking at interim updates to prevent this scenario.

4.
By our assessment, the latest modifications to the reward mechanism have successfully eliminated this strategy from viability.  This is due to:


Round-trip based activity : Even if trading large volumes, if they do not close trades and thus affect their realized PnL and ultimately Sharpe score, the activity cannot be pumped to levels which significantly boost scores without also taking major risks for which they are likely to be punished.
,
Activity Decay : Much more aggressive decay of activity for inactive (capped) miners ensures that score achieved through bursts of trading cannot be ridden to profitability in terms of recouping reg cost.
,

Activity factor now functions mainly just as a motivator to trade consistently, while providing a small boost which allows traders which achieve high Sharpe score while trading larger volumes to outperform those who achieve the same performance with lower volumes.
The penalty mechanism does not seem to be immediately creating unfair destruction of scores for consistent miners, but revisions to prevent this are under consideration.

[2025-12-31T11:57:21.555Z] 6/.

@mvtrx・79  This week we continued to monitor and review the scoring mechanism, and will apply a few adjustments; also yet more optimizations to the validator process to further improve the simulation progression rate:


Optimizations : A variety of optimizations and revisions have been applied in the validator processing to improve the simulation progression rate, avoid delays due to contention and other orchestration issues and ensure that all processes remain up to date with the latest simulation state.
,
Miner Capital Decrease : The initial capital allocated to miners at the start of simulation is reduced from 100000 QUOTE to 75000 QUOTE.  Note that this implies also a decrease in the 24H volume cap to 1.5M QUOTE, as was indicated in last week's announcement.
,
Outlier Penalty Adjustment : In order to avoid excessively harsh penalties applied to miners with tightly clustered Sharpe ratios across books, changes are applied to the outlier penalty calculation: a minimum value is set for the IQR so as to not prejudice tightly clustered Sharpe ratios, and the penalty is scaled in proportion to the range of Sharpes to reduce the penalty when having consistent performance across books.  We also now use the median of outliers to determine the base penalty instead of the mean.
,
Round Trip Requirements : In the current mechanism, if a miner does not complete the required minimum number of round trips within an assessment window, they receive zero score for that book; this is modified to a less harsh form where the Sharpe is multiplied by a factor equal to the ratio of completed round trips to the minimum.  This still enforces to complete the minimum number of round trips, but applies a less severe penalty if having completed some number of round trips.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~14:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

UPCOMING CHANGES
We are also looking into alternate but similar risk-adjusted performance metrics to the current realized Sharpe which would allow to more efficiently and holistically evaluate performance; more on this would be described when research surrounding this is completed.
,
Simulation checkpointing feature is completed but requires further testing to ensure not creating new issues in the simulation processing; focus has been on incentive mechanism, but this will be completed and deployed ASAP.
,

[2026-01-03T00:07:58.056Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1456801224824328293
What I can say currently of our plans is this:


We are looking into releasing a new metric for the miners, on Wednesday 7th, as announced before; this would address more explicitly the concerns raised before, mainly those of Sharpe Ratio being "symmetrically" punishing, and this upgrade would also let us to leave the 1.5 Rule currently applied in the left-hand tail performance. We have not yet had much time to test this new metric, but I remain convinced we can release it on Wednesday and this way support the miners in reaching for the best possible results in making trading algorithms;
,


I can see some of the miners are reaching quite interesting levels of Sharpe, when annualized, so there are profitable trading opportunities in the simulation runs, there is no need to run "random strategies" that are suboptimal. We have also release a few templates that we think are useful in making trading algorithms in general, those are the type that can also be applied in real markets, so the subnet can be used as first testbed for trading algorithms, especially when it comes to any algorithms using L3 MBO level data, which is the "crown jewel" of real exchanges ("market by order" data);
,


In terms of innovations, there is already a long list of them that has never been done in academic literature, and most likely not considered to the level of detail at the industry level either. One of the most recent ones being the combination of a framework called Ising Model that allow allow bubbles and crashes to happen endogenously (within the system). This feature may sound like "academic" but it is very practically relevant for stress-testing algoritms and forecasting crashes. We have indeed evidence that some methods we are aware would have forecasted the October 10th 2025 crash.
,

From our perspective, the Subnet is stronger than ever before, with possibilities to solve some of the main problems in finance, which always deal with risk and return relationship in the end. SInce we are about "risk evaluation" and forecasting of "Black Swan" type of events, the framework is heavy on simulations and runs on C++. This machinery is hard to code precisely, and it is at par with real exchange in terms of advanced order types available, leverage features, and so on. The possibilities that such a framework gives to AI algorithms to learn from will be almost limitless, if data are of high quality.

It all comes down to the single fact that can we reproduce some of the main statistical features found in real exchanges. To address this, we have just now started econophysics.simulate.trading webpage, which showcases visually some key features of TAOS data compared to real exchange data (the data are currently from Kraken, TAO/USD). This page will be improved on every week and the point of that is to showcase how the main features compare and how we are progressing. All of that is therefore transparent development, as is also the coding level work, which is in C++, and getting documented. (edited)

[2026-01-03T22:59:00.555Z] 7/.
