Say, for all here involved with us, JP Morgan has been doing similar experiments, and some of that has been documented on the Internet, and we have been aware of this since the start date to some extent. Of course, some of their stuff is proprietary in nature, so naturally we do not know all the details and motivations – but large institutions in finance do basically what we do, except we do, I dare to say, even more complex product not only because it is decentralized, but how the model is set as a framework, what kind of "agents" are modeled in and to what level their interactions go, with the simplest ingredients but still able to produce realistic series. And since we also work with L3 MBO data production, this is highly unique in the industry and academic work, on top of the fact that really we are on decentralized side. Should people would like to have a look at something such a big institutions is doing and compare to ours, see e.g. "Multi-Agent Simulation for Pricing and Hedging in a Dealer Market" (https://www.jpmorgan.com/content/dam/jpm/cib/complex/content/technology/ai-research-publications/pdf-10.pdf), but we reviewed already years ago some of their associated work (codewise) and chose not to build on theirs for many reasons, among them computational efficience that we have superiority over. But also things I would not rather mention here explicitly at this stage. The above is just one example from a large institution doing things a bit similar to ours. I will just copypaste some of their abstract here for simple and fast review, if people would be in doubt what we do


Deep reinforcement learning algorithms have had consid-
erable success in surpassing human level performance in
several single and multi-agent learning problems. A key
ingredient of these advances has been the availability of gam-
ing and physics simulators which provide a ready stream of
experience for developing, training and testing algorithms.
The financial domain has a rich set of problems, with com-
plex dynamics arising from interactions between hetero-
geneous agents, but doesn’t have a corresponding suite of
simulators that could be used to conduct research. Our ob-
jective is to bridge that gap and develop simulators that can
be used to test and develop learning algorithms for markets.
 (edited)

[2026-01-03T22:59:23.256Z] 7/.

I guess we could run a technical comparison of ours to theirs (of what is public of that, that is) and demonstrate what we do explicitly. Now, the thing is that many financial products are very complex by nature. How many here would have understood what was going on in the US before 2008-2009 crash period with the housing market, with products that were then under subprime products, including such things like " mortgage-backed securities" and "collateralized debt obligations," which were assumed and marketed to be "quite safe" but included tons of risks hidden. The Wall Street (or The City in London) has always been building complex financial products to "lower the risk" with high return, excep that often that is not the case really. The list of complex financial products is a long one, starting from quite tame Asian Options to term structure of interest rates, complex statistical arbitrage strategies, and so on. Our product fits into the Monte Carlo simulations game, numerical options pricing literature and practice, and the applications are almost limitless, considering that some of these stuff can be relatively soon done by quantum techniques, cutting down the computational burden further. That said, one must be able to have AI readable data, and much of that. And that we are doing here.

Yeah we do, the risk metric we currently use has been under investigation, although we have corrected for the stated problems (at least most of them) and will do final checks on Wednesday, and decide whether we push the "new metric" for risk out on 7th. Different risk metrics have different characteristics, and some of the novel uses we would like to push can get computationally a bit too heavy for online environment (although super interesting). So we are going to decide on the features to be deployed tomorrow. We know that we are likely going to decrease the Agent starting capital further from 75,000 to 50,000, but we would then keep the 20x multiplier for trading volume so that the max would be set at 1 M, instead of the current 75,000 x 20 = 1,5 M. This feature would be intended to make it further a bit more careful to set trades, in order to facilitate intelligence over spreading out orders.

@mvtrx・79  This week we have focused on the revision to the scoring metric; this is still in testing, review and analysis, but a couple of updates to be deployed today:


Validator Refinements : Several revisions, refinements and optimizations are applied in the validator to further aid in accelerating simulation progression, avoiding process contention and ensuring stability and perfect function in all scenarios.
,
Miner Capital Decrease : The initial capital allocated to miners at the start of simulation is reduced once more, from 75000 QUOTE to 50000 QUOTE.  Note that this implies also a further decrease in the 24H volume cap to 1.0M QUOTE.  This is intended to further increase the need for careful and intelligent management of funds by miners.
,

We expect to push to the repository and deploy to testnet at ~14:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

UPCOMING CHANGES
After reviewing several alternatives, we have zeroed in on a new risk metric to be applied for scoring in place of the current Sharpe ratio which, while being a standard in industry and research, does only partially succeed in capturing a full picture of the risk-adjusted performance of trading strategies.  We are completing further testing, analysis and tuning of the updated scoring mechanism to ensure that all aspects function as intended, all avenues for exploitation or manipulation are guarded and the changes do not affect the technical operation of the validator.  We plan that this will be released next week.
,
The migration to new scoring metric will be either accompanied or shortly followed by an increase in the duration of the assessment window used in calculation; this to better measure and reward longer term performance as well as improving the statistical significance of the results achieved.
,
Simulation checkpointing feature is completed, further testing to ensure not creating new issues in the simulation processing is pending.  Focus has still been on incentive mechanism, but this will be completed and deployed ASAP.
,

We have additionally been, as always, monitoring and analyzing the data from the live simulation to check for any recurring or novel tactics employed which aim to exploit the reward mechanism; our analysis has not revealed any such behaviour, further confirming the results of previous assessment and the efficacy of the updates applied to address "burner" mining and other score-farming techniques.  This can be seen by evaluating the dashboard data at https://taos.simulate.trading/, or examining the trade cards published at e.g. https://cryptoquay.org/analyzer/bittensor/79/assets/trade-card?simulation=202512311559.
Link: https://taos.simulate.trading/
Link: https://cryptoquay.org/analyzer/bittensor/79/assets/trade-card?simulation=202512311559

[2026-01-07T21:04:23.967Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1458566967714644125
Hello @mvtrx・79 , to add a bit on this regular weekly announcement, in particular related to the mentioned "Trade Cards"


https://cryptoquay.org/analyzer/bittensor/79/assets/trade-card?simulation=202512311559


Yes indeed – I think an unusual and important feature is that this offers visibility over all the miners' trading strategies. Alternative could be to fully open all algorithms, enforcing such, but what we have done here is basically a solution in the middle. Miners retain their IPR, to be used even in real trading activity on real exchanges (not only here), which is the goal.

By having these so-called Trading Cards available for you to review, it is likely easier to develop your own successful ones. There will also be more good templates, and we are working on open AI templates based on RL (Reinforcement Learning). That would mean seriously interesting trading algorithms and templates that serve a real purposes immediately in real life.

The help to more AI does not end there: We have extremely interesting plan on this brewing, of which I will talk more about in another post. This should increase the value of the Sn significantly, building on such Trading Cards already seen on CQ. We hold on to the view that we can reach realistic LOB and usefulness for real trading activity, not only here, but elsewhere.

The cards visual side will be improved on, for sure, and the content can be changed to be even more meaningful for all.

I cite again a JPMorgan Chase "AI Research" division paper where they talk about "Interactive Agent-Based Simulation":


IABS methods provide
an artificial market for the experimental strategy
using a population of background trading agents.
Because the background agents attend to market
conditions and current price as part of their strat-
egy, the overall market is responsive to the pres-
ence of the experimental strategy.


This is different to "common" backtesting that typically serious traders resort to, which they call "Market Replay"


A key weakness of Market
Replay is that the simulated market does not sub-
stantially adapt to or respond to the presence of
the experimental strategy


I would have more to add here, but I will leave that to another post about this explicitly, addressing "why" we do things.
Link: https://cryptoquay.org/analyzer/bittensor/79/assets/trade-card?simulation=202512311559

Yeah so because of it was over 1.5 M  before, and we lowered that to 1 M. Essentially, we are going to give more and more intelligent templates to be worked on, so we expect also the miners to get smarter and smarter in placement, sometimes being less aggressive, sometimes aggressive, like in real markets. Also, since we have a list of advanced features built in already, it is possible to use those advanced order types to your own benefit, again marking more intelligence and more carefully thought out order placement and execution. This is towards what we want to build this to. (edited)

TAOS is an elaborated, decentralized sandbox environment running efficiently in C++. It has the potential to do all of the above and it is getting better. Compared to JPMorgan Chase supported framework, our features are already more extensive. Essentially TAOS is the sandbox for the new exchange, but it could also serve others. [2026-01-16T14:25:32.738Z] 7/.

@mvtrx・79 Hello all! Thanks for following and keep on mining. We are having more exciting news coming up. We expect to release a new risk metric application on Wednesday next week. As you are aware of, we have had Sharpe this far with some modifications. Sharpe is the best known metric in the industry, but it has some drawbacks, essentially that it is penalizing the performance "symmetrically" – seeking high positive returns may lead to low Sharpe. This far, we have combined that with 1.5 Rule from statistics to penalize on the negative tail. This has worked quite okay, but we always seek improvements.

On the next week's Wednesday we are about to replace the Sharpe (including 1.5 Rule) with a metric in the industry called Kappa-3. I can link further information about that here, but you can easily find the original articles and discussions online as well. By replacing Sharpe with Kappa-3 we gain a few things we think are going to be relevant in the next steps. Namely, the aforementioned "symmetry" problem is reduced. Kappa-3 also includes Sortino and Gamma as its special cases, giving space for later refinement in the case of need. This choice is therefore flexible and in ways better than the original Sharpe.

For now, we are going to give you some days to digest and see into that and comment. We welcome your feedback on that.

It is likely we will be then also moving, if not on the same date, but a few days later, from the 1 hour time window to a larger time-window to create more stability in the estimation. This will be explained more in the forthcoming release; the point is to find the best intelligent algorithms that seek to do the best job in this risk adjusted profit seeking universe. Shortly: the game itself does not change really, but the metric will be a bit different as well as the time window will be extended. Those things should address some of the issues raised previously in that more risk taking is welcomed, but controlling that well.

We will have also other incentives likely introduced either on Wednesday, or a bit later, depending on the needs to do that. The stability of any potential "volatile incentive environment" will be further increased by a method we are working on to implement in live then after about 2-3 weeks. This would produce a bit of computational extra burden, but we think it might be a good idea to have the best miners to find the best consistent opportunities here, something that is desirable. More about that technique – probably among the first ones to be really applying that similarly in "real time" – coming soon.


Then for those not so into mining, but interested more generally about the announced direction and in revenue/business:
,
We are taking the whole simulation to another practical level as stated previously. We are likely going to announce the new name for the Subnet by the end of this week (Sunday). Rebranding of that would then commence in steps. The point is to align better with the overall goal of running SOTA exchange integrated with the current TAOS simulation engine, and making the artificial matrix a real-life matrix. Naming and branding will be aligned with this goal in mind. I could go on in depths already of what the system is going to look like, but I will leave that to be revealed in steps as we confirm the technicals.

So, the new name will be revealed and then the connections to the current TAOS which we have been working will be made clearer.

I can say that exciting times ahead and you can expect something unique to be formed by the synthesis to the real world! Together they will form synergies that introduces incentives that bring about more liquidity with proper risk management. Many of the structural and tech changes we are developing are going to improve the business prospects by a large margin. (edited)

[2026-01-16T16:27:42.134Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1461758825370616011
We are first of all saying that the Sharpe, as known, has the "flaw" of symmetry, punishing some excellent performance. We have been noted about that, too, and Kappa-3, in this case would help to resolve. Second, the system would be simplified, since 1.5 Rule (the "Penalty on LHS tail") would be dropped, no longer being necessary as it forms the integral part of Kappa-3. This then means more straight forward calculation. This is what you want as well?

Transparency: Maximum, since it is open to read. But if you have difficulty in understanding of what is going on, we can explain that here in words, as well, no problem. This is not "touched" on except that the "window" over which the calculations are done (currently 1 hour) is likely to be increased to 2 or 3 hours, creating more stable environment, as then more observations from the performance metric are available to be used.

Moreover, the stability can be increased, as mentioned above, by certain rules of filtering which are planned to be done in the next 2-3 weeks and which we have already been investigation and finding attractive also computationally. That is not increasing "complexity" of calculations, it is increasing stability of the players, so that the argument previously woudl be addressed that some players felt their performance is too highly variable.

We are not changing the way things operate. It is still based on 40 books, and the way of averaging works. But the "metric" is slightly different, since Sharpe punishes for "inconsistency". Example: If you shoot consistently at some target, doing that very well, but the target is off, are you shooting actually the best way possible? Sharpe would punish for any bulls-eye hit. We would like to motivate hitting the bulls eye at the right times, with the right volumes.

@mvtrx・79  This week's update includes some important features, upgrades and refinements:

,
Simulation Checkpointing : The long-awaited update to enable resuming of simulations is now included to the codebase; this will allow to deploy simulator updates as well as to recover from any failures without restarting simulation and losing progress.
,
Simulator Parameter Adjustments : Our simulation background incorporates Bornholdt's spin model to simulate potential risks; this model sometimes produces bubbles where prices rise or fall under irrational information: "herding".  The latest updates are aimed at reducing the overall volatility of simulated price series and reducing the likelihood of sudden dramatic changes while still retaining the formation of bubbles and crashes.
,
Validator Refinements : Several further revisions and optimizations are applied in the validator to accelerate simulation progression, improve memory management and ensure stability by avoiding some remaining process contention and data management concerns.
,

UPCOMING CHANGES
Further adjustments to the scoring mechanism are intended to be applied in the next update, either later this week or next, including an extension of the assessment window, revision/removal of activity weighting and outlier penalty components and a further reduction of the volume cap to 10x the current initial capital (10x50,000 = 500,000 QUOTE). These all target to encourage the use of more diverse and careful trading strategies by lowering the threshold for "inactivity" and rewarding intelligence at a wider range of timescales.

TAOS is the "sandbox" environment of the MVTRX Project. Similarly exchanges like NASDAQ, the sandbox provides an environment to develop trading algorithm to be then deployed in live markets. We are designing the mechanism how the incentives work and how the market microstructure is like, and TAOS then is consistent with the rules of the exchange. So, in principle it is straight forward: you can trade at the MVTRX exchange without using the sandbox, but you will gain certain edge by going through the two-step process, aligned with large exchanges, incentivizing building more serious algorithms, giving more liquidity to the market, stability, and predictability over crashes. Essentially, the system is designed to use modern market microstructure rules, including (very likely) the already proposed "DIS" concept (Dynamic Incentive Structrure, see the paper on that at www.taos.im), and alike. We continue to develop the "sandbox TAOS environment," because it is an integral part of the whole MVTRX Project. (edited)

[2026-01-28T12:26:18.406Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1466046730599665775
@mvtrx・79  This week's update revises the scoring mechanism with the intent of allowing a wider variety of strategies by reducing the requirements for continuous activity:


Activity Decay Disablement : The decay of activity factors is disabled so as to avoid penalizing for short term inactivity and allow less frequently acting strategies to become viable; this means that continuous trading is no longer required to maintain full Kappa-3 score, and the miner performance results entirely from the Kappa-3 evaluation.  Only the minimum number of round trips necessary to allow Kappa-3 to be calculated must be completed within the assessment window to be scored; the parameter determining this is reduced from 6 to 3 - i.e. 3 round trips must be completed in each assessment window to receive non-zero Kappa score.
,
Volume Cap Reduction : The maximum volume allowed to be traded in 24 hours of simulation time is reduced to 10x the initial capital - miners will be prevented from submitting further instructions on a book while their total 24H trading volume is above 10x50,000 QUOTE = 500,000 QUOTE.
,
Validator Refinements : Several further revisions and optimizations are applied in the validator to accelerate simulation progression, improve memory management and ensure stability by avoiding some remaining process contention and data management concerns.  These also include optimizations needed for the intended upcoming increase to the Kappa assessment window.
,
BT10 Compatibility : Code is fully updated for compatibility with the latest version of the Bittensor Python package.
,

Updates will be pushed to repository and deployed to testnet at ~14:00 UTC.  Deployment to our validator will be executed ~2H following the push, assuming no issues encountered.

UPCOMING CHANGES
The assessment window for the Kappa calculation is planned to be increased in steps from the current 1 simulation hour in order to further support the use of strategies acting over longer timeframes; this will be executed once having a chance to monitor the system with the latest revisions and finalizing testing to confirm that the additional resource burden created by this update is sufficiently accounted for.  The first adjustment likely to be deployed tomorrow.
,

Updates related to the MVTRX Exchange development, miner infrastructure program and other initiatives will be communicated separately.

[2026-01-29T20:51:24.581Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1466536231776293067
@mvtrx・79 To illustrate our multi-dimensional simulation approach, and the "real matrix" of MVTRX (exchange part), here is something pretty cool to show, 3D cube with six faces, each representing one simulation of Black Swan events.

A “heat bath” is like market noise such as news, rumors, or random shocks that sometimes makes a trader buy or sell even if their peers suggest otherwise. When the market is stable, most traders align and a clear trend forms, such as a steady bull or bear market. Near an unstable point, small bits of news or sentiment changes can cause many traders to switch at once. This can trigger sudden market swings or crashes, even if the original shock was small.

Each face of the cube represents a different possible alignments of the traders. Parallel universes governed by the same rules but driven by different noise. Stability appears as alignment across faces, while instability shows how small shocks can push markets onto very different paths.

You can expect more cool stuff to come – and it will get cooler! (edited)
Friday, January 30, 2026 at 4:54 PM

[2026-02-03T23:46:21.859Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1468392199879135243
Just a bit more context on this road we are on: The main reason – practical as well as theoretical –  for increasing the number of concurrent simulations is that we then (1) gain in statistical significance since we then see the distribution of performance over many simulations, for example, what the average is over the simulated paths (and books) and (2) create more limit-order book data to more successfully and faster fine-tune any of the parameters of the process to match reality.

Why would such a thing matter really? Consider you are actually trying to build AI models, here AI trading algorithms. They will need a lot of data to be successfully trained so they can actually predict something. To not having masses of data means that the AI model is very likely going to be misspecified and any previous success is due to data mining or luck. When then faced a bit different circumstances in the future, the performance degrades and the algorithm loses its edge.

It gets worse. If you believe that AI algorithms can get smarter and smarter, exceeding human level smarts, getting super intelligent, then you definitely need to have large masses of data and have the algorithms conceived being throughly tested before hitting the real market conditions with real money (in finance). Here we come to the point of simulation exercises: before venturing into real trading, with real money, you would like to stress-test (super)intelligent algorithms in sandbox.

Plus there is more to it. You will need to put up correct incentives that hold such intelligence at bay, so they it does not turn against us, or the owner of the algorithm (with real money incentive). The incentives have to govern the actions, and the incentives need to be clear and measurable. This is why we are interested in working on the incentives like we have done, sandboxing, and live markets. Together they will prove to be valuable, in finance (and more generally for the human race). (edited)
Wednesday, February 4, 2026 at 8:15 AM

[2026-02-10T09:09:58.099Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1470708362663563265
When the volume cap is hit, round trips completed within the latest 3 hour rolling assessment window continue to allow score to be calculated until they leave the window.  Once insufficient round trips exist in the window to calculate score on any book, the score for that book goes to zero.
In this 207 case, the cap was hit and scores went to zero, but the UID was not deregistered before old trades left the 24H window and the agent was able to resume trading.

Coming back to this analysis, to provide some clarity on what is measured here - this figure and the one below are produced by analysing the Github repo activity for subnets, where the Consistency Ranking applies some adjustments to the "Raw Development Velocity" (obtained as just median lines added per day) to better capture development pace and consistency.

This ranking rewards subnets that maintain steady, long-term development rather than just bursts of activity. It combines development speed with consistency, coverage, and project maturity to identify teams which actively develop, maintain and improve their subnet code over time.  This highlights the significant effort input by our own team in building and refining our novel, complex and powerful financial simulation environment.

[2026-02-10T15:50:48.075Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1470809235574227156
@mvtrx・79  Expanding a little on the mentioned projects:


Algorithm "exchange" is intended to enable miners, first in our subnet and later in others, to list successful mining algorithms to be licensed or purchased by others.  This aims to increase the capability of the network at large to produce the best possible outputs by providing a more accessible entry point for new participants, fosters iterative development in line with the objectives of open competition, and offers an additional source of income for successful miners, reducing the quantity of alpha token sales needed to cover operating costs.
,
Mining infrastructure service will provide alternative hosting solution for miners (first sn79 and in future other subnets) who invest in subnet alpha tokens; through a convenient and secure deployment and management interface, miners will be able to access compute resources in proportion to their alpha holding profile.  This aims to encourage significant holdings of subnet alpha tokens also by miners by reducing or eliminating their operating costs, removing miner sell pressure as a major source of concern for subnet owners and thus assisting in allowing to reduce burn rates.
,
Our long-awaited upgraded dashboard interface will also be pushed rapidly to release, providing a more intuitive and interactive experience for miners and external observers of the activity within our subnet.  This will increase the transparency of agent and market behaviour, enable convenient detailed analysis of historical data, and through ongoing refinements is hoped to allow to better illustrate and explain the value of our project.
,

Preliminary versions of these tools are expected to be released, at least with limited access, during the course of next week.


Then, this week at the usual time tomorrow we will be pushing a further adjustment to the scoring mechanism aimed at enabling more heterogenous assortment of strategies to be deployed, as well as targeting to include a framework allowing us to incorporate "benchmark" distributed agent strategies:


Inactive Books Allowance : Since particularly signal-based strategies with longer time horizons may not reliably produce sufficient trading activity in all books for every assessment window, an allowance will be made for inactivity on a subset of the books without penalization.  Explicitly, an agent may have up to 24 books with insufficient round trips completed to calculate Kappa score, and this will not contribute negatively to overall scoring.  All books with valid score data will be included in the calculation, only those books up to the 24 maximum which lack sufficient data will be ignored in obtaining the median Kappa.
,
Benchmark Agents : In order to enable us to demonstrate some alternate trading strategy approaches, and also to assist in testing of the abovementioned "algorithm exchange", we will be adding functionality to enable benchmark distributed agents to be defined and operated by us.  These agents will operate in the same manner as miners, receiving state updates and responding with instructions which are executed in the simulation, and all statistics and scoring data will be calculated in order that these agents appear at the dashboard to showcase their performance, but they will not be registered miners and will not be scored on-chain or receive rewards.
,

[2026-02-11T03:33:35.316Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1470986097801691320
In fact, the Bittensor as a protocol has a lot of similarity to how we approach things:


competition between algorithms in real or artificial financial markets is a natural part of the incentive setup
,


on Bittensor there is a horizontal ("panel") dimension across different subnets (128 of them), we have 64 simulations currently, simulated concurrently; horizontal across, vertically would be along one subnet
,

The "difference" is that on Bittensor the 128 "simulations" (different subnets) do different things, they do not have the same data generating process (DGP), they are not statistical even similar

While in our simulations, currently 64, we have price paths and (limit) order books simulated from the "same" DGP, but because of statistical issues, the outcomes, the paths, the realized order books, look different

While we can take the average over the order book simulations and have that tell as more and more precise estimator of the "real performance" (statistically), on Bittensor due to the differences between Sns, taking average does not have the same meaning – you can calculate some averages, but they are not convering to the "true" value

Not sure if that resonates at all, but that's basically what we do. LOL. It is not more complicated than Bittensor.

[2026-02-12T01:19:02.376Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1471314625302888470
Something pretty interesting here. From our LOB simulations. We can detail what it means, but sharing it here for the visuals.

Directed Excitation Network (5-second horizons)

Red = excitation. Blue = suppression. Edge thickness = magnitude.

Self-excitation dominates: market, limit, and cancel events strongly cluster at the same side and level.

Excitation is highly local — largely within-side and across nearby price tiers. Cross-side effects are weaker and less systematic.

Short-term dynamics are driven by localized excitation, not broad cross-book spillovers. (edited)

[2026-02-13T16:03:34.005Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1471899611714158837
Example of "Taker-Maker Flow"

A Tale of Two Traders and the Flow of Money – Sankey Diagram using our simulated LOB data

Imagine a bustling farmers’ market, but instead of fresh produce the stalls are filled with shares, and the shoppers are traders who buy and sell those shares. Every time someone picks up a share and pays another person, a little stream of money flows from the buyer to the seller. If we could see all those streams at once, we would instantly know who is buying the most, who is selling the most, and whether the market is tilted toward buying or selling.

That’s what a Sankey diagram does, but for a market’s trading activity instead of water. In a Sankey diagram the width of each arrow (or “link”) is proportional to the volume of trade it represents, and the arrows connect the “taker” (the party that wants to buy or sell right away) on the left to the “maker” (the party that places a limit order and is ready to trade later) on the right. The colors of the arrows help us read the story quickly: green arrows might mean “buy” activity, red arrows “sell” activity, and maybe blue for “neutral” or “cross‑market” trades.
Link: https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1353733356470276096/1471899611903033524/image_66.png?ex=6ad98b16&is=6ad83996&hm=a53ee9be8013c8399908d53e673717a5a279c9b5bc1c7734d0a7168a557308d7&

[2026-02-14T19:48:40.597Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1472318650332745839
So, this is a trading flow representation between participants using the so-called Sankey diagram technique (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sankey_diagram). Each connection represents executed volume between taker and maker counterparties (left to right). Link colors indicate trade direction, helping highlight behavioral patterns such as aggressive buying or selling activity. 

The chart here is filtered to a defined time window to focus on the most relevant market interactions. This view helps reveal concentration of liquidity, key counterparties, and directional flow imbalances.

Color coding is like this

Trade iniated by:

Red: Sell
Green: buy
Taker: left of link (line attached to right hand side of rectangle)
Maker: right on link (line attached to left hand side of rectangle)

Why it could be relevant: To know which parties are handling most of the volume.
Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sankey_diagram

@mvtrx・79 Updates relevant to MVTRX miners (from thereon, maybe others) in support of the Subnet(s) and Bittensor. The update is related to the overall goal of MVTRX to accelerate and incentivize meaningful, artificially intelligent trading.

A new decentralized point of distribution (or "Marketplace") will soon start start enabling verified Bittensor SN79 MVTRX miners to securely distribute (and potentially monetize) algorithms through cryptographically enforced access control.

Distributors (or "Sellers") undergo multi-chain identity verification before listing. Trading algorithm content is encrypted at the point of listing and remains inaccessible to all parties, including the platform, until purchase. Upon transaction completion, ownership and decryption rights transfer atomically to the acquirer (or "Buyer") on-chain.

Decentralization: Access control is enforced through a network of independent decentralized nodes rather than a centralized server. No single entity holds the keys to decrypt any listed algorithm.

The point of distribution uses native $TAO payments, direct settlement, and immutable ownership records.

@mvtrx・79  This week's update:


Book Count Increase: Book count increases from 64 to 72, stepping towards our 128-book target.
,
PnL Scoring Preparations: Two new PnL-based scoring mechanisms have been prepared but are disabled for now — parameters will be announced for deployment next week.
,
Reporting Adjustment: Simulation ID is now a metric label, preparing for targeted run selection at our new dashboard https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/.
,

Updates will be pushed to repository and deployed to testnet at ~14:00 UTC; validator deployment ~2H later assuming no issues.

─────────────────────────────
Details


Book Count Increase: This incremental step allows us to evaluate performance impacts on validator and dashboard progressively, ahead of the next exchange-relevant target of 128 books.
,
PnL Scoring Preparations: Two mechanisms have been structured. The first applies a PnL-based weighting to the Kappa-3 score, increasing rewards for miners with good Kappa-3 and higher absolute profitability while reducing them when PnL turns negative. The second produces a separate realized PnL metric used in weighted combination with Kappa-3 to derive the final miner score. Both remain disabled pending parameter evaluation — miners are encouraged to review the logic, provide feedback, and consider strategy adjustments ahead of activation.
,
Reporting Adjustment: Simulation ID labelling on metrics will enable convenient selection and comparison of simulation runs via the dashboard in future updates.
,
Link: https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/

It is pushing the envelope in different dimensions at the same time.

@mvtrx・79 Hello, here is a quick review of this current week and heads-up of the next one ahead: Later today, we are releasing another set of updates to the live dashboard, expecting new cool feats. Then, for the next week, there are going to be bunch of things added, more about those next week. First of all, we expect that the Wednesday code release would


add PnL metric to the current Kappa-3 metric; this is to address more comprehensive competition between algorithms;
,
the execution of this idea will be some sort of weighted average (of algorithm rank), 21 % weight on PnL, 79 % on Kappa-3.
,

In addition to the regular code (Wednesday) updates, we expect the "mining service" will take form and allowed to be beta tested, its UI/UX will be alpha version (that is, not properly done), while we allow testing of the functionality. That means, that the supporting platform (CryptoQuay) will allow users to login, connect wallet, and allow miner scripts to be uploaded, processed safely, and run towards Sn-79 MVTRX mining for "almost free" in exchange of holding sufficient alpha of MVTRX.

We will release news here related to the above to the extent it supports MVTRX. We have received DMs inquiries about this.

Further, the "exchange of algorithms" is getting closer to be released. The matter remaining to be done there primarily is a verification process of the associated UID to wallet and the mining script. The two products are intended to facilitate the production of more and more intelligent (trading) algorithms, giving especially newbies better chance to compete in a complex environment. We should be able to send a video/screenshots of the process shortly on how it supports MVTRX.

The use of this exchange of "scripts" can be later combined with the mining service, further exemplified here on MVTRX.

Meanwhile, we have been preparing a working template of reasonable performance, going to be launched at the "sharing platform," and introduce the process more precisely. As mentioned before, we have wanted to create a smooth service to support ingelligence building, especially because here at Sn-79 MVTRX the trading algorithms can be somewhat complex, ideally really dynamically evolving, with dynamic trading volumes, extracting signals from the L3 MBO limit-order book.

We acknowledge that reaching a truly unique product in the space of very competitive financial markets context and AI requires new type of tools with good documentation. So, we are also working on a new data toolbox platform associated with the live dashboard (kind of "more private toolbox"), diving deeper into the datasets, and eventually building to be a toolbox for the real exchange. We have stated that such a combination of tools, data, and novel incentives is a prerequisite for the MVTRX project to work well.

Much going on! (edited)

[2026-02-23T06:05:37.228Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1475373012261011457
We can consider different things surely but the main point in this simulation environment, and the incentives on the exchange is to be able to provide liquidity at the time of "need" and be able to take risk to provide that, while when really the fundamental value (of the asset) seems to change, bid quickly to the right value. The idea of combining the Dynamic Incentive Structure (DIS) paper of ours with this additionally means that we are working on to write a new type of exchange that does incentivize something else than just pure rent seeking in terms of PNL, which can lead to massive speculation and swings. What the right amount of "PNL" and others metrics is not really from our stand point yet that important, it is rather the idea. The fine-tuning process can be done at any time, and the overall numbers, or weights, is to provide the maximal "goodness." That goodness depends on number of different matters, so at this point we are not really intending to optimize yet. (edited)

@mvtrx・79  Early technical update today in further preparation for PnL scoring activation:


PnL Scoring: Revised implementation prepared for miner review — still at 100% Kappa-3, activation of 79% Kappa-3 / 21% PnL weighting scheduled for Wednesday at the usual time.
,
Reporting Refinements: Metric publishing updated for PnL scoring data and improved simulation changeover handling; Grafana updated immediately (https://taos.simulate.trading/) and terminal (https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/) dashboard updated throughout the week.
,
Inactive Books Ratio: max_inactive_books converted from a fixed count to a ratio of 0.375, scaling gracefully with book count — at 72 books this increases the inactive book allowance from 24 to 27.
,

Updates will be pushed to repository and deployed to testnet at ~14:00 UTC; validator deployment ~2H later assuming no issues.
Wednesday's update will proceed on the usual schedule to activate PnL scoring.

─────────────────────────────
Technical Details


PnL Scoring: The realized profitability scoring mechanism has been revised to address concerns identified during testing and to better align its calculation with the Kappa-3 approach. This component remains inactive in today's release (100% Kappa-3 weight) to allow miners time to review the logic, provide feedback, and prepare any necessary agent updates ahead of Wednesday's activation at 79% Kappa-3 / 21% PnL.
,
Reporting Refinements: Metric publishing logic has been updated to include PnL scoring data and to improve handling of simulation changeover, leveraging the simulation ID label introduced last week. The Grafana dashboard will be updated with a simulation ID selector and display of the new metrics. The terminal at https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/ will continue to be expanded with new features throughout the week.
,
Inactive Books Ratio: The max_inactive_books parameter has been refactored from a fixed book count to a ratio of total books, ensuring it scales sensibly as book count grows. Set to 0.375, 37.5% of books may be inactive during an evaluation without affecting the median Kappa-3 calculation — at the current 72 books, this raises the allowance from 24 to 27 inactive books.
,

[2026-03-04T00:31:33.748Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1478550434603073538
@6/. @7/.  Issue: minOrderSize=1.0 is incompatible with partial fills

The problem:

The simulation enforces minOrderSize=1.0 , meaning miners cannot place any order below 1.0 . However, the orderbook allows partial fills — a 1.0  limit order can be filled in arbitrary fractions (e.g., 0.01 , 0.9216 , etc.) depending on available liquidity at that price level.

This creates an unresolvable situation:

Miner places 1.0  BID (minimum allowed)
Only 0.01  fills (partial fill from a small taker)
Miner now holds a 0.01  LONG position
Miner tries to close → must place 1.0  SELL (minimum allowed)
0.01  closes the LONG, remaining 0.99  becomes an unintended resting SHORT
Price moves significantly → 0.99  SHORT incurs a large loss
The miner has no way to close a sub-min position cleanly. Any close attempt with minOrderSize=1.0 creates a new sub-min position in the opposite direction, leading to either infinite oscillation or catastrophic losses.

Root cause:

minOrderSize=1.0 and partial fills are mutually incompatible. The constraint creates positions that cannot be closed within the same constraint.

Proposed solutions:

Option A (preferred): Allow close orders to use the exact position quantity, bypassing minOrderSize only when closing an existing position. The validator can enforce this by verifying that the close order quantity ≤ current open position size on that book — making it impossible to abuse for opening sub-min positions. (edited)
Wednesday, March 4, 2026 at 8:35 AM

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-03-04T00:31:35.442Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1478550441707962445
Option B: Reduce minOrderSize to a small value (e.g., 0.001) so miners can always size close orders to match their actual position.

Option C: Guarantee full fills on opening orders — if a miner places 1.0  and only 0.01  is available, reject the order rather than partially filling it. This ensures positions are always a clean multiple of minOrderSize.

Currently miners are forced to write off sub-min positions as a loss (absorbing the open leg fee) to avoid the catastrophic scenario in steps 5-6. This penalizes miners for a constraint they cannot control. (edited)
Wednesday, March 4, 2026 at 8:34 AM

I would just maybe add here a few words as well. The intent with the minimum order size is/was


to encourage sensible risk taking and not only for the looks; the "right" minimum is under consideration as mentioned, really mostly depending on whether the application of a "significant" minimum serves the purpose of best market quality;
,


to discourage flickering liquidity related to queue priority and tick size; tick size and the minimum order order size can be argued to be dependent on each other, and we are attempting to encourage true intentions and discourage gaming;
,

Plus:


in the simulation setting we have also set maximum amount to be traded so as to incentivize "optimal" trading activity, rather than constant trading activity that would encourage "lesser intelligence building";
,


our new to-be-announced services relavant for this intelligence seeking including especially the "algorithm exchange" (done in collaboration) that would seek to increase the dynamic, intelligent algorithm building rather than "static" style.
,

Thank you for pointing out your concern! We just need to be careful here to avoid going back and forth with the parameters of market microstructure, and go towards the best possible market quality for AI algorithms, especially designed for dTAO.

We have also put in place a few advanced order types, and our intent is actually to put more in. Some of the new ones maybe quite unique, or at least rarely seen, we are intending to innovate in this regard, as also in market microstructure.

==> If there are suggestions or ideas for special orders types to be designed, or need for, we gladly take any suggestions what they could be like, especially keeping in mind the "lower liquidity" end of tokens/assets, to minimize market impact. (edited)

@mvtrx・79  
As mentioned, several supporting projects are on track to reach beta users this week. Here's what to expect:

 MVTRX Data Toolbox
A companion dashboard to the main MVTRX terminal (https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/) is also launching this week. It lets you explore high-resolution data from the simulation engine through an expanding suite of visualizations — great for understanding market and agent dynamics in depth. Those interested in acquiring this data for analysis, model training, or other uses will be able to request it directly through the site, with an automated process planned for a future update.

 CryptoQuay Exchange
CryptoQuay Exchange is an algorithm-sharing platform launching tomorrow with limited functionality (URL announced tomorrow) to support MVTRX AI trading algorithms (later extended to others). Listing access for verified subnet miners will be enabled once everything has been confirmed to be working as expected and all security considerations are satisfied. MVTRX will list a "reverse engineering" algorithm there as the first (free) example.

 CryptoQuay Mining Service
CryptoQuay Mining Service is a platform that allows miners with sufficient staking history on the subnet to run their algorithms on dedicated infrastructure supporting first MVTRX miners, further increasing the decentralized nature of MVTRX. It opens for testing with a select group this week, with broader access to follow once full function is confirmed.

 CryptoQuay Strategy Monitor
Already in production in beta testing mode is a platform done in collaboration with MVTRX for monitoring and evaluating the performance of trading strategies built on the MVTRX trading framework (https://portfolio.cryptoquay.org/; access can be requested from us by DM, for example). As it currently stands, it showcases live analytics for an AI-based portfolio management strategy currently being run using the framework and utilising CryptoQuay data for signal generation — giving an early look at the kind of visibility agents will have into their own strategies once the MVTRX exchange is live. The portfolio strategies' live focus is on dTAO trading with an AI approach, and their rebalancing will later use MVTRX advanced features. (edited)

And most importantly, soon it is possible for miners of SN79 to share their (share license, basically sell, for a price of XXX) trading algorithms to others.

It has been asked from us previously why would somebody want to share, distribution, or sell their algorithm(s) that have taken time and effort to fine-tune, especially in a complicated Sn as ours?

Motivations can be multifod. I will give some examples and what MVTRX (and other subnet) miners want to do, or be interested in such:


too high computational costs versus rewards; miner might not have the access to the right equipment for the right price, but another miner might have
,


too low rewards (too high burning rate of the subnet); the same effect, unattractive considering the costs of mining
,


lower performance over time; waned interest in fine-tuning or following the changes made by the subnet owner(s) so much that better to give up before it is becoming unprofitable
,


personal situation; reasons similar to why somebody might want to sell stock, assets, to liquidate and find cash immediately, since mining has value over time, and not instantly
,


altruism, support just for the sake of it; to support the subnet, community
,


even if the algorithm is still very well performing, problems in scaling up the operations to be meaningful wrt lost time in doing so; others may have better chances to do that and pay more
,

Plus other other reasons. From our subnet owner perspective, we definitely want to accelerate the development of well performing, intelligent algorithms. I will give more throughout discussion of this service and how MVTRX can benefit from that on another day. Glad to answer any questions though!

This Beta is now first accessible and informed about to MVTRX crowd here.
Link: https://exchange.cryptoquay.org/

[2026-03-15T20:52:58.947Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1482844081527980132
Maybe just to say this maybe more broadly:

We are building the MVTRX exchange, it needs to have support from several different angles. In addition to developing the actual technical side of things, part of our team does infrastructure for it and functionalities that help the miners.

Miners from our perspective are the key to doing this in decentralized world. Without them, quite little point of executing on a fairly complicated protocol. We feel we need to find the right incentives and model for miners to support MVTRX.

This would mean in practice that miners provide the liqudiity and main trading activity in the first few months of MVTRX. Therefore, we feel miners form an integral part of it all. We do want to increase the rewards asap we could.

Meanwhile, we have innovated a system that allows this to happen via a separate platform "fine-tuned" first to MVTRX.

While some may feel this is "not developing MVTRX directly," the matter is that part of our team in any case could not directly program the C++ side of the technical side, but have to do supporting side, which is important as well.

For this reason too, we work on the Legals and Sales improvements, so that the exchange could kick in full throttle and would not just be some kind of technical implementation, but a more complete experience.

And as stated, it would start with miners only (exclusively), API approach, and then generalized to allow others to trade. This way too the miners stand in important position like they should, as this is a decentralized protocol for that purpose.

[2026-03-15T20:57:23.152Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1482845189683810538
I should also maybe make a note on LLM and AI related to us.

We have ourselves quite a bit of experience from LLM application, and we have been working on the aspects of LLM applications on financial markets in the past explicitly. In particular, we developed an approach of LLM to the type of data sets we simulate here, and that will form also the basic ingredient of the MVTRX exchange:

L3 MBO 

Read: Level 3, Market-by-Order (https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/faqs/market-by-order-mbo.html)


Market by Order (MBO) describes an order-based data feed that provides the ability to view individual queue position, full depth of book and the size of individual orders at each price level.


Such data are supported by NASDAQ and others, in crypto as well by exchange Coinbase, Kraken, as well as few others.

Without having such data available, LLM in particular is pretty much useless, as it would require a lot of data to be used. We have ourselves used LLM in LOB (limit-order book) modeling and we are interested in taking that forward.

The type of simulations we currently do, and the messages available at the real MVTRX exchange, then supports LLM.

More about this soon. (edited)
Monday, March 16, 2026 at 5:10 AM
Link: https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/faqs/market-by-order-mbo.html

[2026-03-16T17:49:59.537Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1483160418410303752
No worries

We will be updating / renewing our webpage (mvtrx.fi) and it will have more information about it all.

Quite important that the miners have basically two options: to continue in the sandbox, with similar incentives like now, and/or go to the real exchange side, with the same rules (market rules) than in the sandbox, but then with real "money."

While the goal is to make the market more efficient and stable, it is also the case that if the true value of the asset increases substantially, well, like in the case of Templar just recently, the market price also needs to adjust quick.

So it is about finding the true value.

Also to predict and avoid crashes, which is one of the reason we build this toolbox.simulate.trading to let the miners understand more fully what is going on at the HF levels, how to avoid being taken advantage of, how to avoid crashes.

Both the simulation sandbox and the real exchange intended to have the same market microstructure rules. It depends on what the actual rules will be like in matching and such, we are currently reviewing several possibilities to maximize the chances of simulations then being aligned with the real exchange. I would say at this point it is likely that the simulations (sandbox) provides good advise, but not complete match, and simulations may focus on the top liquiidy Sns.

The bottom line in developing a new exchange is really doing innovations at the market microstructure level, what kind of order-types available, how liquidity is maximized, how to prevent manipulation tactics, and overall max out market quality.

@mvtrx・79 Happy Easter! Our GenTRX's (GenTRX is a generative limit order-book model) code and docs are now structurally complete. The remaining work is integration testing and bug fixing.

Model v4 complete:

  - 12.1M params, FiLM conditioning, symmetric log price binning

  - All 5 output heads, weighted loss, sweep + standard training

In more detail what's done:

  - Core model, tokenizer, matching engine, inference

  - Distributed training pipeline (gradient compress/score/aggregate)

  - Agent serves trading (inference) + training concurrently

  - S3 store abstraction (Hippius/R2/MinIO)

  - Docs: assignment protocol, validator integration, join training, training params

  - Tests: model smoke tests, S3 store integration tests

  - Package: pyproject.toml with extras

Will be thrilling to release this on top of MVTRX exchange & simulations! We need a further few days to test it out properly. (edited)

[2026-04-08T11:20:11.204Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1491397241540182108
First, I will share general info on the AI-driven technology we have developed and making an integral part of the MVTRX structure. As those that watch the DEMO of our Prototype will realize, and others will see VIDEOS of, we are actually making meaningful innovations in exchange technology/ies. The first one is related to (more intelligent) order-types.

This is no traditional exchange, features will be interconnected, and AI agents will be at the forefront of it.

MOTIVATION

Traditional stop-loss and take-profit mechanisms are essential tools for managing risk and locking in profits, providing traders with predefined exit levels that bring structure and discipline to trading. However, these levels are typically fixed at the time of order placement, which means they do not adapt as market conditions evolve. In practice, this can lead to stops being triggered too early during short-term volatility or profits being taken prematurely, while in calmer conditions the same levels may be less effective. As a result, traders often need to manually adjust their settings, yet still face limitations in responding to changing market behaviour.

OUR SOLUTION

Our proposed AI-powered order type addresses this by continuously adapting stop-loss and take-profit levels in real time based on current market conditions. Instead of static rules, it intelligently adjusts to volatility, liquidity, and price dynamics— helping prevent premature exits while capturing more meaningful price movements. The result is a more responsive and efficient trading experience that improves consistency and performance without requiring users to change their strategy.

[2026-04-08T12:10:54.732Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1491410007021846589
Secondly, we have managed to develop one more core functionality allowing for efficient on-chain / off-chain ramping:

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

Real-time professional-grade exchange settlement on a decentralised network is a hard problem. Over the past 3–4 weeks we have made significant progress on a core piece of it: an efficient chain data retrieval and instruction handling system capable of querying, batching, and parallelising large volumes of on-chain data and transactions. This is what will allow MVTRX to deliver a true limit order book with full L3 MBO (market-by-order) data and what gives AI trading agents the data resolution they need to operate at exchange speed. No existing venue provides this combination.

WHERE WE ARE:

Over the past 3–4 weeks we have developed an efficient chain data retrieval and instruction handling system to achieve the settlement accuracy and speed that the MVTRX exchange requires.

WHY IT MATTERS:

Our solution enables efficient querying of on-chain data combined with batching and parallelisation of instruction management allowing large numbers of transactions to be submitted and processed within every block. This is closely connected to our core exchange function: providing a professional-grade limit order book with L3 MBO (market-by-order) data, which is essential for AI agents to operate effectively.

This is a core requirement for the exchange to function. It enables us to retrieve all necessary data and submit and process instructions routed through the exchange in an efficient, scalable, and accurate manner. Recall that our goal is to serve AI agents first, others next. That implies our solutions have to be efficient for speedy actions with large amount of data.

More technical details to be explained out.

[2026-04-08T12:55:36.018Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1491421253150703696
Thirdly, to update on the third MVTRX related functionality related to the generative product we are calling GenTRX:

WHERE WE STAND:

GenTRX has its first full end-to-end test running. The simulator, validator, training agents, and gradient server are all connected — miners training on live simulation data, gradients flowing into a shared model, and the matching engine running closed-loop inference through a local test environment. The core infrastructure is in place and working.

We are now validating the full pipeline before wiring it into the live system.

WHY THIS MATTERS:

Markets are driven by order flow; individual bids, asks, and cancellations that most models never see. GenTRX learns that flow at the atomic level, training a shared LOB prediction model that gets better the more miners participate. No hand-crafted rules.

The market dynamics emerge from the data.

This creates a feedback loop that's new for the subnet: miners run simulations, simulations generate training data, training data improves the shared model, and a better model means sharper strategies — both in simulation and on the live MVTRX exchange when it launches.

The model is openly available to every participant. The more miners contribute, the better it gets for everyone.

This also changes the economics of AI adoption on the subnet. Building a competitive AI-based trading strategy from scratch requires data, compute, and expertise most miners don't have. GenTRX removes that barrier — the shared model is a foundation anyone can build on, and miners earn for contributing to it alongside their normal trading rewards.

FOR TRADERS (AT MVTRX):

Unlimited synthetic scenarios for strategy development and backtesting — not the same historical tape replayed, and not scenarios you have to construct by hand.

FOR THE PROTOCOL (BITTENSOR):

GenTRX is the first live demonstration of Templar's distributed training infrastructure applied to a domain outside language models — a financial market prediction model, trained collaboratively across miners, with real economic incentives.

If it works here, it works anywhere. That is a significant result for Bittensor as a whole. (edited)

@mvtrx・79 

No simulation updates this week — full focus on the exchange. Here's what we're targeting over the next week or so:

GenTRX — LOB Prediction Training
Distributed limit-order-book prediction model training opens for miner participation. This is a meaningful new way to contribute to exchange intelligence beyond scoring — participation details will follow as integration is completed.

ExeTRX — AI Stop-Loss / Take-Profit
In process of being fully implemented and integrated across both the simulation and exchange engines. We're evaluating whether to activate this for current simulation runs ahead of exchange launch or hold it for the live environment.

MVTRX UI — Trading & Monitoring
Continued development and testing across the terminal interface. Highlights planned to be included by next week:

Observe Mode — read-only entry into the terminal to watch live dTAO trading activity without placing orders
,
Trading Interface — Simplifying, streamlining and enhancing the "classic" trading view at the UI
,
Chart enhancements — additional candle styles, oscillator sub-panels, multiple independent indicator instances, TV-style hover values in the legend
,
Drawing tools — full select, drag-to-move, and delete replacing the erase tool; hover highlight and hit-testing across all drawing types
,
3D Order Book (Canyon View) — canyon visualisation of the live L3 order book; bid and ask walls animate in real time as orders are placed, cancelled, and filled
,
Explorers view — live force-directed graph of all active UIDs and their trading relationships; nodes connect by volume-weighted edges with real-time trade animations, filterable per subnet
,
SL/TP panel — collapsible Stop Loss / Take Profit section in order entry with AI Tolerance (σ) presets (Fixed / Tight / Moderate / Wide / Aggressive) and a live range preview showing exact price targets
,
Exchange API - A dedicated developer portal with full API reference and interactive endpoint testing, along with API key management for programmatic access. Official client SDKs will be included for Python, Rust, Go, C++, and JavaScript/TypeScript — each with full hotkey auth, REST and WebSocket clients, and worked examples.  This to allow more familiar method of interaction with the exchange in addition to current agent development structures, providing an alternate approach for agent development allowing to use any language and tools to interact with validators.
,

Deployment & Hosting
Completing full hosting and deployment for the MVTRX UI, connecting first to testnet simulation runs then mainnet — so current miners can begin exploring and using the interface against live simulation data ahead of exchange open.

CQ Exchange & MinerQuay — Integrated Deployment
CQ Exchange (algorithm marketplace) and MinerQuay (automated miner deployment) are being integrated into a tighter end-to-end pipeline. Goal: faster onboarding for new miners, and meaningfully lower operational overhead for those already running.

Summary : What's New Deployed

–– Classic Trading view, streamlined

Tabbed order book / trades panel, chart maximize, sidebar collapse, and OHLCV hover bar with inline indicator values. TradingView mode is now the default.

–– Nexus Explorers View
A live force-directed graph of every agent active on the subnet — miners, benchmark agents, and sim classes as nodes, with volume-weighted arcs lighting up between trading counterparties as fills happen. Filter by subnet, hover edges to see who's trading with who.

–– Canyon View — the order-book as terrain (early concept — more to come)
The live order book as a 3D canyon you fly through — bids rise as green mountains on your left, asks as red cliffs on your right, camera drifting toward price movement. –– Multi-wallet support
Connect via Polkadot.js, Talisman, or any compatible browser extension — MVTRX detects what you have installed and lets you choose.

–– Proxy setup in-app
Authorise and fund proxy wallets directly from the UI, with on-chain signatures from your browser extension.

–– Exchange API — coming
Programmatic access to market data and agent state is in private development, with client SDKs planned for Python, Rust, Go, C++, and TypeScript. More details when it's ready.

–– Testing is going well — lots of performance and usability improvements under the hood in this batch too.

[2026-04-29T12:58:47.799Z] 6/.

@mvtrx・79 
A number of updates land in the MVTRX UI preview environment tomorrow, with a lot happening across the project as we push toward testnet and mainnet.


 ExeTRX - Stop-Loss / Take-Profit
,
The first ExeTRX capability will be ready: miners will be able to set static SL/TP levels directly from the UI when placing trades, with the exchange handling execution automatically. SL/TP parameters will also be supported in order submissions from automated trading agents - miners will be able to take full advantage of this once simulation mode opens.
The AI component - an in-house trained model that will actively monitor and adjust SL/TP levels in response to market conditions - is in final integration, expected early next week.


 ARYA - AI Trading Assistant
,
ARYA will be a conversational AI built into the exchange UI. Ask it questions, get market context, or switch on Autonomous Mode and let it generate instructions to be submitted - with full awareness of your open positions and SL/TP levels.
UI is complete; model hosting and final testing are wrapping up, with a version expected online next week.


 Streamlined Trading View
,
The exchange UI has been further streamlined and refined, with entry/exit points and SL/TP levels also clearly visualised directly on the chart. Full TradingView advanced chart integration is prepared and ready to enable once licensing application is approved.


 Batch Order Submission
,
Agents will be able to submit multiple orders under a single signed action. This will enable allocation and rebalancing across multiple subnets in one go - and pairs directly with ARYA, which will be able to generate a full set of trading suggestions submitted as a single batch.


 On-Chain Visibility
,
A new explorer panel will let you observe wallet activity on-chain outside of the exchange - giving miners a clearer view of their full position and flow across the network.


 Deployment & Infrastructure
,
We've been building out robust hosting and deployment infrastructure in preparation for testnet and mainnet. Simulations are the first step, and we expect to move into that phase over the next couple of weeks.


 GenTRX - Coming to Testnet Next Week
,
GenTRX is our distributed model training mechanism. Miners will collaboratively train a shared, open-source AI model for limit order book prediction - lightweight enough that anyone can participate without specialised hardware.
The resulting model will be a public good, equally available to all participants, while individual miner strategies remain private and competitive. Final testing now; miners can expect to get involved on testnet next week.


 CQ Exchange & MinerQuay - Integrated Deployment
,
CQ Exchange (algorithm marketplace) and MinerQuay (automated miner deployment) are being merged into a tighter end-to-end pipeline. Goal: faster onboarding for new miners, lower operational overhead for those already running. Expected ready for beta users this week or early next.
---
Preview access is available to a limited group ahead of broader rollout. If you're interested, reach out.

Again no simulation updates this week as we focus on the exchange and related products. (edited)

I have noticed a slight deviation after registering a new miner.

It's after registration that I encounter such issues, as my trading strategy never receives a penalty.

@mvtrx・79 

GenTRX is live on testnet.
,
Distributed gradient training for SN-79 is now running on testnet. Miners can spin up and start submitting gradients today. We're shaking the system out before mainnet and the more participants we have, the more we catch.


Miners
,
If you plan to mine GenTRX on mainnet, get on testnet now. Setup, GPU sizing, gradient submission, scoring behaviour, all of it benefits from a dry run while there's nothing on the line. The miners who show up here will be ready to go the moment we cut over.

We're also running a non-mining benchmark agent on UID 256 that submits gradients alongside everyone else. It's there as a reference point so miners can compare their own scoring against a known baseline.

Get started:
Code: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test
,
Setup guide: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/test/doc/gentrx/miner_setup.md
,
Quick start: ./run_miner.sh -G -w <coldkey> -h <hotkey> -u 366 -e test
,

GenTRX training can be run alongside your existing miner with no changes to your trading strategy. GPU recommended (RTX 3060-class or better) but CPU works.

A preliminary GenTRX dashboard will be available soon for tracking gradient submissions and miner stats.

If you run into problems, see anything off, or have feedback, please contact us.


Validators
,
If you might be willing to help test, reach out directly. We'd love the coverage ahead of mainnet. (edited)

[2026-05-22T13:24:20.496Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1507373552221819163
Related to our research & development investigation and application in automated parameter optimization methods:

We introduce a framework that uses multi-fidelity Bayesian optimisation to automatically calibrate the parameters of our agent-based market simulators. Realistic markets emerge from the complex interaction of heterogeneous agents — each governed by dozens of parameters that are notoriously hard to tune by hand. Our framework closes this gap by framing calibration as a black-box optimisation problem: it iteratively proposes parameter sets, runs the simulator, and scores the resulting synthetic market against quantitative targets derived from real market microstructure, automatically steering toward configurations that reproduce the statistical fingerprint of real order-book dynamics. Preliminary results show significant improvement over manual calibration, with the optimised simulator reproducing key stylized facts of crypto markets far more faithfully across a range of realistic trading conditions.

More information will be shared next week already. This is an important piece in the overall puzzle of a realistic "matrix."
Link: https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1353733356470276096/1507373552318550086/mvtrx-framework-to-optimize-params-screenshot-1.png?ex=6ad965c4&is=6ad81444&hm=8da90f19b2b99a858dc2642d3bdec8e2b8773343aac3b12c6c8a21bb46c45631&

[2026-05-27T21:23:56.317Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1509387974587060245
A few practical examples for real trading, as well as simulation side:


the approach can for example help in predicting your fill probability (use of market order versus limit order, simply put), essential in efficient inventory management say in market making, or statistical arbitrage strategy classes;
,


the approach can also be used to minimize transaction costs and market impact, helping to produce better PnL and Sharpe Ratio (we use very similar ratio called Kappa-3);
,


the approach can also be used to detect, ahead of time, toxic liquidity and Black Swans, to get out of the way of larger buy or sells, or indeed manipulative attempts on price levels.
,

LLMs do require a lot of computation power and this is one of the reasons why decentralized approach is interesting.

@mvtrx・79  

GenTRX testnet update | v0.4.5
,
Scoring updates, faster simulation progression, and lower memory footprint across miner and validator.

Scoring
Near-miss predictions on price, volume, and interval now earn partial credit
,
Larger gradients by default for better signal preservation
,
Checkpoint versioning keeps scoring consistent across regimes
,
Correctness improvements on the gradient server side
,

Miner
Lower steady-state memory across training cycles
,
Faster flush cadence, better aligned with the gradient server
,
New device override for explicit CPU/GPU selection
,

Validator
Several optimisations to improve simulation progression rate
,
Some scoring-neutral optimisations have already been deployed to our mainnet validator to improve rate of progression immediately
,

State handling
More reliable lifecycle event delivery
,
Tighter handling of scale configuration
,

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

Miners
Pull and restart. A few things worth noting:


Scoring will shift this release. Near-misses on ordinal fields are now rewarded, so models that were close-but-not-exact should see scores rise.
,
Default training config changed. New defaults are now device-aware: 100 steps with batch size 4 on CPU, 500 steps with batch size 16 on GPU. The CPU defaults are tuned to fit the training window comfortably. If you have headroom you can override.
,
New gtx_device setting lets you explicitly pick CPU, CUDA, or a specific GPU index, instead of letting the system auto-detect.
,


Pushed to test branch. Miners should switch already to this branch ahead of mainnet deployment tomorrow, and report any issues.
,
 (edited)

Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

@mvtrx・79  

Coming to MVTRX: SWAP
,
We've been listening - in conferences, in DMs, in this server, in conversations with miners and traders building on Bittensor. SWAP came directly out of those requests from the trading community, and we're shipping it fast because the need is real.

Rolling out over the next 1-2 weeks, SWAP is an interim step ahead of the full exchange release - it brings activity onto the platform, lets us test the basics of the execution layer in the wild, and gives users the simplest way to trade dTAO directly from the terminal, without leaving the browser or giving up their keys.

Accessible through the Nexus UI in observe mode - real stake/unstake, executed directly against mainnet.


What SWAP Does
,
⇄ Direct On-Chain Staking
,
Stake, unstake, and move alpha across any subnet - TAO → alpha, alpha → TAO, or alpha → alpha in a single transaction.


 Non-Custodial, Always
,
Sign with your own coldkey wallet (Talisman, SubWallet, polkadot-js) - MVTRX never holds or sees your keys. Every transaction is shown decoded in your wallet before you sign.
A deeper Talisman integration is also on the roadmap, working with the Talisman team on a smoother end-to-end experience for Bittensor users. We're also open to other wallet solutions - if there's one your community uses, let us know.


 One-Signature Rebalances
,
Bundle multiple swaps into a single transaction. One popup, one fee, every leg settling independently with its own result.


 MAYA Integration
,
Ask the AI for an allocation - execute its suggested swaps as a single signed batch.


 A Real Terminal Around It
,
Live charts, positions across every subnet, full swap history with settled amounts, realised slippage, and fees. Honest results only - what actually happened on-chain, including decoded errors if something reverts.


Why This Matters
,
SWAP is the easiest entry point to MVTRX yet - available through the Nexus UI in observe mode and it's own dedicated page. If you hold TAO in a wallet, you can trade.

It's also a deliberate stepping stone: a way to bring live on-chain activity to the platform and stress-test the execution layer ahead of the full exchange release (order types, AI agents, the works) - which sits one step up from here.

And it's a direct response to what the community has been asking for. Keep the requests coming - we read every one, and the ones that solve real problems get built. The exchange is being built with the people who'll use it, not at them.


Rollout
,
Rolling out in the coming 1-2 weeks as we open access in stages. Exact dates announced here as we flip the switches. Priority access for early supporters.

Questions, requests, or want in early? Drop them below.
