Development
,
⇄ MVTRX SWAP - Targeting Next Week
,
Following last week's announcement (⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠), and built directly in response to requests from the community of miners, traders, and active users, SWAP is progressing well and is expected to open up next week for users with pre-access to the platform - stakes, unstakes, and swaps across subnets, with:


Multi-wallet handling with batch signing - requested by traders rebalancing across multiple wallets, to make managing positions across subnets meaningfully faster.
,
MEV protection - in direct response to concerns raised by users trading meaningful size on-chain, where protection matters most.
,
MAYA integration - extending MAYA's planning capability so it can plan and propose on-chain swap transactions as part of its broader allocation and trading strategy.
,

The wallet integrations themselves are a direct outcome of Proof of Talk in Paris - conversations with wallet teams and active Bittensor traders surfaced clear demand for broader support, so we've extended coverage to include:


Talisman
,
polkadot-js
,
Crucible
,


 UI Refinements - Continued Improvements
,
Further upgrades to the traditional trading view prepared, plus various refinements and responsiveness updates. Expected to land in localnet preview later this week alongside the other completed tools.


 Hangar - First Release Pushed to Next Week
,
Refinement, expansion, and testing continue. New additions include more streamlined wallet management, in-platform UID registration, and algorithm builder features. First release delayed to next week due to a third-party dependency issue requiring some aspects to be redesigned.


 UI + Simulations on Testnet - Still Targeting This Week
,
Still on track for this week, though production hosting config and testing are taking a little longer than expected. We'll confirm timing as the setup finalises.


 GenTRX UI Tools - Alongside Testnet Launch
,
Still targeting this week alongside the testnet launch of simulations + UI - signals, on-demand predictions, order impact estimation, and integrated use by MAYA.


 Exchange - Localnet Next Week
,
Localnet exchange expected to follow the testnet sim + UI release, with the localnet registration process for preview users to start interacting with the exchange directly.


 AI-Driven Simulation Tuning - Strong Progress
,
Work on the automated parameter optimisation framework continues, with promising results. As MVTRX scales, we'll be running hundreds to thousands of calibrated simulations in parallel - each one tuned to match real on-chain market behaviour. No human team can manually tune that many - hence we turn to automated AI tuning. Current focus: reporting tools, feature selection, and parameter selection processes, with the methodology being refined against real datasets - more concrete results to share soon.


 ExeTRX - Patent Application Underway
,
Patent application still underway. Testing against varied real-world data is making good progress in generating evidence of value.

@mvtrx・79  GenTRX testnet update | v0.4.6
Robustness and restart-safety improvements. Pull and restart.


Scoring robustness — cleaner signal on validator dashboards
,
Restart safety — accumulated training data now persists cleanly across gradient server restarts
,
Hot-path improvements — smoother assignment delivery alongside state tick processing
,
Miner retention — new gtx_keep_intervals_per_book (default 12, around 1 hour) significantly reduces local storage requirements
,

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

⚠ Update required to keep being scored. Gradients now include the model version they were trained against. The aggregator will start filtering out untagged gradients once the rollout window closes, so miners on older releases will stop being scored. Pull and restart to stay on the scored set.

Set gtx_keep_intervals_per_book=0 to retain all local parquets if you'd rather trade disk for full offline history.

Mainnet deployment tomorrow.
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

[2026-06-13T17:33:54.956Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1515408892702752891
We will clarify the model(s) next week. The basic logic is here though: We may give all an opportunity to lock in, but not a "have to." If locked in some, it would lead to certain advantages like lower trx costs or other benefits with a lower price point. Since we are currently not so enthusiastic on setting volume based tiers, for reasons to be explained, conviction could give an opportunity to take advantage of the new mechanism of Bittensor in a reasonable manner. However, this is yet at a proposal stage currently and we are collecting feedback and fine-tuning our mechanism, seeing if it would work.

==> That is the first point here, optionality while we are not wanting to use the trading volume tier structure at this point.

Another motivation is that – as most of you guys know well by this time – we have locked in a significant amount of alpha. Having a small reasonable lock-ins from our user base would likely boost the trust and attract also other investors, outside of Bittensor. Those investors could be influential for the business case we have. Again, in this model, no necessary "have to," but an option(s). Threshold would be set to be a reasonable one, which is under research (what the best one would be). 

==> That is, such conviction "boost" would of course would be just an additional investment in the business, that's all. It can be considered as subscription of prepayment, but in the form of investment, rather than "lost" amount to be paid right now.

In other words: The business model of MVTRX is likely to have several ways to achieve better transaction fees and/or fee subscription terms. The "boost" given by the conviction would then be optional, but potentially very useful for the project at hand. Since we are totally committed in the long term in this, the conviction mechanism could just add to that trust by others. In traditional exchanges, trading volumes and token ownership (usually based on past 30 days average, or such) is applied. But to get to a level of trading volumes being meaningful and "tier up," one has to first spend a lot of effort to do so.

The traditional exchange business model model is sort of outdated. We want to be "A New Kind of Exchange" in that as well. We would rather not repeat their exact business model. We seek models that are the future, not the past. New models. The main difference here is that conviction is forward looking: One would not have to wait for certain X limit(s) to be reached. 

In any case, many of the features will likely start with no or little fees on them, at least for some testing and reasonable use. We are definitely not trying to levy costs immediately, rather we will be exploring the usefulness for different type of users. Since we work on top of Bittensor, we are exploring different ways how the protocol could be used intelligently in business.

I hope this explains this motivation a bit more – and we shall have more discussions with interest groups before any launch.

[2026-06-17T14:28:43.590Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1516811839718297621
Regarding business planning, we do have a business plan for the services. Here's a quick brakedown.


It is very likely the "real trading" side (which is the "red" side in MVTRX) will have zero trx costs, at least to begin with
,


There will be use-case for Conviction Mechanism that is not mandatory to use, but it would give certain preference over new functions, the extent of their usage, and further discounts on subscriptions;
,


The subscriptions are planned to be either yearly prepayment, or monthly; the former has clearly cost saving idea incorporated, and Conviction participation gives further reducedr rates, while the latter does not have discounts and operates on monthly basis as is usual in such formats.
,

There will be also different levels of "usage" or game-play, although those features will be somewhat limited in the beginning. These levels mainly attempt to make the UX as fluent as possible ranging from "Easy" to "Expert" usage.

Since we have been requested to implement also "swap type" functionalities, these do not involve any limit-order-book  (LOB) actions, or requirements, while the more "expert" modes with especially AI involved is clearly dependent on LOBs.

The technical update of the status will come shortly.

@mvtrx・79  Status Update

This week's sequencing reflects what the community has been asking for, and how the pieces start working together.


Development
,
⇄ MVTRX SWAP - Activating in Localnet
,
SWAP is being activated in localnet today or tomorrow for select preview users to test functionality and provide feedback - built in response to direct community requests. The flow lets you stake, unstake, and move alpha across multiple wallets with a single signature; protects against stale prices and front-running; and works seamlessly with MAYA's AI-assisted planning. Wider release follows once localnet testing confirms the full flow.


 GenTRX UI Tools - Activating in Preview UI
,
GenTRX inference is being enabled in the preview UI today or tomorrow. What this means in practice: live signals overlaid on the subnet explorer, on-demand predictions for any subnet's market state, an estimator that shows how an order would move price before you place it, and MAYA factoring all of this into its planning. The inference layer needs to be live and serving the latest model before real trading begins - so when the exchange opens, these tools are already integrated.


 UI - Refinements and Upgrades
,
This update directly addresses feedback raised in the channel: drawing tools now work correctly across all screen sizes (the broken behaviour on smaller viewports), compatibility fixes across major browsers, layout fixes across different screen sizes, and polish across the Conviction tier system (tier badges, leaderboards, multi-coldkey wallet picker).

Targeted for next week: an Easy / Advanced / Expert mode selector at the global level - Easy for direct staking with no order-book knowledge needed, Advanced for traditional trading view with full charting, Expert for AI-driven workflows with deep order-book interaction. Also in progress: further UX refinements to the chart for a more familiar and convenient experience closer to what traders expect from professional charting tools.


 MVTRX Terminal - Updated Release Imminent
,
A refresh of the MVTRX Terminal at mvtrx.simulate.trading is expected today or tomorrow - replacing the current Grafana dashboard. All the data that's currently in Grafana is now also available in the new Terminal (previously some was missing), with noticeably faster loading and navigation throughout.


 UI + Simulations on Testnet - Targeting Tomorrow/Friday
,
Targeting tomorrow or Friday. In practice: testnet simulations connected to the production UI. Miners can place orders into the simulated environment, watch them execute against the agent-based market, monitor positions through live charting, and use MAYA and GenTRX to evaluate strategies - all before any real capital is at stake.

[2026-06-17T15:47:56.329Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1516831774150492325
 Hangar - Slightly Deferred
,
Hangar deployment is slightly deferred this week while SWAP and the testnet sim + UI deploy take priority, and we finish the third-party dependency update flagged previously. In the meantime, the underlying MinerQuay miner-launch stack just received a substantial upgrade, now validated by external miner testing - see the CryptoQuay section below. This is the same stack Hangar runs on, so by the time it opens, the foundation is already proven.


 Exchange Localnet - Coming Soon
,
Localnet exchange coming soon - registration live in the UI, requesting localnet TAO is enough to start interacting. Important: this is testing only - no real value is at stake, the stack runs against a local test network so we can validate everything before moving to testnet and eventual mainnet. When it opens, this is where the full trading experience comes together: a live order book with advanced order types, MAYA for AI-assisted planning, GenTRX for predictive signals, and Conviction tiers shaping access.


 AI-Driven Simulation Tuning - Strong Progress
,
The simulations are consistently getting closer to real market behaviour across the statistical measures we care about. The reason this matters: as MVTRX scales to cover every subnet that matters, we'll be running hundreds to thousands of these simulations in parallel - no human team can manually tune that many, and the number only grows as Bittensor does. Internal reports on recent runs are being prepared.


 ExeTRX - Patent Evidence Nearly Complete
,
Close to finalising the compiled evidence of dynamic AI-driven SL/TP levels outperforming static ones - substantive backing for the patent application. The target is to develop this into a new revenue stream, through licensing to external parties and as a premium tool inside MVTRX once the patent process supports release.


 MAYA - Extended Model Fine-Tuning Underway
,
Work underway on extended fine-tuning of MAYA for deeper trading-specific knowledge - sharper planning, more accurate decision-making across subnets and market microstructure, and stronger alignment between MAYA's recommendations and the way the platform actually behaves. Initial investigation underway, with further detail to share as the work progresses.


 CryptoQuay - MinerQuay Upgrade Validated
,
The MinerQuay miner-launch stack has just received a substantial update, validated through external miner testing (the thread Alex and others have been running): deploy miners directly from a GitHub repository, alerting via Discord/Slack/PagerDuty, Python syntax highlighting in the in-platform editor, wallet setup validation before deployment to catch mistakes, real-time CPU and memory metrics during runtime, and a refreshed UI throughout.

Alongside, the marketplace encryption layer has been brought in-house - removing reliance on third-party providers and consolidating control inside MVTRX. Exchange components are also moving in-house to reduce third-party library dependencies, and expansion is underway to extend these tools to serve other subnets.

[2026-06-22T15:34:51.131Z] ΛSSΛSIN [τ, τ]
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1518640420119248927
Hey, @6/. We're currently chasing down an intermittent timeout issue and found a bottleneck in the event loop. It looks like completed coroutine task objects (Task instances) are still hanging around in the internal loop set, holding onto state data for about 128 orderbooks. This keeps the references alive, causing GC pause times to spike from a few ms to tens of ms. Since this GC pause kicks in right in the middle of handle() execution, it stretches the response time and ultimately triggers the timeout. To mitigate or patch this, we need to understand how axon handles task lifecycles and reference clearing under the hood. Would it be possible to get some insights or documentation on the internal implementation of axon regarding this?

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-06-22T15:37:12.920Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1518641014825422938
Will look into this; meanwhile, axon is implemented at bittensor package level, you would need to consult the bittensor module code for details of that implementation.

------------------------------------------------------------

@mvtrx・79  MVTRX 0.5.0 — Exchange groundwork lands 

The biggest push yet on SN-79. Full validator architecture refactor for our upcoming live exchange, with the simulation continuing to run on testnet as the foundation.

Tomorrow we connect testnet simulations to the MVTRX UI alongside a major UI update.

What ships in 0.5.0
Dual-engine validator architecture — the same scoring code now applies to both the simulation we run today and the live MVTRX Exchange that's coming. Exchange-side scaffolding is in place; exchange mode implementation is excluded from this release.
,
Stop-loss, take-profit, and slippage protection on orders. New SLTPAgent example shows the pattern.
,
GenTRX hardening — tamper-evident assignments, broader gradient server reliability, faster scoring loader builds.
,
Substantial codebase consolidation — validator monolith split into focused modules, C++ matching engine reorganised, and more.
,
Faster installs — binary fast paths for g++-14, cmake, and Node.js. Setup time drops from hours to minutes.
,

Miners
You don't need to update for testnet to keep running, but it's strongly recommended. New order options and quality-of-life improvements available only on 0.5.0. See the follow-up message for the full miner-facing breakdown.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

Once testnet confirms everything is working, we'll announce the mainnet deployment timeline. (edited)

[2026-06-24T16:01:41.073Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1519371948436488294
MVTRX 0.5.0 — full details for miners 

New order options
market_order() and limit_order() now accept stop_loss= and take_profit= as signed fractional offsets from the fill price
,
market_order() also accepts max_slippage= to protect against adverse fills
,
The matching engine enforces SL/TP brackets and auto-generates close orders when triggers fire. Resulting trades carry aggressingCloseReason (1=SL, 2=TP) so your onTrade handler can recognise auto-closes
,
New agents/SLTPAgent.py demonstrates the full pattern across BUY/SELL × market/limit
,

Bundled agent improvements
RandomMaker gains a spread param (default 0.01) — handles empty-book / pool-price cases gracefully
,
RandomTaker gains a max_slippage default on every market order
,

No required code changes
Custom agents overriding respond(self, state) continue to work unchanged — the new respond_simulation / respond_exchange dispatch falls back to respond() by default. The bundled examples have been rewritten to use respond_simulation directly as the canonical pattern going forward, but renaming is only required if you want different logic in simulation vs exchange mode (which the public release doesn't run anyway).

GenTRX updates
Tamper-evident assignments — bucket credentials and training window are now bound into the signed body_hash. Your miner verifies automatically, so a MITM on the dendrite path can no longer redirect your training to a malicious bucket.
,
Gradient server reliability work continuing from 0.4.6: better restart behaviour, fewer S3 round-trips per round, round-drift detection from chain to recover cleanly from partial crashes.
,
Scoring loader builds are now bounded by --max-loader-files, so scoring time is more predictable per round.
,
Clean 0.4.6 → 0.5.0 transition — the training regime version is unchanged, so existing checkpoints resume cleanly with no forced warmup cycle.
,

Installation
Run ./install_miner.sh — much faster this release with binary fast paths
,
Dependencies now split: pip install -e . is the lean trading-side install; pip install -e .[gentrx] for full GenTRX. Run scripts handle this automatically.
,

Heads up on scoring
The PnL kappa-lookback unit fix means PnL-component scores will land differently than before. Miners with consistent realized PnL should see those contributions move visibly. This is intended and reflects underlying correctness work.

@mvtrx・79  Miners: Testnet Simulations in the UI 

Mainnet-registered miners can now observe their trading behaviour on testnet - and intervene manually - through the MVTRX UI.

This is the first time miners can step into their own agents' shoes: watch your agent place orders, see the order book react, monitor your positions across subnets, and intervene manually whenever you want.


 Funded for Participation
,
To make participation friction-free, we've funded the coldkeys of registered mainnet miners with a small amount of testnet TAO - enough to register and start interacting with the simulation on testnet.


 How to Get Started
,
Request access at https://mvtrx.exchange/.
,
Connect your mainnet-registered coldkey and hotkey in the UI (polkadotjs, Crucible, Talisman and Subwallet supported).
,
Register your hotkey on testnet if you haven't already - either directly through the UI when connecting hotkey, or via btcli with --subtensor.network test.
,
Start interacting with the simulation.
,


 New Miners Channel
,
A dedicated miners channel in our Discord exists as a place for miners to provide feedback or request support on using the UI. Whatever your experience is like - what works, what's confusing, what's broken, what you wish was different - we want to hear it directly. The simulation phase exists to shape the live exchange, and your feedback drives that.

@mvtrx・79  MVTRX 0.5.1 — Testnet Update

A depth-focused release on top of the 0.5.0 baseline - no major new features, but meaningful work under the hood: a big simulator speedup, a more robust GenTRX mechanism, and further groundwork for the exchange.

Now on testnet.

 Simulator ~2× faster - a sweep of optimisations roughly halves the C++ processing time each step. This is another step towards running many more order books concurrently on the same hardware - more markets, more realistic environments. It also lays groundwork for multi-asset simulation, which we're working toward.

 GenTRX hardening - a round of robustness and fairness work across the subnet mechanism. A single misbehaving miner can no longer disrupt a training round, scoring is fairer to newly-registered miners and more consistent overall, and the gradient server is more resilient with clearer diagnostics when something looks off.

 Exchange groundwork - the GenTRX agent has been reworked to be mode-agnostic, so the same code path serves both today's simulation and the live exchange that's coming. Further scaffolding toward exchange launch, building on the dual-engine architecture from 0.5.0.

Also folded in: validator restart guard, bittensor 10.5.0 upgrade, and reproducible-install tooling.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

Miners — no required action. No protocol or scoring change needs miner code edits, and custom agents continue to work unchanged. The one thing to know: newly-registered miners now build up their GenTRX score gradually over ~22 rounds rather than inheriting their first score immediately. If you're already running 0.5.0 with score history, your EMA is unaffected.

Once all confirmed in testnet, v0.5.1 will be deployed to mainnet (targeting tomorrow).
Shortly thereafter, mainnet simulations will be connected to the UI so that miners can start to interact with and give feedback on the UI in real usage. (edited)
Tuesday, June 30, 2026 at 11:13 PM
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

@mvtrx・79  MVTRX 0.5.3 — Now on Testnet

A big step forward for GenTRX, plus a round of validator performance work - now live on testnet, with mainnet deploy scheduled in ~24 hours.

What's in 0.5.3

 A smarter GenTRX model
The intelligence layer's biggest upgrade yet. The model now understands executions as their own distinct events and can work across markets of wildly different sizes with a single model - making it far more general and capable across different assets.

 Rewarding genuine predictive skill
Scoring now evaluates miners purely on how well they predict what comes next - measured on fresh data that follows their training window. This puts the focus squarely on real, forward-looking market insight, and rewards the models that generalise best.

 Faster, leaner all round
Training runs to a time budget rather than a fixed step count, checkpoints sync via small deltas instead of full re-downloads, and a validator hot-path pass keeps everything responsive under real load.

 Stop-loss & take-profit on market orders
Market orders now support stop-loss and take-profit directly, bringing them in line with limit orders across the trading surface.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

GenTRX miners: this is a breaking update - a separate message with full details and upgrade steps follows shortly. Please read it and make sure you're prepared to upgrade before the mainnet deploy.

Join our Discord for support and to share feedback: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test
Link: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv

[2026-07-08T15:39:47.731Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1524439869999415418
GenTRX Miners — Action Needed for 0.5.3

0.5.3 upgrades the GenTRX model to a new regime (v3). This is a breaking change for GenTRX training - you need to update to keep earning your GenTRX score.

What happens if you don't update
Once the v3 aggregator goes live, a miner still on 0.5.2 can no longer train against the new model - so it produces no GenTRX gradient and earns zero on the GenTRX component, immediately, not a gradual taper.

To be clear on scope: this only affects the GenTRX share of your reward. Your trading rewards (the large majority) keep paying as normal whether or not you update. The GenTRX pool grows as more miners participate, so it's worth keeping.

How to update
The normal flow - no special migration step:


Fetch and check out 0.5.3 (on the test branch for now, since it's testnet-only at this stage - we'll confirm the branch/tag for the mainnet cutover in the deploy notice)
,
Run ./install_miner.sh (or just pip install -e . if your dependencies are unchanged)
,
Restart your miner
,

The checkpoint transition is automatic: on your first assignment after updating, your miner re-downloads the new v3 baseline from the aggregator and picks up from there. There's nothing to hand-migrate.

(Optional tidiness: you can rm checkpoints/GenTRX/\*.pt before restarting to skip a harmless "old checkpoint" log line - not required, an old local checkpoint is handled gracefully either way.)

New defaults worth knowing
A few GenTRX defaults changed with the new regime:


Budget-driven training - training now runs to a time budget (gtx_round_budget_s, default 240s) rather than a fixed step count. gtx_train_steps=0 is the new default (budget mode); set a positive value only if you want to pin the step count for experiments.
,
Top-k default raised from 0.05 → 0.10 (gtx_top_k_frac). The validator can also push per-round top-k guidance regardless of your setting.
,
Sequence length default is now 512.
,
Max gradient size raised to 20MB, accommodating the richer v3 model - handled automatically, nothing to configure.
,

Multi-UID (optional)
If you run several trading agents, one training service can now serve them all against a single in-memory model on one GPU, splitting the round budget across them. Optional and not required - see doc/gentrx/miner_setup.md if you want it.

Update before the mainnet deploy (~24h after testnet) to avoid any gap in your GenTRX scoring. Questions - drop them here or at our Discord and we'll help. (edited)
Thursday, July 9, 2026 at 12:00 AM

What shipped this week

 MVTRX 0.5.3
GenTRX model regime v3 - a smarter, more general model - plus fairer forward-looking scoring, leaner checkpoint sync, and a round of validator performance work. Now live on mainnet. Full details: ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠

 Terminal updates
Further updates and optimisations to the MVTRX Terminal (https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/), with more to come.

Landing early next week

 Hangar - launching
Your agent operations console, built right into MVTRX. Bring your own algorithms or start from an SN79 template, get MAYA's help developing and refining the code, link a GitHub repo as your source, then deploy hosted agents through a guided wizard and manage everything live - logs, metrics, build history and output files. Acquire strategies from the CQ Exchange marketplace, and track per-agent performance. Waiting on final hosting config - fuller detail to follow with the release.

 UI Updates
Shipping alongside Hangar. Led by a big performance overhaul: the app now loads just what you're looking at and streams the rest, so it's up in a second or two and snappy across every mode. Plus a full mobile responsiveness pass, new High / Medium / Lite graphics tiers in Nexus, tier perks laid out clearly on your profile, and steadier live-data connections throughout.

Where we're headed

 Localnet exchange
Pushed back slightly as we focused on getting 0.5.3 and Hangar right this week - targeting next week.

⇄ SWAP mainnet
Launch date to be announced soon - also targeting next week.

 Dashboard
Progressing well, targeting 1-2 weeks.

 MVTRX API + SDKs
A REST + WebSocket interface to the exchange: live market data (depth, trades, candles, tickers), full account and order management, and real-time streams. SDKs for Python, JavaScript, Rust, Go and C++, plus a signing proxy for any other language. It'll let miners and users automate trading, connect agents and bots straight into SN79, and build their own tooling, analytics and dashboards. Targeting 2-3 weeks.

[2026-07-13T16:19:44.362Z] Mykola
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1526261861526540448
i think it's difficult to block him with that way alone, because his real income is the few top-rank uids , not low performance uids.

i just asked an AI about this, not sure it would work, but please have a look:

Suggestion: cap how much any single counterparty can contribute to a miner's kappa.

Every trade already carries maker + taker agent ids (Ma/Ta), so the validator can count, per miner, what share of their realized-PnL observations comes from each counterparty uid. Then one rule in scoring: obs from a single counterparty count toward your kappa only up to X% (e.g. ~25%) of your window volume — the excess is simply dropped, same as the existing zero-round drop.

Why it hits only wash trading: his top uids' kappa is built almost entirely on fills against his own cluster. With the cap, those obs stop counting — to score he'd have to trade against counterparties he doesn't control, i.e. take real market risk, which is the whole point of the subnet. Honest miners are unaffected: on books with 250+ agents nobody organically gets most fills from one specific uid (on thin books the cap can scale with that counterparty's share of the book's total volume, so trading with a dominant market maker stays safe).

And it's cheap: O(trades) counting on data the validator already processes every tick. No IP/coldkey rules, no banning anyone — just stop paying for self-dealt fills, and the whole farm (including the reg-fee wall) stops being worth the money.


for now, let's first block this guy and his coldkeys manually, if it's obvious that he is using wash trading - 38.127.44.98.

[2026-07-13T16:38:20.034Z] s_xander
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1526266540993806536
Nice idea but it won't actually catch him, for three reasons:


His fills are already fanned out - each of his maker uids trades against ~60 different counterparties, so the biggest single one is ~3% of its volume, nowhere near a 25% cap. The concentration you're capping doesn't exist.
,
He has ~100 uids to spread across. Any per-counterparty cap just makes him fan wider - it basically rewards running more sybils, not fewer.
,
It only catches a lazy 2-uid washer. A real cluster this size stays under any per-counterparty limit by design.
,

The numbers are checkable - count each maker uid's fills per counterparty and you'll see the spread yourself.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-07-13T17:02:37.233Z] Mykola
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1526272652929532015
Good point, response from AI again.  

The two invariants fanning cannot hide

Total cluster-internal volume. Spread wash across 60 internal counterparties and each pair is 3% — but the sum still lands inside his own cluster. That's arithmetic, not behavior: wash volume must have him on both sides, so it can never leave the cluster. An honest miner in an anonymous CLOB cannot choose its counterparties — its fill mix converges to each counterparty-group's share of the book's volume. So the test isn't "concentration per uid," it's: fraction of your matched volume against counterparty-set S vs. S's share of total market volume. If his cluster is 40% of market volume, honest miners fill ~40% against it; his uids fill 70–90% internal. To evade he must dilute internal volume down to the null — at which point the wash volume is too small to manufacture anything. Diluting the signal = losing the exploit. Same knob.
,

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-07-13T17:02:41.029Z] Mykola
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1526272668851114106
One-directional realized-PnL flow — the structural bind. The scheme's whole purpose is warehouse+wash: winner uids realize only wins, puppets eat the other side. So realized PnL along internal edges flows one way, into the winners, by construction. Here's the trap: to fake bidirectional flow, his winners would have to realize losses — which destroys the very kappa the scheme exists to manufacture. He cannot randomize this away. Fanning doesn't help either: 100 small puppet→winner trickles are individually tiny, but a sign-consistency test across thousands of fills is brutally powerful, and honest miners can't trip it — with anonymous matching you have no way to be systematically profitable against specific counterparties. Persistent signed flow = information about your counterparty = collusion, full stop.
,

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-07-13T17:02:49.746Z] Mykola
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1526272705412730921
The mechanism
Validator builds a collusion graph from the fills it already processes: edges weighted by (a) internal-volume excess over the null and (b) PnL-flow sign-consistency.
Community detection (Louvain-style) on that graph. No IP, no coldkeys — the cluster identifies itself by the geometry of its own fills, and here's the inversion s_xander should like: more sybils make the community denser and easier to detect. His scale becomes his liability instead of his shield.
Scoring rule: kappa obs earned against your own detected community count only up to that community's market-share null (+margin); the excess is dropped. No bans, no censorship — self-dealt fills just stop paying.

Why honest miners are safe
Honest counterparty mix ≈ market shares (can't choose who fills you) → test 1 never fires.
No counterparty knowledge at order time → no persistent signed flow → test 2 never fires.
Multi-uid operators running independent agents: mutual matches sit at the null rate and PnL between own uids is symmetric noise — no community forms. Only coordinated uids cluster. (edited)

@mvtrx・79  Status Update

What's Live Now

⇄ MVTRX SWAP on localnet
The mainnet launch date is pending final coordination with the Hangar and localnet exchange work - we'll announce it as soon as possible.

 GenTRX
0.5.3's updates are live on mainnet, and the new model continues training. More refinements and improvements are on the way.

 MVTRX Terminal
Optimisations and improvements ship on an ongoing basis at https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/. Latest (v0.3.0): duration-format and decimals fixes, CSV download of trades and the order book, a book/plot-type selector in fullscreen, and a redesigned price-plot animation, loading, and sidebar agent selector.

 0.5.3 - deployed on mainnet & testnet
The GenTRX model update plus validator performance improvements are running live - simulations now average ~5.5 real-world hours per simulated hour.

In Progress This Week

 0.5.4 - this week
Targeted measures to address the farming behaviour recently identified on the network, plus exchange-prep and boot-resilience work under the hood. A proper list of updates to follow shortly.

 UI Update +  Hangar - opening this week
Both are in final testing. The UI update is essentially there; the Hangar is in the last stretch of validation and we're holding it until it's fully solid - likely today, possibly rolling into tomorrow as we finalise. Announcement the moment they go live.

 Exchange Localnet
Expected to be deployed with final internal testing completed this week, opening up either later this week or early next.

 The Dashboard Vision
The one-stop shop for all your dTAO trading continues to progress - expected in 1-2 weeks.

 MVTRX API
A public, Binance-style trading API in development and testing - letting external traders and bots connect to the exchange programmatically, with scoped API keys, order and market-data endpoints, and multi-language SDK support (Python, Rust, JS). The foundation for third-party tools and automated strategies trading through MVTRX. Targeting 2-3 weeks.

The AI Side - Compounding Progress

 Simulation Tuning - the tuning process continues, steady progress toward full data-driven automatic tunability.

 ExeTRX - patent evidence collection is near completion ahead of submission.

 MAYA - fine-tuned models and Voice Mode expected in 2-3 weeks.

Building the Ecosystem
Beyond the code, we're investing in the foundations for long-term growth:

 Growing the team - two new hires joining this month, with more emphasis going into community building and our MVTRX server integration with CryptoQuay®.

 Academic collaboration - discussions are ongoing with professors and researchers we connected with at Bachelier, deepening the research partnerships behind the platform.

 Conferences ahead - we're targeting participation at Exploit Montreal (September) and several conferences in Chicago (October), the latter especially relevant for GenTRX.

 Getting the word out - new brochures, posters, and website updates in the works as we broaden our reach.

 Tying It Together
The pieces are converging. GenTRX keeps getting smarter, the platform keeps getting faster, the Hangar opens the door for anyone to build and run agents, and the exchange groundwork is falling into place step by step. Every release moves us closer to the initial goal: MVTRX as the complete home for dTAO trading, where you can build, analyse, and act all in one place.

And that's just the starting point. The same principles - agent-based market simulation, decentralised incentivisation of trading behaviour, and AI-driven tooling - are built to extend beyond dTAO to other markets in time. dTAO is where we prove it; the vision is much bigger.

We'll keep you posted as each piece lands. Follow along on X:

@mvtrx・79  

MVTRX 0.5.4 — Sharper Rewards + New Tools
,
Now deployed to testnet and mainnet. This release sharpens how rewards recognise genuine performance, ships a new opt-in miner anyone can run, and continues the validator and exchange groundwork.

 Sharper reward concentration
Scoring now concentrates emission more decisively on top performers - a steeper payout curve that puts more weight on genuine skill, with a smooth taper on the lower half of active scores that keeps the incentive squarely on quality. It's a gentle taper, not a cliff: an improving newcomer clears it comfortably within the immunity window. Purely a function of the score distribution - no synthetic or ad-hoc rules based on IP, wallet, or counterparty, fully grounded in realistic market dynamics.  We will be monitoring and make further adjustments if seen to be necessary.

 An example arbitrage miner agent
0.5.4 includes a new opt-in example agent (ArbitrageAgent.py) that competes for mispriced orders - crossing when the book drifts away from fair value. Beyond being a great way to put fast, well-placed execution to work, it's a miner-driven answer to a cross-UID reward-farming tactic: the more honest arbitrageurs compete for off-market orders, the more those trades get taken first - so the tactic pays less and the market stays efficient. Speed is the whole game: the fastest responder wins a contested trade, so optimised, co-located setups have the edge. Entirely optional - a new opportunity for those who want it, with nothing changing for miners who don't.

 Validator & exchange groundwork
The scoring engine now runs as a dedicated, parity-verified process for faster, smoother reward cycles, alongside boot-resilience improvements and continued exchange-integration work.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79

Miners — fully backwards-compatible, no action required. No code changes needed. The arbitrage agent is an optional example, not a requirement - but it's the miner-driven way to compete away the cross-UID reward-farming tactic we've identified.
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79

@mvtrx・79  The Hangar is Open 

We've opened the Hangar - your agent operations console, built right into MVTRX. Everything you need to build, deploy, and run trading agents on SN79, in one place.


 What the Hangar does
,
 Bring your own, or start from a template
Upload your existing algorithms to manage and deploy, or start from one of our SN79 templates.

 MAYA assists throughout
Use MAYA to help develop and refine your agent's code at any stage - from a plain-language prompt to in-place edits with a review-and-refine loop.

 Develop in GitHub
Link a GitHub repo as your agent's source and sync it straight into the Hangar.

 Deploy & manage, live
Launch hosted agents through a guided wizard, then manage everything in real time: start/stop/restart, live logs, metrics, build history, output files, and shareable read-only links.

 Acquire strategies
Browse the marketplace and acquire agent strategies to run as your own - we have listed RevEngAgent to acquire and deploy, so you can try the full flow end to end. (The marketplace contract currently runs on testnet.)

 Track performance
Per-agent stats for incentive, score, PnL, KAPPA3, and alpha earned - scoped to your chosen network, so you can see exactly how your agents are doing.

 Make it yours
The Hangar plugs into the same customizable layout system as the rest of MVTRX - dock, pop out, and arrange panels to suit how you work.


 Your code and wallets, protected
,
We know your strategies and keys are sensitive. The Hangar is built around that:


Your strategy code stays private. Private drafts are encrypted at rest with a key derived from your own wallet, and any strategy content on the marketplace is encrypted and owner-gated - only the owner can decrypt it.
,
You authorise wallet actions yourself. Marketplace purchases and wallet funding are signed by you in your own wallet, and every action is scoped to your account.
,
Uploaded keys are handled securely. To run a hosted agent, you provide its hotkey - never your coldkey, which stays with you. Uploaded hotkeys are sent over TLS and stored in HashiCorp Vault, which encrypts them at rest; only the public address is kept in our database, never the secret. Best practice still applies: use a dedicated hotkey for deployment, funded only as needed.
,
You choose what's visible. Nothing about your agents is shared or advertised unless you explicitly opt in.
,

To request testing access: DM us or post in the MVTRX Discord. Because spots are limited, let us know a little about what you'd like to test or why you'd be a good fit for the group.

[2026-07-15T21:13:35.931Z] Alex
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1527060589417857155
With this approach, farming becomes even more profitable, because the top-ranked agents now receive an even larger share of the rewards.

At the same time, this approach hits stable mid-tier agents in the top 50 quite hard — agents that deliver consistent results over several days rather than just explosive growth within the scoring window.

Good, stable agents tend to remain around the middle of the ranking, showing steady, break-even or moderately profitable performance without sharp spikes or sudden crashes. Under the new system, it becomes more profitable to generate explosive growth during the observation window, collect the larger reward, and then simply register a new agent.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-07-15T21:50:50.050Z] Alex
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1527069959992250429
In the end, this makes things worse for everyone except the very person you were trying to stop, assuming his top-ranking agents got there through farming.

Top agents can earn several TAO per day. Even if his supporting agents get deregistered after a day, the registration cost is still several times lower than what the top agents earn in that same day.

So as an anti-farming measure, this update is essentially pointless.

Concrete numbers behind Alex's point - a 30-min wall time (just my sample window — likely longer). live snapshot of the current top:

Ranks 1–9 right now: zero round-trips, zero orders placed, several literally frozen. No instructions sent this window at all. They hold the top purely on stale kappa observations that haven't aged out of the 3-sim-hour scoring window yet - that's ~17h of wall time riding a rank while doing nothing.

The couple of active ones near the top: 100% taker, 3–5% win rate, every single book negative, bleeding fees. That's not performance - it's deliberately loading up stuck/negative inventory to manufacture round-trip observations and pump kappa density.

So the top is built on: pump kappa hard in-window → stop trading → coast at the top for ~17h → re-pump. The new soft floor + top-concentration doesn't touch any of it - a pumped agent parks comfortably above the median and rides it out. The
floor only zeroes the honest steady miners below the median, i.e. exactly the people you didn't mean to hit.

An "anti-farm" change that leaves pump-and-park untouched while nuking consistent mid-tier miners isn't an anti-farm change. (edited)

[2026-07-16T08:01:55.499Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1527223746031521832
Thanks @Alex  @s_xander @James  @Rosty , this is careful analysis and worth engaging properly. Let me set out what each piece of 0.5.4 is for, and address the specific patterns you have flagged.

The arbitrage agent is the anti-collusion lever. It is an opt-in example anyone can run that competes for the mispriced, off-market orders the cross-UID tactic relies on: the more honest arbitrageurs take those trades first, the less it pays. On the economics, you are right that registration cost is trivial against a top agent's daily earnings, so cost alone deters nothing, and that is exactly why the deterrent is removing the profit at its source rather than registration cost or the reward curve.

The concentration and floor are a separate, incentive-quality change, not the anti-farm lever. On a flat curve the reward gap between a genuinely skilled miner and a merely-adequate one is small, so there is little incentive to improve and it is cheap to run many mediocre agents that each skim a slice. Concentrating the curve widens the payoff for skill and stops paying for mere participation. It is purely distributional and a gentle taper rather than a cliff, so an improving miner clears it within the immunity window, and we will ease it if it turns out to be penalizing genuine miners with real trading skill. It is not aimed at the top and will not by itself remove a farmed top agent, that is the arbitrageur's job; it does cut the extra emission the scheme's low-scoring support agents pick up, though that is only a small part of the take.

The behaviours you are describing, an agent that pumps then sits idle, one that trades constantly at 100% taker near breakeven to manufacture round-trips, or one that generates an explosive in-window burst, collects, and re-registers a fresh agent, share a single root: the score rewards risk-adjusted consistency, currently rewards realized profit only weakly, and does not penalize going idle. That is pre-existing. The window and the absence of inactivity decay exist to support lower-frequency strategies, and kappa is deliberately a measure of profit quality rather than profit magnitude. 0.5.4 targets the cross-UID collusion and left that behaviour alone, so we agree it is untouched.

It is possible this is a real gap, but it needs further analysis to confirm, and that analysis is currently confounded by the farm itself: while the wash tactic is active it is hard to separate genuine coasting from farm-driven scores. Two things frame it. First, all of these still require earning the favorable result in the first place; once the wash is competed away by arbitrageurs, doing so takes genuine, well-timed trading rather than collusion, so removing the wash is the first-order answer, and it also cleans the data enough to judge whether any coasting remains. Second, the open questions are whether a short or merely-consistent burst is scored too highly relative to sustained, genuinely profitable trading, and whether the collect-and-re-register churn actually pays. If the analysis says yes, a change lands in a following update. (edited)

[2026-07-19T21:15:31.299Z] s_xander
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1528510624768856204
The mistake is assuming one UID equals one independent economic actor. The subnet may detect self-crossing inside a single UID, but it does not identify or penalize coordinated trading across separate UIDs/accounts. To the validator, one UID simply looks like external liquidity for another, while both produce valid exchange fills.

After the target UID builds enough in-window kappa, it stops trading and retains the score because activity decay is disabled. Right now ranks #0–#5 have produced zero fills over the last 60 wall minutes, yet still hold kappaN around 0.74–0.75.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-07-19T21:26:53.968Z] NinjaWolves

[2026-07-19T22:09:26.250Z] s_xander
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1528524193136902215
They don't need adjacent queue positions or synchronized submissions. If two UIDs are coordinated, UID A can leave a limit order resting at a known price, and UID B can later submit a marketable order sized and priced to reach it. The matching engine does not care when those two orders were submitted.

They do not even need separate validator cycles. Miners are queried in parallel from the same published state, and their responses are collected within the configured response window — 3 seconds. A coordinated backend can return UID A's maker instruction earlier and UID B's crossing instruction later. Both responses receive the same simulator occurrence timestamp and can execute within one simulation step before the next state is published. Execution remains sequential inside the matching engine, but both actions belong to the same validator cycle.

The current simulator STP path is scoped to one agent/account: it prevents a UID from matching its own resting order, but it does not link distinct agent IDs. At the exchange layer, this appears as an ordinary maker/taker fill between two participants. Whether particular UIDs are coordinated is a separate attribution question; the mechanism itself is straightforward.

If you're actually building trading agents here, I'm honestly surprised this needs explaining. This is basic order-book mechanics.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-07-20T16:06:11.511Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1528795167241273415
Thanks @NinjaWolves @s_xander @Rosty  @James  @jaoejxnc , genuinely useful thread, and credit to those tracking the numbers.

On the mitigation: encouraging. The 38.127.44.98 cluster fell from ~101 UIDs to ~56 and off the top-10, matching what we see on our side. As @s_xander says, correlation isn't proof, so we won't call the farm 'gone', but it's a real move in the right direction. Your read matches ours: the concern now is a small concentrated set, most miners are clearly heads-down improving their agents.

The arbitrage path is working as designed: mispriced, off-market orders are captured by a distributed pool of takers rather than funnelled to one recipient. A controlled wash needs a single colluding winner, so spread capture makes the pump pay less.

What still warrants work is what's raised here: high, steady consistency on very low volume with near-zero net profit. KAPPA3 is a risk-adjusted measure of a UID's own round-trip returns, so steady, low-drawdown trading is rewarded, and it should be, consistently not losing money is a genuine signal. The gap is that it is scale-independent: a small steady edge on very low volume can score as high as genuinely profitable trading on real volume.

@s_xander on pump-and-coast: pre-existing, not created by the reward change. A score still has to be earned, KAPPA3 only accrues from real in-window trading, so it is not free. Two separate gaps sit on top of that: the scale-independence above (breakeven consistency on tiny volume ranking too high), and, distinctly, that holding a score once set does not require ongoing trading, so a UID can spike and then sit quiet for the scoring interval. Both are in the review.

@James  on the churn: yes, fresh, still-immune hotkeys rotating in is consistent with rising registration cost. Registration timing and the immunity window are on the review list.

The matcher can't block coordination across separate UIDs, by design it only ever sees a single UID's own orders, so the self-trade check can't catch two accounts working together. That makes it an analysis problem, not a matching one. The pump, then idle, then rotate-a-fresh-UID cycle you're describing is those two gaps combined, a held score plus fresh-UID churn, so the leaderboard showing it is confirmation.

@jaoejxnc  on price manipulation: book prices form around a fundamental seeded from real market data, and the background trading population tends to stabilize the market, an aggressive push is met by liquidity that trades against it and pulls price back toward fundamentals, so the mover pays impact and fees for a move that decays under them. KAPPA3 then scores a miner's own realized round-trip profit, not the price level, so a lone push doesn't raise a score by itself. What can pay is the coordinated version, one UID moves, another captures, which is the cross-UID case above.

@Rosty  on the reward curve: true that concentrating payout raises the value of holding a top slot, that trade-off is also part of the review as we stated previously.

Where we're heading: we think the durable answer is on the scoring side, making the score track ongoing, genuinely profitable activity at real volume rather than a one-off snapshot that can be parked on, covering both whether a spike was earned and whether it should be holdable while idle. We expect conclusive results and a decision on the next refinement within about a week.

Keep the concrete cases coming.

@6/. how to improve kappa score?

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-07-24T23:06:03.436Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1530350381295599737
Similarly to Sharpe Ratio, Kappa-3 betters with better risk managed decisions. Avoid having too few trades, but avoid having too many (to avoid excessive trx costs), also pay attention to "MTR" (maker taker ratio), which pays off similarly to what happens in futures markets against the spot. There are multiple ways to take advantage of arbitrage opportunities, with trend detection and mean-reversion. The idea with Kappa-3 is that you need to get the maximal profit, but with least risk at the same time, so your decisions to the right direction matter a lot.

[2026-07-25T10:02:14.250Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1530515514458243223
There is Kappa-3 that matters the most, while we also give some explicit weight on PnL. One more thing: We used Sharpe Ratio before, which is the "norm" in financial markets. However, Sharpe "penalizes" on the upside. That is, Sharpe benefits those with very consistent pattern and behavior, leading to a problem that one does not necessarily even want to get a better PNL. This is one of its weak-points. Kappa-3 "solves" that by letting the good side run, while penalizing on the downside. So yes, PNL is at the centre of the action, but with risk managed decisions.

Thanks for the detailed reports. We've evaluated these cases and the next update addresses them on four fronts:


Kappa-3 normalization update: adjusted in response to recent trading patterns so the risk-adjusted metric more directly rewards consistent, genuinely profitable performance.
,
Track-record smoothing: standing builds from sustained performance, so a single strong window no longer tops the board.
,
Flatter payout curve: the top few UIDs no longer capture an outsized share; honest mid-tier miners are rewarded more fairly.
,
Market-structure fix: correcting the persistent uptrend that let large directional positions score highest (the root of the "high-risk agent scores best" cases).
,

On the coordinated-trading reports: we're analysing counterparty-level flow directly. If it proves to be an active winning strategy, we'll consider further scoring adjustments.

[2026-07-28T16:08:33.359Z] 6/.

@mvtrx・79  

MVTRX 0.5.5 — Testnet
,
Now on testnet, with mainnet following ~24 hours later. This release refines how miner performance is measured and rewarded, informed by observing 0.5.4 on mainnet, alongside operational hardening. Nothing changes about what miners submit or how they trade - only how existing performance is scored.

What's in 0.5.5

 Rewarding sustained skill over single windows
A miner's trading score now carries a track record: performance is smoothed across the assessment window, so standing reflects consistent results over time rather than one strong window. A newcomer still ramps up quickly, but holding a high position now means performing well repeatedly - the way real allocators judge a track record, not a single period's P&L.

 A refined risk-adjusted measure
Informed by the latest mainnet data, we've refined the KAPPA3 risk-adjusted-return metric so that it now behaves monotonically: a better risk-adjusted return can never score worse than a poorer one. The score is now tightly aligned with what a risk-adjusted measure is designed to reward - genuine, well-managed performance.

 Better-balanced reward distribution
The payout curve is tuned so rewards reach further down the field and the competent middle is recognised more proportionally, rather than concentrating so heavily in the top few. Competing for the top is still clearly worth it; placing well outside it now counts for more than it did.

 Operational hardening
Exchange checkpoint-restore resilience, steadier state persistence so scoring rounds stay smooth, refined engine dynamics, and a build-memory safeguard for validators.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

Miners: there's an important change for GenTRX training miners in particular - a separate details message follows shortly. Please read it before the mainnet deploy.
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

[2026-07-28T16:08:56.446Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1531694961953607822
0.5.5 — Details for Miners

A rundown of what 0.5.5 means for you. The changes are all on the scoring side - nothing changes about what you submit or how you trade, and no changes to your agent code are required.

How to update
Standard flow - fetch and check out 0.5.5 (on the test branch for now; we'll confirm the branch/tag for the mainnet cutover in the deploy notice), run ./install_miner.sh, and restart.

 What's changed in scoring

All three changes act only on how existing performance is scored:


Track record smoothing. Your trading score now carries a track record via a smoothing average over the assessment window (half-life = the 3h KAPPA3 window, in sim-time). One strong window converts into standing gradually, and holding a high position means performing consistently. New miners still ramp up quickly - the smoothing is age-annealed, so you track your live performance inside the immunity window and settle into the track-record average as your history builds. A deregistered slot resets, so a re-registered miner starts fresh with full newcomer protection.
,
Refined KAPPA3. Informed by the latest mainnet data, the risk-adjusted-return metric now runs every record through a single downside-aware formula, so it more cleanly reflects the risk-return tradeoff. Loss-bearing books behave as before under the standard path.
,
Rebalanced payout curve. The distribution curve is reverted to pre-0.5.4 state - the top-5 share moves from roughly 51% back to roughly 33%, rewarding the competent middle of the field more proportionally while keeping a strong gradient toward the top. The soft floor introduced in 0.5.4 stays on, keeping the incentive weighted toward quality.
,

 Note for GenTRX training miners

[2026-07-31T12:54:03.999Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1532733083873181806
@mvtrx・79  New-Miner Ramp-Up Refinement

Thanks to those who raised how new miners ramp up under 0.5.5. A newcomer could reach a strong KAPPA3 quickly while its overall score climbed much more slowly, leaving it ranked below its actual performance for much of its immunity window.

What changed
A new miner's track-record standing built up from zero, so it only gradually caught up to the performance its KAPPA3 already reflected. Standing now takes up a new miner's real score as soon as it clears the initial assessment window, instead of averaging up from zero. Strong newcomers reach a matching rank much sooner, comfortably inside their immunity window.

Miners currently in immunity
We've also re-based every miner currently in immunity so its standing immediately reflects its real KAPPA3, rather than leaving it to wait out the slow climb. If you have a strong miner in its immunity window, you should see its ranking correct within the next scoring cycle.

What to expect on incentive
Your standing (the trading score) updates right away. On-chain incentive and rank follow more gradually, over the next few hours rather than instantly: the weight that drives incentive smooths in over time, is pushed to chain once per tempo, and then accrues on chain across several epochs.

What this means for miners
Nothing to do on your side: this is a validator-side scoring change, with no agent or setup changes. The scoring path for established miners is unchanged, and nothing changes about what earns score: sustained, above-median market-making quality is still what counts.

This refines the age-annealed smoothing described in the 0.5.5 miner notes: ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠

[2026-08-03T10:06:40.534Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1533785546340569181
Thanks Mykola, and I understand the frustration. We tracked the flagged agents over time, scanned every agent across the full period since the last update, and specifically checked them for the ways an agent could earn without providing real liquidity.

They come up clean: no self-trading, flat inventory (they capture spread rather than ride a position), and a thin per-trade edge spread across many thousands of roundtrips. That is textbook market-making, not extraction. The Kappa3 Score 0 / Trading Score 0 you and Adrian saw was a momentary reading between trade bursts, and the flat-roundtrip stretch and kappa collapse in the charts are the score correctly letting go of stale activity: an agent earns while its recent trades are still inside the assessment window, and the score comes down as those trades age out. Nobody earned above what their in-window trades justified, and nobody rode a stale score indefinitely.

If you can share evidence pointing to genuinely exploitative behaviour, we'll certainly reopen this and evaluate it. On the data we have, these are legitimate providers.

On bans, we don't ban coldkeys or hotkeys as a matter of principle. We judge agents by the liquidity they provide, not by trying to work out who is behind them, which is unprovable anyway and just leads to whack-a-mole. Everything is handled through the incentive mechanism itself, so anything genuinely undesirable stops being rewarded for everyone.

And to be clear: if you build an agent that provides that kind of liquidity, that isn't defecting, it is exactly what the mechanism rewards. Good makers, simple or not, are a win for the market.

There are genuine issues we have found and are addressing, though: new miners taking too long to reach their real score during immunity, and cases where similar-performing miners end up rewarded unevenly. Both come from the same lag in how a new miner's score builds, and a fix for it is shipping this week, with further responsiveness improvements to follow.

@mvtrx・79  Status Update

The localnet exchange is in final comprehensive testing, the scoring work went deeper than planned and got better for it, and the surfaces that sit on top of the exchange are queued right behind it.

What's Live Now

 MVTRX UI
Live at https://mvtrx.exchange/: the interface itself, enabling to observe and interact with mainnet simulations and observe mainnet trading activity. This cycle's updates are exchange-facing and appear alongside the exchange launch, with a larger overhaul in the works behind them.

 The Hangar
Still open for testing: build, deploy, and run trading agents end to end, right inside MVTRX. Any SN79 mainnet miner can apply for testing access with free credits - just DM us or post in the MVTRX Discord.

⇄ MVTRX SWAP on localnet
Live and in use on localnet, with the mainnet opening lined up behind the exchange launch.

 MVTRX Terminal
https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/ continues as the one-stop view of SN79 activity. Upgrades and improvements continue.

In Progress This Week

 Exchange Localnet
The final acceptance run is in progress. This took longer than last week's note suggested, for two reasons. Focus shifted to the incentive landscape on mainnet and the scoring updates that came with it, and the acceptance testing itself was widened and sharpened, taking the exchange from working to polished.

⇄ MVTRX SWAP on mainnet
Still pending testing on the mainnet seeded chain. That testing has started internally and follows more broadly immediately at the exchange launch.

 Scoring
A minor update is expected this week, refining some newcomer protections and the distinguishment of similar performance. Behind it, a deeper investigation and the planning of a more comprehensive revision are underway, prepared carefully against sufficient data rather than rushed into place.

 MVTRX API
Testing finalisation is pending the localnet exchange. That is deliberate rather than a delay: the localnet exchange provides the complete surface on which to verify all API functionality.

 The Dashboard
Continues to be developed further alongside the UI overhaul. The prototype is prepared and needs styling, feedback and testing before it is ready to show.

The AI Side - Compounding Progress

 Simulation Tuning - ongoing, with steady improvements to both the methodology and the outcomes it produces.

 GenTRX - being monitored and evaluated, and shifting further back into focus once the localnet exchange lands.

 MAYA - the models process is prepared and awaiting the right timing to proceed with training and hosting, which follows full testing under the exchange.

Building the Ecosystem

Beyond the code, the foundations for long-term growth keep moving:

 Growing the team - interviewing and onboarding across UI/UX and additional exchange capabilities, alongside continued community building and our MVTRX server integration with CryptoQuay®.

 Academic collaboration - discussions continue with the professors and researchers we connected with at Bachelier.

 Conferences ahead - targeting Exploit Montreal (September) and several conferences in Chicago (October).

 Getting the word out - brochures, posters, and website updates continue as we broaden our reach.

 On the Horizon

 Multi-asset simulation - running simulations that model many statistically distinct underlying assets at once, which the automated tuning process is being scaled to calibrate across.

 Derived products - reaching toward instruments like options, first in simulation and then on the exchange.

 Tying It Together
Most of this week's work sits behind one thing, and that is by design: the localnet exchange is the surface the API, SWAP, and much of the UI are proven on, and proving them there is what lets each of them arrive complete. The scoring work is the other half of the picture, and it applies to the exchange just as much: the updates target accuracy, fairness, and properly incentivised market quality under exchange conditions, not only in simulation. Every step still moves toward the same goal: MVTRX as the complete home for dTAO trading, where you can build, analyse, and act all in one place. And it's just the starting point - dTAO is where we prove it; the vision is much bigger.

@mvtrx・79  Release 0.5.5 - Hotfix 2

Just deployed to testnet and mainnet:

 Newcomer standing
Standing is a track record rather than a snapshot, so two miners on the same current kappa are separated by their history: a level held consistently reads at that level, a fresh spike reads below it, and a decline from higher still reads above it. A miner's track record now seeds from its first genuine score, so a strong new miner carries its real standing from the start instead of building it up across its immunity window, while established miners are unchanged.

 Miner docs
MTR is now populated on the state updates miners receive. The miner documentation has been reviewed and aligned with the latest behaviour.

 Larger scoring revisions remain under evaluation
This work is being done carefully, alongside the finalization of the localnet exchange. We are holding these updates until they are fully and provably verified to improve miner and market quality without introducing new potential issues.

Miners: Backwards compatible, but recommended to pull the latest in order to see the populated MTR field in state updates.

Code: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79

[2026-08-07T15:40:34.264Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1535311701140832336
@Alex you've got the mechanism right: newcomers now seed at their real current score (a recent fix), while established standings are smoothed over their history, so a fading miner slides down slowly rather than dropping at once. We're reviewing that smoothing so standings track current performance faster.

On uid 82: yes, it's resting maker orders across the books that incoming flow fills. But large maker volume isn't automatically genuine liquidity. Concentrated or coordinated counterparty flow (a handful of uids trading heavily into each other) doesn't reflect broad market-making, and we're refining scoring to reward genuinely diverse two-sided liquidity. So that kind of approach won't rank the way it does today, and it isn't something worth building toward.

Checked uid 67. Its current scores are genuinely good (trading score ~0.57, active across all 128 books), so nothing's wrong on its side. What you're seeing is the standing: reward is driven by a smoothed average of your score over time, not the instantaneous value, and that average is still catching up to the recent improvement. Early in a run especially, it lags. If the performance holds, the standing and reward will climb, just not instantly. This is the same smoothing behaviour raised above, and it's what we're reviewing.

[2026-08-11T22:39:50.889Z] Antonio
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1536866767136366593
hey  @6/. 
 I think I found a scoring bug around miner deregistration, wanted to flag it before opening an issue.

In taos/im/utils/kappa.py, inside kappa_3() (around line 86), the fingerprint cache lookup happens before the if uid in deregistered_uids check. So the dereg guard gets skipped whenever the cache hits.

That matters on a UID replacement. handle_deregistration() zeroes scores[uid] right away, but realized_pnl_history[uid] isn't cleared until apply_resets → reset_agent_histories runs, and that waits on the simulator's RDRA notice. In that gap the new miner hasn't traded yet, so its pnl history is byte-identical to the old occupant's → fingerprint matches → it gets handed the deregistered miner's cached kappa, and the guard never runs.

Practical effect: a brand new UID starts building its score EMA off someone else's kappa before placing a single trade. It corrects itself once the reset lands or the first fill changes the fingerprint, so normally it's just a couple of rounds — but it'd stay stuck if RDRA notices are ever delayed or erroring. Might be worth checking whether you're seeing any Failed to Reset Agent alerts.

Fix seems simple — move the deregistered_uids check above the cache lookup, and evict cache[uid] on reset. Happy to open a PR if useful.

One thing I'm less sure about: neuron.moving_average_alpha defaults to 0.008298755, which is about an 83-round half-life on self.scores — roughly 10 min of wall clock at current cadence. Is that the intended speed? I originally thought new miners were ramping too fast, but if 83 rounds is by design then that part is expected and only the cache thing above is an actual bug.

@mvtrx・79  The Exchange Is Live: First Iteration, on a Mainnet-Seeded Chain 

The first iteration of the real MVTRX exchange is online, trading on a localnet subtensor seeded from live mainnet. Real market structure, real curve maths, real prices, but with test funds.


 The Localnet Exchange
,
The engine that has been running our market simulations is now running the exchange itself. Not a venue built to resemble the simulator: one machine in two modes. Everything we have learned simulating markets is what you are about to trade on.

And it trades like the real thing because underneath it is the real thing. Your order meets a live limit order book, matched off chain at exchange speed. Buys and sells fill against the book and the AMM together. Every price you see comes from live mainnet reserves, held continuously in step, so this market has mainnet's shape rather than a synthetic one. Settlement lands on chain, co-signed by your proxy wallet, which step 7 sets up.

First iteration, and everything load-bearing is already standing: the book, the matching, the settlement, and the AMM alongside it.


⇄ SWAP
,
SWAP is a separate rail from the exchange, and this is the environment it has been waiting for before going to mainnet: a chain that behaves like mainnet, but where a mistake costs nothing. Stake, unstake and move run through real subnet reserves, the real constant-product curve and the real swap fee, signed with your own coldkeys.

Please try to break it. This is the comprehensive verification SWAP has to pass before it opens on mainnet, and we want as many hands on it as we can get. Stake into a subnet, unstake, move between subnets, try sizes that look wrong, do the things you would never risk with real TAO. Then tell us what you find in Discord.

Our own numbers already line up: a stake on the fork returned alpha matching the curve to within a fraction of a percent. What the rail needs now is other people testing it, and getting there is quick: a coldkey and the faucet, steps 1 to 4 below. No subnet registration, no proxy, nothing else.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-08-13T14:03:36.705Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1537461627723587604
 The chain underneath
A Bittensor fork whose genesis is a snapshot of live mainnet, so every subnet on it opens with real reserves and real prices, and those prices are then held in step with live mainnet, reconciled whenever they drift past roughly a tenth of a percent. Worth being precise about the rest, since simulation accuracy is a large part of what we do: mainnet blocks do not flow into the fork, so there is no outside order flow, and block production is local rather than driven by mainnet blocks. That puts it closer to a backtester running over real market structure than a live simulation of mainnet, which is exactly what we need for proving components today, and a base we will keep pushing toward a genuine simulation of mainnet conditions.

 The UI alongside it
A busy cycle for the interface, and most of it was in service of this launch. New on the trading side: a live cross-subnet trade tape, real per-subnet token symbols wherever a token appears, identity on every fill, and order entry that shows your limit price, advanced parameters, fees and notional up front. Wallet support now spans four extensions with the localnet signing path built out end to end, and the faucet and proxy on-ramp arrived with it. Behind all of that sits a great deal of quieter groundwork, the kind that makes an exchange launch possible rather than visible, from the Hangar's live parameter editor to in-site dialogs, one shared volume vocabulary across the platform, and charts that pick up cleanly after an idle gap.

 Getting started
Request access at https://mvtrx.exchange/ if you are not registered already. Access may need to be approved before you can log in, so start here rather than at trading time.
,
Make sure you're on the localnet exchange. The topbar carries a Simulation / Exchange toggle - click Exchange, and select LOCALNET.
,
Connect a coldkey, using any of the four supported wallet extensions: Polkadot.js, SubWallet, Talisman or Crucible. Then prove ownership when the panel asks. Proving is free and moves no funds, and the faucet in the next step stays hidden until you do it.
,
Fund it: hit LOCALNET FAUCET in the identity panel. That TAO sits on a fork, so it carries no real value. You can claim up to 5 localnet TAO in total. If you need more, please justify the need in a DM or at our server.
,
SWAP is live for you from here. If the rail is what you came for, you can stop at this step.
,
Connect a hotkey and register it on the localnet. Registration burns a little TAO, so keep some back at step 4. This is what gives you a UID.
,
Authorise and fund your proxy wallet: in the connect-wallet flow it is the Proxy step, and it asks you to Authorise, then Fund. It is the proxy that co-signs and settles your exchange trades, so do not skip this one.
,
Trade. The exchange is open to you in the UI.
,

 Next week
The framework and instructions for running your own agents against the localnet exchange follow next week in release 0.6.0. Nothing to prepare for that in the meantime, and nothing stopping miners testing manual exchange interaction, or anyone testing the SWAP feature, today.

Try it out: https://mvtrx.exchange/
