[2026-08-14T09:17:51.200Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1537752102128979978
Rank tracks your standing, not your live score. Standing is an age-annealed track-record EMA of the score, and emission then runs through a Pareto sort-multiply.

At ~21:16 uid 21 was strong (kappa 1.33 = top ~13%, pnl-factor 1.00) but its standing was only 0.335 (up from 0.258 five hours earlier) -> final score 0.017. Two reasons it crawls:


Standing is a slow average: for an established miner the per-round update weight (~1/(k+1)) has decayed to ~0, so even a sustained-high kappa lifts it only gradually -- that's your ~1 spot/hour. A higher kappa converges to a higher standing, not a faster climb; the rate is capped by the EMA half-life.
,
Pareto + floor concentrate reward at the top, so a mid-pack standing pays low incentive even with high skill.
,

It keeps rising while you hold the kappa. One note from the data: uid 21 went inactive ~23:17-07:25, which dropped its standing and restarted the climb from a low base -- staying continuously active matters.

The old "high score -> quick rise" was changed on purpose: rank now follows a smoothed track record rather than the instantaneous score, so skill earns a high rank over the EMA horizon instead of within an hour (rewards sustained skill, resists flip-in/flip-out farming).

[2026-08-17T13:05:10.364Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1538896472525901904
On scores going to zero after a sim restart (thanks @τourisτ@@Adrian@ @Dev ): it's an inconsistency in how breakeven roundtrips are handled. Breakeven (zero-PnL) roundtrips count toward your scoring window during the sim, but were being dropped when the validator rebuilds history at a changeover, so the window could fall below the minimum right after a changeover and read "not scorable" (score 0 while the EMA decays, hits established miners not newcomers). Fix: keep them consistent across the boundary so the window doesn't change through a roll. Verified against today's real mainnet crossover, it restores everyone who was zeroed; ships with the next validator update. Whether breakeven roundtrips should count toward the window at all in general is a valid question that we're reviewing.

[2026-08-21T14:34:33.071Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1540368516811591750
@mvtrx・79  Release 0.5.5 - Hotfix 3

Just deployed to testnet and mainnet, ahead of the next simulation crossover:

 Scoring continuity across simulation restarts

The scoring loss at a simulation restart, described previously, is fixed. Intervals in which a miner closed no position were being dropped as history carried over onto the new clock, which could shorten a miner's assessment window below the minimum needed to score and zero its trading score for the rounds after a restart. The transition is now a pure rebasing of the existing history, so every interval carries over exactly as recorded. No action is needed from miners.

 0.6.0 in progress

While validating the next scoring revision against live data, we concluded that it does not by itself address some of the concerns raised. Component level analysis has demonstrated that the revision does what it was designed to do, which is to reward genuine two sided liquidity provision and to stop rewarding directional exposure. However, the manufactured price movement miners have been asking about is created in the market itself, not in the scoring formula, so it has to be addressed in the engine rather than in the reward calculation.

We are therefore adding venue level price protection to the simulation, of the kind real exchanges run, comparable to the limit-up/limit-down bands and market-order price collars used on equities and crypto venues. This bounds trades relative to a slow reference price rather than to the immediate top of book, so a single order cannot drive a price far from where the market has actually been trading, and moving that reference requires sustained activity over time rather than a burst. It bounds the trade itself rather than one order type, so it applies to market and limit orders alike. The threshold is being set to sit far above ordinary price movement, so that genuine repricing is not blocked.

We are currently carefully determining the appropriate parameterization for this, analyzing the effects in conjunction with the other revisions, and confirming that market quality is not degraded by the changes and that this can be confidently expected to result in better alignment between the incentives and the behaviour the subnet needs.

 Timeline
0.6.0 is expected on testnet early next week. We will monitor it there, confirm that all the new pieces are fully functional, including the updated background agents and the framework for writing agents to trade against the localnet exchange, and collect any feedback and criticism. Mainnet is expected a couple of days after the testnet launch.

Miners: Both the scoring revision and the price protection ship dormant in the 0.6.0 release, and neither will be enabled without sufficient notice. This allows us to put the actual design in front of you before it counts for anything, so that 0.6.0 shows what to expect when these are enabled in 0.6.1, and your feedback and criticism can land on the real implementation rather than on a description of it. The 0.6.0 run is also where we gather the data to set the 0.6.1 parameters, which will be published before anything is switched on. Enabling is then a configuration change against code that has already been deployed and reviewed.

[2026-08-26T16:45:26.676Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1542213396546715698
@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.0 - Testnet
,
Deployed to testnet, with mainnet following a couple of days later, once we have confirmed everything is working well and that miners are able to transition cleanly. 0.6.0 completes the exchange side of the agent framework, refines the market dynamics your agents trade in, and publishes the next scoring revision, switched off, so it can be reviewed and evaluated before it counts for anything.

What's in 0.6.0

 The exchange framework, published in full
The order instructions, the state model, the notice types and the response envelope for the exchange are all in the public tree, so a strategy can be written and tested against the exchange venue for the first time. This is the framework for running your own agents against the localnet exchange, as promised at the localnet launch.

 One agent, both mechanisms
No second agent, no second process and no mode flag. Your existing respond() is called on both the simulation and the exchange, and the framework builds whichever response that mechanism expects. Override respond_exchange() only when you want the exchange to behave differently.

 Refined market dynamics
The simulation's background agents have been retuned, and the market they produce is more realistic for it. Expect a noticeably different regime from 0.5.5. If your agent was tuned against the old dynamics, plan to re-tune it against the new ones during the testnet phase, rather than assuming the old settings carry over.

 The next scoring revision, shipped and switched off
Nothing about how you are scored changes in this release: the live path is KAPPA3 on realized round-trip P&L scaled by trading volume, exactly as it is today. What is new is that the next revision ships in the open, wired and switched off, so it can be studied, reviewed and criticised before it decides anything, and so we can collect the data that sets its parameters while the live scoring carries on unchanged.

In plain terms it adds a reward for providing liquidity, and it stops paying for simply being long a rising market. The liquidity side credits quoting both sides of the book and earning the spread between them, counted on whichever of your two sides is smaller. The skill side measures your P&L with the book's own drift taken out. Holding a position through a rise earns exactly zero from it; what counts is the part of the result the market did not simply hand you.

 Venue price protection, shipped inert
The limit-up/limit-down style collar mentioned previously is in the engine, inert by default, and no published config enables it. It refuses fills beyond a maximum deviation from the book's slow trailing reference of recent trades, so a manufactured price excursion is unprofitable at the point of execution rather than penalised after the fact.

 Install
The documented pip install -e . path now covers every runtime dependency the validator imports, a manifest ships the runtime config files for non-editable installs, install_miner.sh is idempotent and refreshes your agents in place when re-run, and a new .env.example documents the runtime environment.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

[2026-08-26T16:45:57.895Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1542213527488430080
Details for Miners
,
 Whether and when to update

Your existing agent keeps working. Nothing on the pre-0.6.0 agent surface was removed, an agent that implements only respond() is called exactly as before, and we verify that against the published example agents as part of every release.

Timing matters more than the update itself. 0.6.0 reaches testnet first and mainnet a couple of days later. If you run on testnet, or you want to start building for the exchange, take the test branch now. For a mainnet miner, update when the mainnet deploy lands.

Standard flow when you do update: fetch and check out 0.6.0, run ./install_miner.sh, and restart. Re-running the installer refreshes ~/.taos/agents in place; if an earlier re-run left a nested agents directory inside it, remove that after updating so the launcher reads the right files.

 What your agent needs

To keep trading the simulation, nothing. FinanceSimulationAgent is still exported as an alias of the same class object, so existing imports and issubclass checks hold, and a FinanceAgentResponse you construct yourself is returned unchanged.

For new work, subclass FinanceAgent and build responses with self.make_response(), which returns the same order API in both modes and finalizes to whichever type the current mode requires. self.exchange_mode tells you which mode a request is in, and it is request-scoped, so it stays correct while one agent instance serves both validators.

Three venue behaviours to handle if your agent will run on the exchange:


Leverage is refused. The venue runs with maxLeverage=0, so an order requesting leverage is rejected at placement rather than reduced. Gate leverage on self.exchange_mode.
,
Positions cannot be closed. Closing a position settles a margin loan, and with no leverage there is none to settle. The exchange accepts three instructions in total: limit order, market order and cancel.
,
A sell draws on one delegate. Size a sell against the largest single delegate's stake, not the sum across your delegations. An empty per-delegate map means not reported for that step, never no stake, so fall back to free balance when it is empty.
,

 New data for your logic

Accounts now carry the per-delegate stake map that makes the sell rule above actionable. The fee schedule the engine applies is published on the config alongside its volume tiers and the maker-taker ratio they derive from, and there is a minimum order size on the config that the engine rejects orders below. Every short wire field name now has a documented readable property, and existing code using the short names is unaffected.

[2026-08-26T16:46:06.340Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1542213562909458552
 Developing an agent for the localnet exchange

Scope first, because it matters: mainnet netuid 79 declares a single mechanism today, so there is nothing to register on and no exchange payload reaches a mainnet miner. What this release supports is developing and testing an exchange agent against a localnet exchange. The mainnet exchange mechanism is a later release, and registration and scoring details will be announced before it arrives. The agent you end up with is the one that will work then.


Update to 0.6.0, then read agents/MIGRATION_0.6.0.md and the "Running in both simulation and exchange mode" and "Exchange venue behaviours that catch people out" sections of agents/README.md.
,
Subclass FinanceAgent. Keep one respond() for both mechanisms, or add respond_exchange() when you want the exchange handled differently, and build with self.make_response().
,
Handle the three venue behaviours above, and read your fills from the notice handlers while treating the account on each state update as the authority. Notices are delivered as they happen and fills are repeated for a short window, so an agent that is down misses what happened while it was away.
,
Get localnet TAO. Connect a coldkey in the UI and prove ownership when the panel asks, which is free and moves no funds, then claim from the LOCALNET FAUCET in the identity panel. The faucet stays hidden until the proof is done. It costs nothing and the TAO sits on a fork, so it carries no real value, but you do need some: registering a hotkey burns a little.
,
Run it against the localnet yourself. Register a hotkey on netuid 79 on the localnet, then launch your miner against wss://localnet.mvtrx.exchange:443 instead of mainnet. The venue itself is not something you can stand up: the matching engine, the exchange-side engine and the chain reconciliation layer are not included in the repository and are ours to operate. If you prefer, the Hangar and the grants below cover it with no infrastructure cost to you.
,
If you want to see the venue behave before you point an agent at it, manual exchange trading is already open on EXCHANGE mode, LOCALNET network in the UI (https://mvtrx.exchange/), and the steps are in the localnet exchange launch post ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠.
,

 How the scoring revision and the collar get switched on

Together, in 0.6.1, and not before you have seen the design. The miner-facing explainer will be published first, covering the whole mechanism in plain language and the evidence behind each parameter. The parameters are re-measured on observed 0.6.0 data against thresholds fixed in advance, rather than carried over from the 0.5.5 regime this release changes, so no value published today should be read as final. The first weeks after enablement are monitored against those same measurements. They go together because the collar is what makes a manufactured excursion unprofitable.

Expect the miner rankings to reorder when it is switched on. The change is substantial rather than a tweak, and that is by design: the revision replaces the trading score rather than adjusting it.

If you want to prepare, the revision is behind --scoring.debeta.enabled and defaults to off, so you can turn it on in a local run and see how your agent scores under it. The strategy most exposed is one whose returns come mainly from holding direction while a book trends.

 Grants for testing against the localnet

We will be reaching out to miners directly with grants that cover deploying and testing strategies against the dual-mechanism localnet through Hangar, so you can put an exchange agent in front of the real venue at no cost to you.

Questions on any of this, bring them to Discord and we will help: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv
Link: https://mvtrx.exchange/
Link: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv
Link: https://mvtrx.exchange/

@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.0 - Now on Mainnet 
,
Following testnet confirmation, 0.6.0 is now live on mainnet: the exchange agent framework published in full, one agent class serving both mechanisms, a retuned simulation background population, and the next scoring revision shipped switched off.

Full details of what is in the release: ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠

Miners - update recommended, no agent code changes required

Nothing on the pre-0.6.0 agent surface was removed, so an agent that implements only respond() is called exactly as before, and an existing response object is still accepted as it is.

The market your agent trades has changed, though. A new simulation has been started, running the retuned background agents, so the new regime is live. It is noticeably different from 0.5.5, so plan to re-tune rather than assuming your old settings carry over.  Your score is not reset by the new run. Scoring is continuous across a simulation boundary.

To run 0.6.0 on mainnet, use the main branch.


Fetch and check out 0.6.0 on main
,
Run ./install_miner.sh
,
Restart your miner
,

Re-running the installer refreshes ~/.taos/agents in place. If an earlier re-run left a nested agents directory inside it, remove that after updating so the launcher reads the right files.

Building for the exchange

Wondering whether you need to register for the exchange mechanism? You do not. The exchange mechanism is not live on mainnet: netuid 79 declares a single mechanism today, so there is nothing to register on and no exchange payload reaches a mainnet miner. What this release supports is developing and testing an exchange agent against a localnet exchange, and the miner details in the release post cover how to do that.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79

Join our Discord for support and to share feedback: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79
Link: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv

@mvtrx・79  Status Update

0.6.0 reached testnet and then mainnet last week, putting the exchange agent framework in miners' hands, with the UI update landing behind it. This week is about the data: monitoring the new scoring on mainnet and preparing to enable it in 0.6.1.

What's Live Now

 0.6.0 on Mainnet
Live on mainnet, following testnet confirmation. It publishes the framework for writing miner agents that trade the exchange, completes the exchange plumbing, refines the simulation background agents, and ships the reworked scoring switched off for review and observation. Full release notes: ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠
The exchange mechanism itself is not live on mainnet, so there is nothing to register for - 0.6.0 enables developing and testing an exchange agent against the localnet exchange.

⇄ SWAP on Mainnet
Live since the launch post ⁠79・m∧τrx・ي⁠. Fully non custodial, with funds never leaving your wallet. Link several wallets, compose one plan across your whole portfolio, and execute it with a single signature. MAYA can compose those plans for you, and Nexus watches the market and your positions in one view.

 The Localnet Exchange
Running on the mainnet-seeded fork: a real limit order book, real curve maths and mainnet prices held in step, with test funds. Monitoring and testing continue, and with the 0.6.0 framework published this is where miner agents go next.

 MVTRX UI
Live at https://mvtrx.exchange/. Last week's update brought theming, refinements to complex multi-wallet and multi-delegate SWAP plan handling, clearer activity, Nexus loadout populated for swap users, a pass over layouts and charts, and another round of mobile work.

 The Hangar
Open for testing: build, deploy and run trading agents end to end inside MVTRX. Hangar capacity grants are ready and will be offered soon, so miners can deploy agents against the localnet exchange at no cost to themselves.

 MVTRX Terminal
https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/ continues as the miner and validator view of SN79 activity.

In Progress This Week

 UI updates
Iterative updates continue in response to feedback and testing, with the next batch expected later this week. A larger overhaul is in the works behind them.

 Scoring
0.6.0 put the reworked scoring on mainnet switched off, while the existing mechanism continues to determine miner ranks. We are monitoring it and analysing the data it produces, and preparing to enable it in 0.6.1 once the data confirms it behaves as intended. Its parameters will be set from that data and published first.

 Automated SWAP
Limit, DCA and other automated order types in development, switched off while we test.

 Sentiment integration
Work underway to bring external sentiment APIs into the simulations as an additional exogenous input.

 Multi-asset simulation
Under testing: several statistically distinct assets simulated at once, with automated tuning calibrating across them. Two configurations tuned to different market conditions are expected in the update after our first automated simulation.

 MVTRX API
Testing finalisation continues against the exchange, which is the complete surface it waited for.

 The Dashboard
In private testing and review alongside the UI overhaul.

Link: https://mvtrx.simulate.trading/

 UI update

In Progress

 0.6.1 and the new scoring

 Testing suites

 Simulation auto-tuning

 Everything else

@mvtrx・79  MVTRX UI Update 

The UI takes on the MVTRX look, SWAP gets quicker to work in, markets gains another surface for comparing subnets, and the Hangar is extended for the miner grants coming next.


⇄ SWAP
,
Identifying subnet trading opportunities gets easier: a sortable table you can scan at a glance, which stays responsive however many markets you follow. Signals read as a single clear line with the detail there when you want it, and choosing which of your wallets take part is more explicit.  Once a swap settles you can see what it actually cost you on chain, and follow it back to the transaction that settled it.  Also a number of general refinements and optimizations to the display and experience.


 Charts
,
The chart is easier to drive. The market selector leads with the subnet name and number, and the whole control cluster is simplified. The drawing tools gained spacing and clearer grouping, and the volume pane is labelled on hover.


 Hangar
,
A round of revisions, refinements and extensions across the Hangar, aimed at supporting agent deployments to the localnet exchange. This provides the groundwork for the capacity grants we will soon offer, so miners can test agents against the localnet exchange at no cost to themselves.


 Markets
,
Markets now has a sortable table, so you can line subnets up against each other on what matters: movement from the last hour out to the last month, emissions, market cap, liquidity and spread.


 General
,
The UI now wears the MVTRX palette by default, if you preferred the previous look it is still there as a Dark preset, and the colour palette is customisable through the whole interface, so you can tune it to your preference.  Alongside, a pass over the controls, topbar and preset layouts for a sleeker experience.

Let me try to rephrase our big agenda a bit here if interested in having a minute on that


The QUANT research side we have, and its simulation ("the blue side") + live ("the red side") environment, it has the touch of "biotech" x1000 potential applied to fintech; with patent applications, and powerful engine, and uniqueness, it stands in the space of "high risk + high reward"
,


The more mundane UI/UX part, with its trading related platform, with business intelligence, is more of a "infrastructure" type solution, the kind of consistent more predictable revenue creator, what typically exchanges apply, with transaction costs and services/fees.
,

The business model we have consists of these two, it is a combination of high risk and high rewards, and more consistent performance. This was a deliberate direction chosen. We work on both sides, since we want to take the chance on the high risk high reward game as well.

If you want to read further why we want to keep both of them alive regardless of the pressure:

If one is interested in finance applications, and the direction we are heading, then from purely from investor/staker perspective there are those two benefits, which I think personally which makes it interesting in its own right. Patents do not create revenue now. Data sales do not create revenue immediately, but reasonably fast. The big breakthroughs can, like in biotech, can become highly successful in the longer run.

[2026-09-09T14:44:57.478Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1547256505210904598
@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.1 - Now on Testnet 
,
0.6.1 is on testnet. This is the release where the reworked scoring starts to count.

What it changes, and why it matters

The reworked scoring pays for something more difficult and valuable than before: genuinely making a market. It measures the spread an agent captures on both sides of a book, strips out the part of a return that was simply the market moving, and discounts making volume that comes from a small set of dedicated counterparties rather than from a diverse set of takers. The intent is that the agents earning the most are the ones a trader would actually want on the other side of their order.

That matters beyond the miners it scores. The books these agents make run on the same matching engine as the exchange we are launching, so paying for market quality here is how the simulation becomes a market worth trading.

It arrives as a graduated transition rather than a switch. Shortly after deploy, once enough trading has accumulated to compute it, the new score is published for every miner while emissions still come entirely from the existing mechanism, so miners can see where they stand before it carries any weight. The weight is then raised in measured steps. Day one emissions match the current mechanism exactly.

The simulation also gets a live price band

A match can now reach at most 10% from a book's trailing reference in either direction, with that reference taken over the last 5 minutes of simulation time. In 0.6.0 the machinery existed but nothing was configured to use it. In practice this means a thin book can no longer be walked out to an extreme price: those sweeps stop at the band.

What to expect

On testnet the steps run to a fixed schedule, to verify the mechanics: a quarter weight Thursday morning, half Thursday evening, full replacement on Friday, then held over the weekend to gather data.

On mainnet each step is held against conditions registered in advance rather than against a date, and at the current simulation pace those holds work out at roughly 31 to 36 hours apiece. The transition there begins early next week.

Those are estimates derived from the conditions, not commitments. If a step's conditions are not met it waits, and we will say so here as each one is taken.

 Testnet dashboard

The testnet dashboard now shows the new statistics, in the De-beta scoring (0.6.1) row, so the numbers miners are scored on are the numbers anyone can see. The terminal (mvtrx.simulate.trading) will be similarly updated ASAP.

 Thank you

To everyone who reviewed the scoring revision and provided feedback while it sat switched off. Several changes in this release exist because of it.

 For miners

Update is recommended. Check out 0.6.1 on the test branch, run ./install_miner.sh, and restart your miner. Your score is not reset.

A detailed post will be attached to this one with the full parameter list, the exact step values, what the new published fields mean, and the smaller behaviour changes.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

Join our Discord for support and to share feedback: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test
Link: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv

[2026-09-09T14:45:35.211Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1547256663474446366
@mvtrx・79 

0.6.1 - Details for Miners 
,
 The blend and its dial

The trading score is a flat three way blend, and the validator refuses to start unless the three weights sum to 1.0:


trading = kappa.weight * kappa + pnl.weight * pnl + debeta.weight * debeta



--scoring.kappa.weight 0.79, --scoring.pnl.weight 0.21, --scoring.debeta.weight 0.0 (new)
,
--scoring.debeta.w_make 0.30, fixed for this release, and --scoring.debeta.p11_strength 1.0, was 0.0
,
--scoring.debeta.floor_scale 0.5, --scoring.debeta.centered_window 15, --scoring.debeta.mark_mode last
,
--scoring.debeta.min_books 4: an activation guard, not a per-miner rule. If fewer than four miners earn a positive de-beta score in a cycle, that cycle scores on the legacy path. A miner needs four books with |alpha| above the floor to receive a skill score, and that minimum is fixed in code.
,
--scoring.debeta.enabled is deprecated and ignored.
,

 The rungs

debeta.weight steps up and the legacy pair scales down in proportion, so kappa and realised PnL keep their current balance throughout: 0.0 (0.79 / 0.21), 0.25 (0.5925 / 0.1575), 0.50 (0.395 / 0.105), 1.0 (0 / 0).

Testnet runs these to a fixed schedule to verify the mechanics: 0.25 Thursday morning, 0.50 Thursday evening, 1.0 Friday, then held over the weekend.

Mainnet holds each rung against conditions registered in advance: blend invariant clean, reallocation within 10 points of prediction after at least two EMA half lives, no premature floor zeroing, extractor share under 5%, regime health, validator lockstep. One config change rolls any rung back.

One state worth knowing about before you see it: at the 0.25 and 0.50 rungs, while the de-beta score is still warming, the legacy part is renormalised to fill the whole score, so your emissions do not shift until de-beta scores actually exist. A rung being set is not the same as it taking effect. The final rung is only stepped once de-beta scores are already flowing.

 Making credit is now batch independent

Your spread capture is measured against a rolling centred mid per book, over 31 prints, that carries across state updates, so it no longer depends on how prints happen to be batched. A fill settles once 15 forward prints arrive, or after 60 sim seconds on a quiet book. 

 The counterparty diversity discount is already in your preview

p11_strength now defaults to 1.0. At debeta.weight = 0.0 it does not touch emissions, but it shapes the de-beta score you can see, so the preview already carries it. If your making volume comes from one or two dedicated counterparties who do not otherwise trade the market, that making credit is discounted; a market that a diverse set of takers actually uses is untouched. debeta_p11_factor is the discount you carry, where 1.0 means none, and debeta_making is the value after it.

 A ranking correction

Tied raw values now take their block's minimum rank. Previously equal values were separated by position in the uid list, which mattered because about 88% of miners on the board we measured share a making value of zero.

Re-measured at full replacement (weight 1.0) against a kappa-only baseline, on the last three windows of the 20260828 board: 85.1% reallocation, 70 uids zeroed. Nothing reallocates at the deploy weight of 0.0. If you saw the earlier pair of 67.5% and 41 zeroed, that used a different baseline and is superseded.

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-09-09T14:45:38.032Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1547256675306709022
 Published fields, per uid

debeta_score, debeta_making_rank, debeta_skill_rank, debeta_making, debeta_skill, debeta_skill_floor, debeta_p11_factor, debeta_weight, debeta_w_make, num_scored_books, scorable.

The dial and coverage fields publish every cycle. The decomposition publishes once at least four miners have positive de-beta scores. Note that num_scored_books and scorable describe the kappa leg until de-beta applies, and de-beta coverage after: books whose |alpha| clears the floor, and whether the uid received a score. A uid with no scorable books scores 0.0 with scorable false.

 Price band

No match prints more than 10% from a book's 5 minute trailing median, sampled every sim second, enforced at the single matching point, so sweeps stop at the band edge.

 Self trade prevention: if you set NO_STP, read this

NO_STP is now accepted and coerced to CANCEL_OLDEST. In 0.6.0 that flag caused your entire response to be discarded, silently, every time, so if you used it your historical scores understate your strategy. Self trade prevention is not disableable. An incoming order cancelled by it now sends a cancel notice to its owner, as resting side cancels already did.

 Notices

closeReason is normalised to SL, TP or none at parse time. The engine sent an integer and the exchange path a string, so a check written against one mechanism never fired on the other. Both now behave the same.

 GenTRX

Still opt in, as since 0.6.0. What is new is that the shard is adopted from the aggregator's assignment, which carries a bucket_prefix. Leave the mode empty to adopt, or set it to pin a shard.

 Example agents

Two bin/agent_params.sh values were at the wrong magnitude and now match each agent's documented units: expiry_period is in simulation nanoseconds (200 to 120000000000), and sampling_period is in seconds (1000000000 to 60). If you copied either, take the new values. RandomTakerAgent now takes leverage and mechanism from the response, like the other examples.

Questions: Discord, or bring them to the AMA: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv
Link: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv

[2026-09-10T08:09:57.313Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1547519487379505152
@mvtrx・79 

0.6.1 de-beta ladder: the first rung is live on testnet 
,
The testnet validator on SN 366 is now scoring at rung 1 of the de-beta ladder. A quarter of the trading score comes from the new metric, and the legacy legs are scaled down by that same quarter.


trading = 0.5925 x kappa + 0.1575 x pnl + 0.25 x de-beta
de-beta = 0.30 x making rank + 0.70 x skill rank


Parameters are unchanged from the release: w_make 0.30, and the four book breadth floor.

What this means

A quarter of what you are scored on is now two-sided spread capture and drift-stripped skill, rather than the direction a position happened to catch. The kappa and PnL legs keep exactly their balance relative to each other, so nothing has been re-weighted between them, only scaled to make room.

Give it time to show

Scores move over the scoring EMA, whose half life is three hours of simulation time. At the pace testnet is currently running, that is closer to two days of wall clock than to an afternoon, so expect placements to keep drifting well past today rather than settling this evening. A placement you see an hour from now is not the finished picture.

Where to watch


https://testnet.simulate.trading/, the Validators dashboard: the De-beta per miner table and the blend panels.
,
The Books dashboard: per-book capture and alpha columns.
,
Background reading: Notes on the Incentive Metric of MVTRX, on the docs page.
,

What happens next

Testnet runs a fixed schedule to exercise the mechanics: 0.50 later today, and full replacement, (0, 0, 1), on Friday. Because the rungs step faster than the EMA settles, you will see one rung applied while the previous one is still working through. That is deliberate on testnet, where the point is to prove the mechanics rather than to let standings stabilise.
Link: https://testnet.simulate.trading/

@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.1 Final - On Testnet 
,
0.6.1 is finalised and published to the test branch. It has been running on testnet with the reworked scoring at full weight since Friday 11 September, and this build carries the revisions identified during the testnet monitoring phase.

What the reworked scoring pays for

It pays for the two things a trader wants on the other side of an order. Liquidity: the spread an agent captures on both sides of a book, summed across the books it quotes, discounted where its flow comes from a few dedicated counterparties rather than a diverse set of takers. Skill: the profit an agent's timing adds beyond what simply holding its position through the market's move would have returned, and how consistently that shows up across its books, so riding a trend earns nothing and a good call is worth the same whether the market rose or fell. Both are computed over the last three simulated hours of fills, weighted 30 to 70 toward skill, and both require the agent to be answering the validator. The intent is that the agents earning the most are the ones providing exactly that.

What the testnet week refined

 Standings are decided among the agents that performed. On both measures, an agent with a positive result is ranked against the other agents with a positive result, so a place in the table is earned against genuine competition.

⇄ Concentration is measured across an agent's whole flow, rather than against a subset of the takers on the other side of its volume.

 An agent that stops answering is not scored while it is dark. One valid response brings it back with its record intact, and that record now survives a validator restart.

 Every score is published in full, component by component, so the numbers behind a ranking are open to anyone reading them and not only to the agent being scored.

 The price band holds through a restart

The band has been running on testnet since 0.6.1 first arrived there. In this build its state travels with the book across an engine restart, so a resumed book keeps its band instead of coming back without one. A book the band has been holding starts to release after five simulated minutes of silence, widening one band width at a time until it prints, and snaps back to the normal band on that first print. That release is the only time the band sits wider than its configured limit. The reference itself moves only on trades, so quoting cannot move it.

Why this matters beyond the agents it scores

The books these agents make run on the same matching engine as the exchange we are building, so paying for market quality here is how the simulation becomes a market worth trading.

 For miners

Update is recommended. Check out 0.6.1 on the test branch, run ./install_miner.sh, and restart your miner. Every parameter, the dials and their defaults, and the smaller behaviour changes are in the details messages as a thread on this one.

Mainnet follows later today, with its own announcement. It ships with de-beta inert: the metric computed and published for every agent, carrying none of the reward. The first weighted step, 0.25, follows once the initial checks and verification are complete, likely tomorrow.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

Join our Discord for support and to share feedback: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv (edited)
Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 8:27 PM

[2026-09-15T12:26:51.189Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1549396077189267490
@mvtrx・79 

0.6.1 Final - Details for Miners 
,
Companion to the 0.6.1 announcement, for anyone running an agent, a validator or a localnet deployment.

 The rollout


Testnet, now. The code is on the test branch and running. The testnet validator is deliberately at full replacement, de-beta weight 1.0, which is how this week's data was produced.
,
Mainnet, expected later today. It arrives at the rehearsal rung: de-beta computed and published for every agent at zero weight, paying nothing. The score formula on day one is exactly the one mainnet runs now, kappa 0.79 and PnL 0.21. The price band becomes active on mainnet at the same time, for the first time.
,
Then the ladder. De-beta weight 0.25, then 0.50, then 1.0. Each step is a defaults change and a fresh deploy, held for at least a full day that includes the daily changeover, longer when one of its pre-registered conditions is marginal, and taken only when those conditions hold. Rollback is one defaults change back to the previous rung.
,

Everything below is in the release. Nothing in it changes the scoring formula on mainnet on day one; the band changes which orders can print.

 The blend, and what a fresh checkout gives you

The trading score is a flat three way blend, and the validator refuses to start unless the three weights sum to 1.0:


trading = kappa.weight * kappa + pnl.weight * pnl + debeta.weight * debeta



The branch defaults are --scoring.kappa.weight 0.79, --scoring.pnl.weight 0.21, --scoring.debeta.weight 0.0. That is the rung mainnet starts on, and it is what you get from a fresh checkout of test.
,
The testnet validator runs at de-beta 1.0 through its own launch line rather than through these defaults, so do not read the testnet board as what the defaults do.
,

 What changed in how a leg becomes a rank

These shape the de-beta metric. On mainnet they change nothing until its weight is raised above zero, and you can watch them in the published decomposition before then.


Skill. Non-positive skill is clamped before ranking, and positive skills are then ranked among themselves. A lone positive ranks 1.0. Skill needs at least four books whose alpha clears the magnitude floor.
,
Liquidity. The same rule now applies to making: positive makers are ranked among positive makers rather than against a pool that is mostly non-makers.
,
Counterparty discount. Non-miner takers are kept in the denominator under a single market-flow bucket, so the discount is measured against all of your flow. The top-k concentration is still drawn from miner takers only.
,
Presence. The validator keeps the outcome of its last 50 queries to each agent, about four minutes of queries on testnet. An agent whose window is full and holds no successful response is not scorable for that cycle; one valid response makes it present again with its accumulators intact. The windows are persisted with validator state, so a restart neither empties the board nor reopens the gate, and a uid with a partial window counts as present.
,
Continuity. At full weight, a cycle that produces no map now carries the previous map for a bounded time rather than scoring the board zero, and the decomposition is published for every agent at every rung.
,

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-09-15T12:27:06.474Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1549396141299466341
 Dials and defaults

| Dial | Default | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| --scoring.debeta.skill_rank_scope | positives | whole |
| --scoring.debeta.making_rank_scope | positives | whole |
| --scoring.debeta.presence_gate | 1 | 0 disables |
| --scoring.debeta.presence_window | 50 | |
| --scoring.debeta.making_floor_scale | 0.0 (built, off) | |
| --scoring.debeta.p11_strength | 1.0 | 0 disables |
| --scoring.debeta.w_make | 0.30 | |
| --scoring.debeta.centered_window | 15 | |
| --scoring.debeta.floor_scale | 0.5 | |
| --scoring.debeta.min_books | 4 | |
| --scoring.debeta.publish_book_gauges | on | |
| --scoring.kappa.lookback | 3 simulated hours, both legs | |

The ranking and presence rules are the ones with a dial. The counterparty discount and the continuity work have no alternative rule.

 The price band

Active on testnet today, and active on mainnet from the deploy later today. It is configured per exchange rather than as a validator dial:


maxPriceBand 0.10: an order priced further than this from the trailing reference is refused. 0 disables the band.
,
bandRefWindow 5 simulated minutes, bandRefInterval 1 simulated second: the reference is the median trade price sampled once a second over the window. It is taken from trades only, so quoting cannot move it.
,
bandReleaseAfter 5 simulated minutes: silence since the last print, or since the first refusal where no print is known, before a band that has been refusing marketable orders starts to widen. 0 disables the release.
,
bandReleaseStep 30 simulated seconds, bandReleaseMax 0.5: one further band width per step, capped. The first print snaps it back.
,

A release is the only time the effective band exceeds maxPriceBand. The band's state travels with the book in the checkpoint, and the silence is counted from the last print the checkpoint carries, so a book that was already held when the engine stopped still releases after a resume.

[2026-09-15T12:27:12.024Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1549396164577857647
 Operational


The engine source changes, so a redeploy needs a taosim rebuild. The Python side alone is not enough. This applies to validators and to anyone running a localnet deployment; updating a miner does not.
,
The engine now writes a checkpoint on an intended stop. Resuming from that stop checkpoint is off by default in this release, so a resume still starts from the last periodic checkpoint. The restored books have been checked against the ones before the stop and are not thinner, and the default is expected to flip in a later release once a resume from it has been watched.
,
Validator robustness. Hourly log compression and the disk cleanup behind it no longer abort on a log file whose name the period parser cannot read. A metagraph sync arriving while the worker is shutting down no longer raises. A trade's close reason is normalised on every trade event, so the reason you read is the same on each surface.
,

 Smaller changes worth knowing


The L3 archive gains a record kind. When the validator resets an agent, the engine writes an r record to each book's L3 log after that book's reset-cancels, so a reset is visible even for an agent with nothing resting. Readers that select on the o, t and c kinds skip it untouched. A reader that assumes every record is one of those should be checked.
,
Order and fill identity is consistent across surfaces. Pool-executed orders are numbered and acknowledged, settlement signals carry both ids to the fill notice, and each fill is delivered once. Refusals are typed and sized.
,
STP cancellations are announced to the owner in simulation as well as exchange mode, and a GTT expiry is scheduled at its deadline rather than one expiry period later.
,
agents/README.md documents which notice handlers fire on both mechanisms, so an agent written against simulation needs no change on the exchange, and it describes the settlement-proxy notices that are exchange only.
,
A whole number keeps its value. Trailing zeros are stripped only from a fractional part.
,
The decomposition reaches the data service. Per-agent scoring maps carry the de-beta legs and the dials, so the API and the UI show what the validator computed, including at zero weight.
,

MVTRX 0.6.1 - Now on Mainnet 
,

Emissions do not change today

The weight is then raised from zero in measured steps, 0.25, then 0.50, then 1.0, each held for at least a full day and taken only when conditions registered in advance hold. We will say so here as each step is taken.

That ordering is deliberate. The new metric is visible on every agent, scored and published, before it carries any reward at all. Nobody has to take on trust what it would have paid.

 A live price band, new to mainnet

A book the band has been holding starts to release after five simulated minutes of silence, widening one band width at a time until it prints, and snaps back to the normal band on that first print. That release is the only time the band sits wider than 10%. The reference itself moves only on trades, so quoting cannot move it.

MVTRX 0.6.1 - De-beta rung 1 on mainnet 
,
De-beta now carries weight on mainnet. The trading score from this deploy is kappa 0.5925, PnL 0.1575, de-beta 0.25, the first of the measured steps announced with 0.6.1. Since the 15 September deploy the metric ran at zero weight while every rehearsal gate was checked against the live board: weights published as configured, nothing paid to absent agents, a settled skill floor, a stable board over the whole day.

What changes for you

A material share of emission reallocates over the next day or two as the score EMA converges, about half of it within the first sixteen hours. Agents with a zero de-beta score lose share; agents that capture spread on both sides of a book and time their inventory well gain it.

Your decomposition, per agent and per book, is on the dashboards, and the dashboard guide in the repository is refreshed for 0.6.1 with the de-beta panels documented.

Also in this build

The skill leg and its floor are scored over the books an agent filled inside the window, not the books it merely holds.

@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.1 - De-beta rung 2 on mainnet 
,
The second measured step. From this deploy the trading score is kappa 0.395, PnL 0.105, de-beta 0.50. Rung 1 ran for ~2 days with every gate read against the live board: the reallocation arrived as expected, nothing was paid to an absent agent, the skill floor stayed settled and the board held its shape.

What changes for you

De-beta is now half of the trading score, and most of the weight added at this rung goes to the making leg: the making weight moves from 0.30 to 0.50. Two-sided spread capture carried 0.075 of the trading score at rung 1 and carries 0.25 now; drift-stripped skill goes from 0.175 to 0.25. Agents that capture spread on both sides of a book gain share, and agents whose score rests on one-sided taking give it up.

Why the making leg

The two legs settle at different times. Spread capture is fixed at the fill, against the mid at that moment, and pays only when you are filled on both sides of a book. Drift-stripped alpha is settled at the window's end, against the whole window's move, so it also credits round trips closed before a move reverted. Two-sided liquidity across the books is what the subnet most needs to grow now, so this rung's added weight goes to the leg that measures it directly. The skill leg keeps its definition; a refinement that strips drift only over the prints an agent held is being calibrated for 0.6.2 and will be announced before it takes effect.

Also in this build


The Recent Trades table on the agents dashboard shows the counterparty of each fill.
,
Validator engine-restart handling is hardened.
,
Site references updated to the new mvtrx.ai home.
,

Next

As at rung 1 the reallocation arrives over the next day or two as the score EMA converges, about half of it within the first sixteen hours.

The last step takes de-beta to 1.0 and retires kappa and PnL from the trading score. It is taken only when the same conditions confirmed to hold. The earliest that allows is Monday 21 September, and we will say so here when it is done.

Update is recommended.

@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.1 · De-beta at full weight on mainnet 
,
The last step of the ladder. From this deploy the trading score is de-beta alone: kappa and PnL to zero, de-beta to 1.0. 

What changes

De-beta carries the whole score. The reallocation arrives over a day or two as the score average converges, about half of it in the first sixteen hours, as at every previous rung. The legs are unchanged from rung 2: making weight at 0.50 against drift-stripped skill at 0.50, measured over the books an agent filled inside the window.

Nothing in this step changes what miners run. It is a validator-side configuration change.

Also in this release

Reliability work across the validator and the simulation engine, and a few dashboard labels. None of it changes what an agent earns.

What we are watching

How concentrated emission becomes at full weight, across the top of the board and by operator. Board health, meaning positive scores, the skill floor, and that nothing is paid to an absent agent, and the opening of the next simulation run, due in the coming days.

0.6.2

Two scoring options follow with 0.6.2, planned for this week, both shipping switched off, with every agent's figure under the alternative published so the effect is visible before anything moves: the skill leg's drift stripped only over the prints an agent held, and the making leg paid in proportion to the spread actually captured, so an operator's total follows the liquidity it provides rather than the number of accounts it spreads that liquidity across. Testnet this week, mainnet shortly after, both these new parameters off while we observe the effects. Neither is enabled without a dated announcement here first, and the scoring page records every change on the day it takes effect.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79

[2026-09-22T09:20:03.184Z] 7/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1551885782468399106
I will say a few things here first to all. DIS, Dynamic Incentive Structure was innovated by us to give a dynamic incentive structure to liquidity makers and takers. When there is too much taking, makers will get rebate. When there are too much making, takers will get rebate. The rebates are directly from the opponent party – the middleman (the organizers, that is, MVTRX) does not take anything, but may in the future.

We can manage where the optimal "point of balance" is. Usually, one would think 50-50 is the ideal, that is, we want as many takers as makers. But clearly, if we see too much taking, we can edit it to support more the making side, or vice versa. So the "tipping point" is important to note. These things are explained in the TAOS white paper sequel, and if you have not seen that, I can link also here for everybody to find easier.

It is important to note that ideally this works peer-to-peer. We are observing how this plays out, and what is the final form of implementation.

Do you need help in something in particular?

[2026-09-22T15:44:35.632Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1551982555329335329
On this week's scoring questions
,
Addressing points raised by @sonny @Dev @τourisτ @NinjaWolves 
All figures below were taken from the board earlier today, 22 September, unless dated otherwise.

The counterparty factor is being applied to the accounts named. It applies to the making leg. On the operator behind uids 89 and 230, most making accounts carried a factor of 0.22 or lower when measured, so most of their measured making was removed before ranking; the board median is 0.995. uid 230 was at 0.13. uid 89 was at 0.26 when the screenshot was taken and 0.86 when we measured, because the factor is recomputed every round from who has been trading against that account recently, so it moves as those counterparties change.

The score is the average of the two ranks, making and skill. uid 89 when measured: 0.5 x 0.338 (making rank, after the discount) + 0.5 x 0.729 (skill rank) = 0.5334, as published. Nothing is skipped.

The real issue is how few books some skill scores rest on. Skill measures how consistent an account's results are across the books it trades. Measured across very few books it can read as extremely consistent when there is not enough evidence to say so. When measured, eighteen accounts scored on eight books or fewer took incentive at a median skill of 8.9, against 0.83 for the 171 scored on more. uid 230 was on four books, uid 89 on eight. That is not what the skill leg is for, and 0.6.2 will address this.

On trading between accounts. No account trades with itself here, and the board shows none doing so. Trading between accounts under one operator is a different question. We are monitoring it, the counterparty factor already reduces the making credit it produces, and 0.6.2 carries further work on this.

On the EMA. The published de-beta score is the live window; what the ladder pays is a smoothed record of it, so the two differ, most of all in the days after a weight change. That gap is 64 per cent closed from the 21 September change. Whether to remove the smoothing is a real question and we have measured it both ways: on the 21 September board removing it would have concentrated emission further; on today's board it would spread it slightly. It cuts both ways, and it is being kept while the transition finishes. The one part we do consider a defect, a newly registered slot starting with no history so its first window counts in full, is being reworked separately.

On 0.6.2. It includes changes to how the skill leg is measured that address the thin-book scores above, and further work on the trading-between-accounts question. The details will be published with the release note when it goes live (testnet planned tomorrow, mainnet on Thurs before the next simulation changeover).

@sonny @JDonald @Dev @BugsBunny[τ , ⛏] @victor Thanks for the reports. 

5HZ6SkYNHhWBC4Dqpf2LqcCeZs9e3eupEH7ZDgFeZEfqi3bz: confirmed. When measured earlier today, most of the fills of its paid accounts came from a handful of accounts that lose money on every fill, rather than from the market, on very few books. That is wash trading in market terms. A mitigation for exactly this pattern is in the 0.6.2 candidate that goes to testnet today, with mainnet to follow this week after acceptance. We will publish the details once it is live.

5Dyy5Q9qpHMNfgogecBTLZc63CrujPGiNb2P7Jov7C3xY5Xq: not confirmed. Its accounts' fills come overwhelmingly from the market's background flow and from unrelated takers, and they are paying for it in realized PnL at very high volume. That is what real market making looks like. 

On the CP factor: it is applied to the making value before the making rank, so a 20 to 30 per cent discount does not move a rank position much, which is why it looks inert on the dashboard. It was also built primarily for a single dedicated counterparty, and a ring of many small ones reads as diverse to it. Both points are addressed in 0.6.2: the factor reaches further and is felt in the payout rather than displayed next to it.

On the zero 24h volume: that column shows the lowest daily volume across all books, so 0.00 means no trades on at least one book, not that the account is inactive. Those accounts did trade. Skill scored on a handful of books is addressed in 0.6.2 as well.

We will not ban on IP or coldkey. As sonny says, those are cheap to change. Every measure stays market-based, and the monitoring that produced these numbers keeps running.

@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.2 - On Testnet 
,
A market chosen by calibration

This is the first market configuration chosen by our automated calibration rather than tuned by hand: a search over roughly 800 candidate markets, each scored against real exchange data.

Conditions differ from 0.6.1 as a result. Anything tuned against the old book is worth re-checking, and results that span the two configurations are not like-for-like.

Scoring asks for breadth

Four scoring values change. They are on now on testnet, and on mainnet from the run boundary at 16:18 UTC on 24 September.

Under 0.6.2, skill counts only for accounts trading a real breadth of books, and scales down for an account covering a narrow slice of the field. The counterparty discount that already applies to the making leg now applies to the skill leg too, and looks at a wider set of counterparties.

Two further steps follow only after observation on mainnet, each announced before it changes: a minimum edge per book before an alpha counts, decided Friday 25 September; and paying both halves of the score in proportion to what each account earned rather than by rank, on testnet from Friday after that read, with a mainnet decision Monday 28 September. The quantities behind both are already published, so what they would pay can be read on the live board first.

 For miners

Rebuild from the published tree and restart: the engine, the configuration and the protocol package all move. No code change is required, and an agent still on the 0.6.1 model keeps working.

A separate post follows with the parameter detail and the dials.

[2026-09-23T15:45:24.131Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1552345146614349876
0.6.2 - Details for Miners 
,
Companion to the 0.6.2 announcement, for anyone running an agent, a validator or a local deployment.

 The sequence

Today, 23 September. 0.6.2 on testnet, on the configuration mainnet will launch with: the calibrated market and the new scoring. Mainnet is unchanged until tomorrow.

Thursday 24 September, 16:18 UTC. The mainnet run boundary: 0.6.2 deployed, a new simulation run opens on the calibrated configuration, and the four scoring values below are on. Market conditions change from that point; the effect on incentive phases in over the following day rather than landing at the minute.

Friday 25 September. First post-boundary read, and a decision on a 2.3 basis point skill hurdle, a minimum edge per book before an alpha counts. Small if enabled: on replay three accounts moved. After that read, testnet switches to proportional pay for both halves of the score. Testnet only; on mainnet the debeta_making_share, debeta_skill_net_alpha and debeta_skill_p11_factor gauges keep showing what it would pay. Nothing changes over the weekend.

Monday 28 September. Mainnet decision on the same, on three days of those gauges and three testnet days. If enabled, the making half is paid by discounted captured spread and the skill half by net alpha, and splitting a strategy across accounts gains nothing.

Any later switch is announced and dated in advance. Rolling a dial back is a configuration change and a validator restart; accumulators persist and no state migrates.

 The simulation configuration

The first configuration chosen by automated calibration rather than by hand, from a search over roughly 800 candidate markets each scored against real exchange data. What moves:


The price process: both the fundamental price and the magnetic field, which is reshaped rather than trimmed.
,
The agent population: twice as many high-frequency traders, re-parameterised throughout, with new variance and bar-based quantities they can now compute; noise and stylized traders re-parameterised; agent wealth drawn uniformly rather than from a seeded Pareto draw; FuturesTraderAgent at zero instances.
,
psiHFT_constant is renamed psiHFT_quotes. Both spellings load, so an existing local configuration keeps working. Only simulation_0.xml is published.
,

The agents changed in conduct, not only in calibration, the high-frequency trader most of all, so a market difference is not the parameters alone:


Background agents read the top of book and the running statistics directly instead of round-tripping the exchange, so each acts on the book as of its own wakeup. The exchange still serves those requests for external agents such as yours.
,
The high-frequency trader keeps exactly one resting quote per side per book, tracks whether an order is live or in flight, requotes the side that was hit, and gained an inventory rebalance gated by psi. Its quote size can be drawn as a multiple of traded volume, and psiHFT_quotes scales inventory by the agent's own average quote, so its value is not comparable across the rename.
,
The ALGO trader gained a slice mode that either clears the touch or caps at the resting volume, and its volatility recursion steps on regularly sampled returns.
,
The stylized trader's post-only volatility guard is now two numbers: the sigma at which it is half on, and the band over which it completes.
,
Several agents gained bound accessors that clamp without drawing from the random stream, so a seeded run stays reproducible.
,

tauF is fractional in the configuration but stays an integer on the wire, with the exact value in a new optional field: the config is a wire contract, and retyping it would make an un-upgraded miner reject the whole payload.

[2026-09-23T15:45:32.280Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1552345180793741383
 The scoring values

The four are 0.6.2's code defaults: a validator on 0.6.2 runs them with no flag set, and only validators are involved. With them off the scorer reproduces the 0.6.1 leg exactly, which is how the change was measured.


skill_min_books, 20. Skill counts only when measured on at least 20 qualifying books and reads 0 for the cycle below that. The making leg is unaffected.
,
skill_max_inactive_books, 0.375. Skill scales down below 62.5 per cent coverage of the field's books, unscaled at or above.
,
skill_p11_strength, 1.0. The counterparty factor applies to skill as it already does to making.
,
p11_topk, 10. The factor looks at ten of a maker's largest counterparties rather than two, so concentration spread across several accounts registers the same as concentration in one.
,

"Qualifying" means the account's per-book alpha, its result net of that book's drift, clears the field's skill floor at half the median absolute alpha across the board; a negligible or accidental result does not count toward the twenty. debeta_coverage_books shows the books an account filled, num_scored_books the ones that qualified.

Unchanged: w_make at 0.50, the making leg paid by rank, the presence gate, the skill floor, and de-beta at weight 1.0. The 0.6.1 ladder completed on 21 September; there is no ratchet left.

When you will see it. The legs are measured over a rolling three simulation hours, about eighteen wall-clock hours at the current speed, and the published score is smoothed by the track record. Gauges and ranks are on the Agents dashboard at dashboard.simulate.trading.

 What to do


Rebuild from the published tree. The engine, the configuration and the protocol package all move. No code change is required: protocol imports are unchanged, both psiHFT spellings load, and a miner still on the 0.6.1 model keeps working.
,
Re-check any strategy calibrated against 0.6.1 conditions. This is the release's main practical impact; backtests spanning the two configurations are not comparable.
,
Trade a real breadth of books. Fewer than twenty qualifying books reads zero on skill, and coverage under 62.5 per cent of the field scales it down.
,
Check your own configurations for the unknown-attribute warning. An attribute the engine reports as unknown has been doing nothing, most likely a typo or a renamed parameter; the warning names the attribute, the element and the file.
,
Restart a long-lived local simulation rather than resuming it. 0.6.1 checkpoints still restore, but a restore under 0.6.1 lost wakeup state.
,

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

[2026-09-25T06:51:19.434Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1552935517144875013
@Dev @victor @sonny @Alex On blocking addresses or coldkeys and on zeroing scores by hand: no. The score reads what the fills show, not who sent them, and a list of names is one thing any group of accounts can route around.

On the counterparty factor: it is applied, to both legs. What limits it today is that the score pays by rank, and a discount only moves an account when it pushes it below its neighbours. The step that removes that limit is paying by value, where the factor scales the payout directly. It was announced with 0.6.2, will be enabled on testnet today, with the mainnet decision on Monday 28 September after sufficient live gauges have been collected and evaluated to confirm and select appropriate parameters.

https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1553033653569720431
@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.2 - Proportional Pay on Testnet 
,
As announced on Wednesday, testnet now pays both halves of the score in proportion to what each account earned.

The making half is paid by each account's share of the spread it captured, and the skill half by its net edge over the books it traded, among accounts with real breadth. Shares add up, so a strategy run across several accounts earns the same total as the same strategy run once. A single strategy that captures spread or carries an edge keeps its standing or improves it.

Mainnet stays as it is over the weekend. The mainnet decision is on Monday 28 September, on three days of the live figures and three days of testnet, and it will be announced here before anything moves.

The per-book skill hurdle stays off: on the current run it would not have moved a single account.

 For miners

Nothing to rebuild and nothing to configure. What the new rule pays is already visible on both networks, and the dashboard guide is refreshed from the live boards to show where: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/test/doc/dashboard/README.md

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/blob/test/doc/dashboard/README.md
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

[2026-09-25T13:42:57.134Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1553039106806644828
The CP factor is applied today, on both legs, but the ladder pays positions in the ranking and a discounted score can still hold one. That is why it is on the dashboard now: for everyone to observe while the pay rule is prepared. Monday's rule pays shares, and the factor multiplies the share directly: a factor of 0.3 earns 30 per cent of what the same contribution earns at 1.0. That is the penalty, it is already running on testnet, and the column stays because it is what will pay.

[2026-09-25T14:22:20.540Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1553049019650019329
You are right that testnet cannot show it; it was never the evidence. The evidence is mainnet's own data: every post-boundary mainnet board is replayed through the shipped code with the pay rule on, so what Monday pays is computed from this board and this pattern.

The A-versus-B test you describe exists and runs on every mainnet window before a change ships. Splitting: the best real account split across sixteen accounts earns no more than the one. Coordinated fills from many different counterparties: a synthetic ring where every fill comes from a different private feeder drops the fed account's factor from 0.83 to 0.17 while the rest of the field is untouched, because the measure cancels counterparties everybody trades with and not the private ones. A parked account at the minimum with perfect consistency and no edge is paid its edge, not its rank.

On the live boards that gives the largest coordinated set roughly a quarter of what the ladder pays it today, and about sixty more accounts paid.

It lands Monday because the flip is gated on data, not on a calendar: three days of that live comparison on mainnet agreeing with the prediction, and three days of the rule running on testnet without a fault. The counterparty discount itself has been applied on mainnet since Thursday.

Monday's rule pays measured contribution, discounted for who it was earned against; it does not yet ask how much of it the open market actually received. That share is measured on every mainnet board from today, next to what the rule pays. If, after Monday, flow between related accounts still pays out of line with what the market received, the next revision weights contribution by that share. Whether it is needed is decided on that evidence, the same way this change was.

@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.2 - Proportional Pay on Mainnet 
,
As announced on Friday, mainnet now pays both halves of the score in proportion to what each account earned, the rule testnet has run since then.

The making half is paid by each account's share of the spread it captured, and the skill half by its net edge in the current window, among accounts with skill on at least twenty books. Shares add up, so one strategy run across several accounts earns no more than the same strategy run once. What pays is current performance: a strong window pays now, and a strong start carries for hours.

Alongside it, each account's skill bar is set by its own trading. A book's edge counts once it clears 2.3 basis points of the account's own filled notional on that book, so nobody else's size can move it. This takes the place of the field-wide floor and was set to qualify the same accounts.

Incentive follows over the next few hours as validators set weights.

 For miners

Nothing to rebuild and no code change: the agent interface and the notices are unchanged. The detail, including direct answers to the questions raised about large operators and early leaders, is in the post below.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79

[2026-09-28T15:14:01.987Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554149191658242090
@mvtrx・79 

0.6.2 Mainnet Enablement - Details for Miners 
,
Companion to today's announcement, covering what is new since Friday's testnet post and the questions people asked. There is no protocol or interface change, and agent code works unchanged.

 Emission is paid by magnitude on both halves

As on testnet since Friday, both halves pay by magnitude; the ranking ladder is kept only as the fallback for a half in which nobody qualifies.

In practice the reward for making is close to linear in the making you do, and the reward for skill close to linear in the alpha you realise, so a small improvement moves your share by roughly the same amount wherever you sit. Splitting one account's activity across several uids gains nothing, because shares add, and a freshly registered slot earns its current window's share.

 Your skill bar is your own

A book's alpha counts toward skill once it clears 2.3 basis points of your own filled notional on that book. This replaces the field-relative floor, which was set against the median absolute alpha across the field and so could move with other agents' size. The hurdle was chosen to reproduce the membership the floor gave on both a young and a mature field: it is meant to keep the answer stable, not to change who qualifies. Both settings remain configurable for a validator operator.

 Run boundaries

A run-boundary issue was identified and corrected following the last simulation changeover; 0.6.2 includes the fix.

 Price band release

A validator operator can now let the exchange price band widen gradually while a book is pinned; it is currently configured off.

 Can a large operator set the floor for everyone? @snakesss

No. In 0.6.2 there is no field-wide floor for anyone's size to move: a book's alpha counts once it clears 2.3 basis points of the account's own filled notional on that book, so each account's bar depends only on its own trading. You read the earlier floor correctly: it was set from the median alpha across the field, the counterparty discount came after it, and that is why it was replaced.

 Does a strong start carry for days? @Alex 

The EMA is neither removed nor shortened: it is no longer what decides pay. Under the ladder the track-record memory was three simulation hours, about half a real day at the current rate. The pool pays current magnitudes: the skill half is the current three-hour window with no smoothing, and the making half carries the three-simulation-hour smoothing of captured spread. A strong start carries for hours, and a strong window pays now.

 Unchanged

The 24 September launch values stay: at least twenty qualifying books for skill, coverage weighting at 0.375, the counterparty discount on both legs, and de-beta weight 1.0. Presence gating, the agent interface and the notice formats are all as they were.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79 (edited)

[2026-09-28T15:31:39.162Z] richard
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554153625771573361
@6/. 
Suggestions: making feeding rings and account farming unprofitable

A few ideas based on what I've seen. You know the system best, so treat these as input.


Ship proportional pay
,
 (already staged)
Pay each UID in proportion to what it actually contributes, not by rank position. Copying one strategy across 20+ UIDs then stops multiplying income.


Only credit profit made against the background market
,

Feeding works because a miner can profit from another miner who loses on purpose. If making and skill counted only trades against your background agents (or heavily discounted miner-to-miner trades), feeding would earn nothing. Honest miners would lose relatively little, since background agents do most of the trading.


Push out consistent losers
,

UIDs with near-zero making and steadily negative skill on huge volume don't behave like real traders. Give them zero weight so they are the first replaced when new UIDs register, and ignore the profit others earn by trading against them.


Raise the registration fee
,
 (e.g. to ~$40–50 through a higher minimum burn)
The farming depends on cheap churn: many registrations a day to rotate UIDs and replace pushed-out feeders. At ~$45 a UID that gets expensive, while a one-off $45 is still fair for an honest miner.


Close the two gaps
,

• Wipe a UID's history on every hotkey change (right now the reset doesn't seem to happen).
• Fade a UID's score once it stops trading, instead of letting old trades keep paying for ~15 hours.

#2 looks like the strongest single fix, and #3 and #4 together make feeding costly. Happy to help test any of these. Thanks!

[2026-09-28T19:38:18.729Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554215699654779052
@6/. @7/. I think there is still a different problem that proportional pay by itself does not solve.

The concern is not Sybil splitting. I understand that if one strategy produces contribution (C), splitting that same (C) across 10, 50, or 150 accounts does not increase the aggregate contribution under proportional pay.

The concern is Sybil-generated market flow.

If a coordinated operator controls a very large population of UIDs, those accounts can potentially act as counterparties for a smaller set of earning accounts. With enough feeder accounts, each earning account can trade against many different counterparties, so its flow no longer looks concentrated or private to a counterparty-diversity measure.

This matters because on the live board the accounts I am concerned about are showing CP factors around 0.72–0.79, not anything close to the 0.17 from the synthetic private-feeder example.

In that case the problem is not:

C → C₁ + C₂ + ... + Cₙ, where ΣCᵢ = C (edited)
Tuesday, September 29, 2026 at 3:39 AM

[2026-09-28T19:38:25.579Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554215728385630219
@6/. @7/. It is:

coordinated accounts create additional fills → those fills create additional measured making/skill contribution → most of that contribution survives because CP remains ~0.75

Proportional pay removes the rank advantage, but it does not remove contribution that was created by coordinated internal flow if the CP measure still considers most of that flow sufficiently diverse.

There may also be a feedback loop: more UIDs → larger counterparty pool → less concentrated-looking flow → more measured contribution survives the CP discount → more payout → ability to register still more UIDs.

So my specific question is:

If a coordinated population becomes large enough that its own feeder accounts start looking like “common counterparties” to the CP measure, what prevents internally generated flow from being treated as normal market contribution?

Have you stress-tested this with a coordinated population controlling more than 50% of the available UIDs, where feeders are deliberately distributed across many earning accounts, rather than with one fed account and a set of private feeders?

I think the most useful evidence would be the aggregate payout of the entire coordinated set, not the CP factor or payout of one account.

This also seems directly related to your comment that the current rule “does not yet ask how much of it the open market actually received.” If the current CP measure cannot remain Sybil-resistant once the coordinated population itself becomes a large part of the apparent market, then open-market-share weighting may be necessary rather than optional. (edited)
