@mvtrx・79 

0.6.2 Hotfix - Details for Miners 
,
A hotfix on the published 0.6.2. The version does not move, nothing in the agent interface or the notice formats changes, and agent code works unchanged. The validator restarts once to apply it; the simulation does not, so books, positions and the current scoring window carry on. Live on mainnet since 13:52 UTC today.

 One pay rule

Every round's pay is built by a single function, whichever way the pool is configured.

 A round carries one unit of weight

Each round's pay is normalised to sum to one before it enters the moving average, and a saved state is rescaled on load with the weights unchanged. A change of pay rule reaches the chain within a couple of hours. This restart produced no jump.

 Skill needs twenty qualifying books

Skill requires at least twenty books that clear the 2.3 basis point hurdle, and the pool gates on those books only.

 What you should see

Nothing to do on your side, and for almost every account no change in pay.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79

@6/. @7/.  There is one separate issue I think is still important after proportional pay, and this one is not about CP or splitting the same contribution across accounts.

The 500k/24h volume cap is per book, per UID. A newly registered UID therefore receives fresh per-book capacity.

What I am observing is an economically viable front-load-and-rotate strategy: a fresh UID uses a very large part of its available volume in only the first few simulation hours, creates a large current-window Making/Skill contribution, and benefits from that contribution for hours while it remains in the scoring window.

There is no reason for that operator to wait for the UID's 24h rolling capacity to recover. Once the useful capacity has been consumed, replacing the UID is economically cheaper than waiting, because the reward earned from the fresh capacity exceeds the marginal cost of registration, operation and replacement.

So this is not:

one contribution C split across many UIDs. (edited)

[2026-09-29T18:02:11.512Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554553898059038812
@6/.@7/.  It is:

new UID → fresh 500k/book capacity → additional executions → additional measured contribution → replace UID → fresh capacity again.

Proportional pay removes the rank advantage from splitting accounts, but it does not appear to remove the economic value of repeatedly obtaining fresh per-UID volume capacity.

The same applies even if the flow is legitimate open-market flow, so CP and open-market-share weighting do not by themselves solve this particular issue.

In effect, the 24h rolling cap constrains the lifetime behaviour of a persistent UID, while an operator that can profitably rotate disposable UIDs can repeatedly reset the resource that the cap is intended to limit.

Have you specifically stress-tested fresh-UID volume-cap recycling under the new pay rule?

More specifically: if an operator front-loads the 500k/book capacity of a UID into the first 3–5 simulation hours, earns from that contribution while it remains in the scoring window, then replaces the UID rather than waiting for the 24h capacity to recover, what mechanism makes repeated rotation no more profitable than keeping one UID and respecting the full rolling cycle?

If there is no mechanism tying the rolling volume budget across replacements, I think this remains a separate incentive from the rank/Sybil problem that proportional pay just fixed. (edited)

@6/.  @7/.  I think there may be a much simpler way to address the front-loading issue I am seeing.

If the relevant scoring window is 3 simulation hours, why is the per-book volume budget allowed to be concentrated from a 24h rolling cap into that much shorter scoring window?

With the current 500k/book/24h cap, a miner can front-load a very large part of the entire 24h allowance into the first 3–5 simulation hours. That produces a disproportionately large current Making/Skill contribution, and because simulation time progresses slowly relative to wall time, that strong window can remain economically valuable for many real-world hours.

Wouldn't it be cleaner to align the volume-control horizon with the scoring horizon while preserving exactly the same long-run allowed volume?

For example:

Current:
500,000 / book / 24h rolling

Equivalent 3h rate:
500,000 × 3 / 24 = 62,500 / book / 3h rolling

Both allow exactly the same average throughput:

20,833 notional per book per simulation hour.

The difference is that the 3h rolling limit prevents a miner from concentrating almost an entire day's volume budget into one scoring window.

This also makes disposable-UID rotation substantially less attractive. A fresh UID would no longer provide up to 500k/book of immediately usable capacity inside a 3h scoring window; it would provide only the amount corresponding to that same 3h rate.

It does not completely solve fresh-UID cap resets, but it removes most of the temporal advantage without changing the long-run volume allowance, the agent interface, CP logic, or proportional-pay formula.

Is there a reason the volume-cap horizon needs to remain 24h rather than being aligned with the scoring window at an equivalent rate?

More generally, have you checked whether 500k front-loaded into 3–5h earns materially more during its useful scoring lifetime than the equivalent volume supplied at the intended 24h rate? (edited)

[2026-09-29T19:16:43.090Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554572653216538758
You are misunderstanding the issue. I am not proposing a maximum order size, and I am not saying a trader should be prevented from trading whenever they want.

The protocol itself already imposes a 500k per-book rolling volume budget over 24 simulation hours. My question is about the mismatch between that 24h budget and the much shorter scoring window.

If using the entire 500k immediately gives the best score, as you suggest, that is exactly the incentive I am pointing out.

Two agents can have the same long-run permitted volume and the same execution quality:

A: uses 500k gradually over 24h
B: concentrates most of the same 500k into the first 3–5h

If B receives materially more reward because its contribution is concentrated inside the scoring window, then the scoring/cap horizons create an incentive to front-load rather than continuously provide liquidity.

I am therefore suggesting something completely different from “max 100 per order”:

500k / 24h = 62.5k / 3h

A 62.5k/3h rolling cap preserves exactly the same long-run permitted trading rate. It does not make the market less active over time. It only prevents a 24-hour allowance from being compressed into one short scoring window.

And there is a second issue: the cap is per UID. If a fresh UID receives fresh capacity, an operator for whom registration is profitable can front-load one UID, replace it, and repeat instead of waiting for the 24h rolling capacity to recover.

So “why don't you use 500k at once?” is actually the question: should the optimal scoring strategy really be to burn an entire 24h volume allowance as quickly as possible and then wait or rotate the UID?

That does not look like continuous market making to me. If the goal is to simulate a real market, I would expect the mechanism to reward useful liquidity provision over time rather than reward whoever concentrates the largest fraction of a 24h allowance into the shortest scoring period.

[2026-09-30T14:45:18.240Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554866737470636084
Thank you for the continued detailed analyses. 

Using the budget all at once is not the optimal strategy, it is a neutral one. Pay is a share of captured spread, linear in the fills, over a rolling window carried by a track record, so the same fills earn the same total whether they land in three hours or twenty-four, only paid out earlier. On the board, how concentrated an account's credit was in time has no relation to its pay per unit of credit. B does not out-earn A, and this is now a standing acceptance check. For the same reason 62.5k per 3h would change nothing an account earns; it would only cap ordinary bursts, and in a typical hour between a third and two thirds of the active accounts exceed that rate on some book.

Rotation is a capacity question, not a timing one. The cap is per agent, so a replacement starts with a fresh budget; what that costs is the registration burn, which the chain raises with the registration rate, and what it earns is only the spread it captures against real flow. This week the operators that replaced UIDs earn the same share on the new UIDs as on their standing ones, and the accounts at the cap hold about 3 per cent of emission.

We watch slot turnover, the replaced accounts' cap usage and fresh UIDs' pay, and we will act if rotation grows or fresh UIDs start out-earning standing ones.

[2026-09-30T18:55:29.999Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554929701351329934
I agree that executing the same 500k in 3h or 24h does not need to change its total pay. My concern is the fresh capacity from UID rotation.

Current registration cost is about 0.055 TAO (mostly ~0.01–0.08 recently), while the top miners are currently earning around 0.13–0.23 TAO/day.

With roughly 3 simulation hours taking ~24 real hours, an operator can front-load a UID's capacity, then replace it instead of waiting for the 24 simulation-hour rolling cap to recover.

A replacement UID does not need to outscore a standing UID for this to be profitable. It only needs the additional payout unlocked by its fresh 500k/book capacity to exceed the ~0.055 TAO registration burn.

So the question is simply:

Have you measured whether the incremental emission unlocked by a fresh UID before the old UID's capacity would recover is greater than the registration burn?

If yes, then registration is effectively a profitable way to buy fresh volume capacity, even though fast vs slow execution of the same fills is payout-neutral.

[2026-09-30T19:27:24.349Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554937730717327381
@6/.  I think we are talking past each other, so let me try a simple race analogy.

Imagine the same race has 10 marathon runners and 10 sprinters, and only the top 10 positions are continuously paid.

A marathon runner has a 40 km cycle. A sprinter can extract the useful value of his allowance after only 100 m.

The sprinter finishes his 100 m quickly, enters the paid positions and earns a prize. The important part is that the prize is larger than the entry fee.

He then pays the entry fee again and is allowed to register a fresh sprinter into the same race while the marathon is still running:

Sprinter 1 → 100 m → gets paid → replaced
Sprinter 2 → 100 m → gets paid → replaced
Sprinter 3 → 100 m → gets paid → replaced
...

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-09-30T19:27:42.988Z] snakesss
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1554937808894820353
@6/.  Meanwhile the marathon runner is still running his original 40 km.

By the time the marathon runner reaches the finish, multiple generations of sprinters have already occupied the paid positions and collected rewards. The marathon runner may complete his entire race and earn nothing at all, because the paid positions kept being occupied by fresh sprinters.

That is the part I think is missing from the “same fills earn the same total whether they happen in 3h or 24h” argument.

I am not saying that running the same 500k faster makes those 500k intrinsically worth more.

I am saying that a UID can use its economically useful capacity quickly, collect reward, and then be replaced by a fresh UID with a fresh 500k/book budget, while a persistent UID is still waiting for its 24 simulation-hour rolling capacity to recover.

With roughly 3 simulation hours taking ~24 real hours, this difference is enormous in wall-clock time.

And today the entry economics matter: registration is around 0.055 TAO, while leading miners are showing roughly 0.13–0.23 TAO/day.

So if a fresh UID can earn more than its registration cost before its capacity becomes constrained, the rational strategy is:

use → earn → replace → use → earn → replace

rather than:

use → wait for the 24h rolling capacity to recover.

The persistent “marathon” miner can therefore behave correctly for the entire cycle and still earn nothing, while disposable “sprinter” UIDs repeatedly enter the paid set and are replaced.

That is the economic issue I am asking about: does fresh registration allow profitable recycling of per-UID capacity faster than a persistent UID can naturally recover it?

[2026-10-01T13:31:42.269Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1555210603411284091
@snakesss Some additional measurements at the operator level over the last seven days, to complete the analysis.

The race you describe was the ladder, and the ladder is gone. Under it, operators that registered and lost slots continuously took almost all of the emission. Since proportional pay went live on 28 September they take about their share of the slots, on an unchanged registration rate, and a persistent account is paid every window for what it captures.

What is left is smaller: a replaced slot still earns more in its first day than a seasoned slot does, because its standing starts fresh. It is bounded, since each registration pays the burn and competes with every other fresh slot for the same windows, and it is a newcomer-standing question rather than a pay-rule question.

@τourisτ @victor  on the wash trading: we read the set you point at on the newest scoring window. The counterparty factor already removes part of its making credit, and under proportional pay its share of the pool has fallen by about two thirds since Sunday. It is still paid for some of the flow it supplies to itself, which is what you are seeing.

Measures to address both are being evaluated for the next release, in the credit and in how a new UID earns its standing - changes of this kind go out with a full acceptance run and a testnet soak behind them, not as a hotfix. 

Lowering the making weight would take pay from every maker, honest or not, and move it to the skill half while leaving that set's share of the making half unchanged, so the weight stays. Until then we watch slot turnover, what a replaced slot earns against the registration cost, and the set's share of the pool on every read.

Thank you again for the observations and detailed assessments.

@mvtrx・79  Status Update

 0.6.2 on mainnet
0.6.2 is running with significant improvements that answer the points miners raised and what we observed ourselves: an account's place in the skill half depends only on its own trading, not on the size of other accounts; both halves pay in proportion, the making half to the liquidity each account supplies to the market and the skill half to the trading skill it shows; fills concentrated from a few counterparties count less.

Since the 28 September update, emission follows liquidity actually supplied to the market. The liquidity miners supply has more than doubled, the volume miners take with aggressive orders has fallen by three quarters, and about two thirds of maker fills now come from market flow rather than from other miners' orders, up from a third or less. The share of emission that went to accounts cycling registrations rather than consistently trading has fallen to a few per cent.

 0.6.3
In final preparation, targeting next week. It brings the first multi-asset simulation, on a second market configuration finalised through SimTRX, our automated calibration tools, along with further scoring refinements drawn from our monitoring and observations.

 TradingView and anonymous access
The TradingView integration is ready, pending a few updates for license compliance. It launches together with anonymous access once those are cleared, targeted for next week.

 Testing and monitoring
Our acceptance suites, monitoring and reporting tools, including SOAIM, keep improving and expanding.

 TOKEN2049
Three of our team are heading to TOKEN2049 in Singapore.

 In parallel
Automated swaps, the API, dashboards and configurable alerts are progressing alongside, though our priority sits on scoring, live market preparations and marketing.

Follow along on X: https://x.com/mvtrx_79

[2026-10-05T01:17:25.678Z] victor
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1556475368137826305
@6/. Under the current reward structure, it is nearly impossible to reduce registration costs. The system encourages many miners to re-register repeatedly in order to remain competitive, which increases unnecessary registration activity and makes the overall model less sustainable.

At the same time, many miners are currently using relatively weak or inefficient trading strategies, yet they can still compete mainly through repeated registration and higher turnover rather than better trading quality.

Because of this, I think the current reward logic should be reconsidered and upgraded. The reward system should place more weight on trading quality, consistency, efficiency, and long-term performance, similar to how the system worked before. This would reduce the incentive for constant re-registration and encourage miners to improve their actual trading strategies instead of relying on short-term volume or fresh registration advantages.

The goal should be to reward miners that generate sustainable, high-quality performance over time, rather than creating a structure where frequent re-registration becomes the most effective strategy.

@mvtrx・79 

MVTRX 0.6.3 - Multi-Asset Simulation on Testnet 
,
0.6.3 is on testnet from today and brings the first multi-asset simulation. Alongside the existing market there is a second asset class with a character of its own: wider spreads, fewer fills and a choppier path, so a strategy tuned for one market needs its own sizing and distances in the other.

Scoring builds on what we have seen on mainnet. Making now rewards quotes that still hold their value after they fill, so liquidity that serves the market pays and liquidity the market runs straight over does not. Credit from trading against other miners is tied to what an account offers the open market. Each asset class is paid separately, with the new one starting small while it proves itself.

Mainnet follows in two steps, both dated here in advance. The validator update may reach mainnet ahead of the next run boundary; the second class and the new making basis start at the boundary.

 For miners

Rebuild from the published tree. A few small changes let an agent size and quote each book on its own grid and minimum and know which asset class it is trading; the default example agents show how. The details are in the post below.

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

[2026-10-06T16:48:13.610Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1557071999208132682
@mvtrx・79 

0.6.3 - Details for Miners 
,
Companion to the 0.6.3 announcement. Testnet runs 0.6.3 from 6 October. Mainnet follows in two steps, dated in advance: the validator update, which brings the tether on miner-sourced credit, may land ahead of the next run boundary; the second class and the new making basis start at the boundary.

 What you must do


Pull the published tree and restart your miner: the miner neuron and the protocol package changed. A 0.6.2 agent loads and runs unchanged; there is no API or wire change.
,
On the second asset class (books 96 to 127), size to the book's minimum, 2.5364 units, with self.min_order_size(book_id); round per book with self.round_price and self.round_volume; and scale any price-unit parameter (offsets, spreads, thresholds) to the book's price, about a tenth of simulation_0's. self.class_of(book_id) (simulation_0, simulation_1; exchange on the exchange mechanism) and self.asset_classes() tell the classes apart. Otherwise orders below 2.5364 units are rejected there and price-unit parameters are ten times too large.
,
If you implemented process, review it: notifications the validator sends outside the state update now reach it on a live miner. Simulation start and end still arrive in the state update and fire onStart and onEnd. No response is required.
,
On the exchange mechanism a book id is the pool's netuid, so ids need not start at zero or be contiguous: iterate simulation_config.book_ids, not range(book_count).
,

 What you should know


128 books in two asset classes. Books 0 to 95 are simulation_0, the original calibrated market. Books 96 to 127 are simulation_1, a second calibrated market at a tenth of the price with order sizes and the minimum order ten times larger, so a minimum order has the same notional. It has the same agent types and fundamental process, but its background traders are calibrated differently: its market makers quote far less tightly and its other traders react on shorter horizons. Both classes quote on 2 price and 4 volume decimals, so a simulation_1 tick is ten times larger relative to price.
,
Capital stays per book, each with its own balances and volume allowance (ten times its starting capital per simulated day). Nothing moves between books or classes.
,
Mainnet runs simulation_0 on all 128 books today. At the boundary, books 96 to 127 become simulation_1: they reprice from about 300 to about 30, and their minimum order rises from 0.25 to 2.5364 units.
,
The distributed proxy in agents/proxy/ reads the two-class layout (config.multiasset.example.json shows the shape).
,

------------------------------------------------------------

[2026-10-06T16:48:15.434Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1557072006858674256
 What to expect on simulation_1


Wider spreads and fewer fills, more impact for size, directional moves that run further before they are closed in, and a choppier path at a daily volatility similar to simulation_0. A strategy calibrated on simulation_0 needs its own sizing and distances there.
,

 How the scoring changes affect you


Making pays on quote quality: your two-sided captured spread, as before, multiplied by the share of it your maker fills still hold 20 simulation seconds later, summed over all your fills and capped between 0 and 1. A maker the market runs over keeps none of its making credit, nobody earns more than before, and taking never earns making credit. The mark is set by prints with the background market on at least one side, so prints arranged between miners do not move it. Quoting width, and how long a quote rests in front of flow, are what is priced. Both bases are published.
,
Making credit is tied to open-market service: fills against other miners count only up to four times your fills against the background market, so making credit is scaled by (background + min(miner-sourced, 4 x background)) / total. A maker with at least 20 per cent of its maker volume against the background market is untouched.
,
Each asset class is paid through its own share, 0.95 for simulation_0 and 0.05 for simulation_1 at launch, with the second expected to step up as it proves itself on mainnet. Shares, the counterparty factor and the skill bar are judged per class: 15 of 96 and 5 of 32 books.
,
Unchanged: proportional pay for both halves, w_make 0.50, the presence gate, the counterparty factor, de-beta at weight 1.0 and the volume allowance. Age plays no part: the same performance pays the same.
,
The dashboards' Scoring Config table shows the making basis, horizon, tether, class weights and skill bar each validator runs.
,

Code and setup: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

Join our Discord for support and to share feedback: https://discord.gg/372ec3U8mv
Link: https://github.com/taos-im/sn-79/tree/test

[2026-10-08T13:18:50.816Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1557744082762334298
@mvtrx・79 

0.6.3 Final - Details for Miners 
,
Companion to the 0.6.3 final announcement. The 6 October details still describe the release as a whole; this covers what the final tree adds. Testnet moves to it now. Mainnet validators update on Friday 9 October and pay making on the captured basis, as 0.6.2 does; the second class and the realized basis arrive with the next simulation changeover. Pull the published tree and restart: the protocol package, the miner library, the engine and the launchers all change.

 What you must do


Pull the published tree and restart. An agent built for the 6 October release runs unchanged, and a 0.6.2 agent still loads and runs.
,
If your agent logs book-check warnings after the update, look at them: what remains is real.
,
Testnet opened a new simulation run at 12:55 UTC today, after an issue resuming the previous run on the validator host.
,

 Scoring


The realized mark comes only from the open market. A maker fill is marked 20 simulation seconds later against the size-weighted average of background-sided prints around the horizon. The mark looks outward up to four windows each way for the nearest such prints; a fill with none in reach books no realized spread. Each fill's realized spread is capped at plus or minus its own captured spread, so one fill moves your markout quality by at most its own share of your fills.
,
The markout matures on the prints' own clock, at the 20 second horizon on simulation time.
,
Both bases are visible. Your captured and realized making credit, and which one pays, are on your miner gauges and in the Agents table of the validators dashboard. The agents dashboard draws your making credit, ranks, factors and books within each asset class, following the asset-class selector, beside the whole-miner lines that pay.
,
Unchanged: the capture reference keeps its 0.6.2 definition, w_make 0.50, the tether at 4, class weights 0.95 and 0.05, the per-class skill bar, the presence gate, the counterparty factor, de-beta at weight 1.0 and the per-book turnover budget. Nothing is paid for tenure.
,

 Miner library and launchers


Book check. L2Snapshot.compare matches a level within half a volume increment and ignores reconstructed levels beyond the published depth when the publisher's side is full. A published cancellation now carries its side (s) and the cancelled order's leverage (l), so book replays place it on the side it names and handle leveraged orders at their leveraged volume. The library reads both fields for you.
,
Per-book decimals in the history helper. taos.im.utils.history.decimals_for(volume_decimals, book_id) reads the volume decimals of the book in hand, and the state history manager reads each book's own class configuration. Agents that replay the book from events need no change.
,
Launchers install against the lockfile on every start: run_miner.sh and run_validator.sh run pip install -e . -c constraints.txt.
,

[2026-10-14T01:03:16.828Z] salmano
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1559733298593271819
Security disclosure — fundamental-price RNG is reconstructable from public data

Hi @6/. — I run miners on SN79. Flagging a scoring-integrity issue in how the fundamental price (F) is generated. Happy to share a full write-up and an offline proof.

The issue. F is reseeded every 30 s with

seed = round(BTC_price × 100) + bookId × 10      // FundamentalPrice.cpp:83
where BTC_price comes from the public Coinbase/Binance trade feed (validator/seed.py) and the generator is the open-source mt19937 process. Every input is public and the generator is non-cryptographic.

Impact. Any participant running the published generator on the same public feed can reconstruct the next F exactly, ahead of publication, for every book — a deterministic match (~100%), versus ~2⁻⁶⁴ under a keyed design. That lets a miner pre-position for the next F move with near-certainty and collect skill/making reward with little risk, degrading the signal for honest miners. It's invisible to statistical checks (mt19937 scrambles the seed, so BTC-vs-F correlation ≈ 0) but trivial by replay — the scramble defeats regression, not reconstruction.

You can easily know that many of the top miners esitmate F 30 sim-s before publish and they retain 40 sim-s maker orders all day long. (edited)
Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 9:03 AM

[2026-10-14T14:31:33.359Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1559936707787358222
Thanks @salmano and @richard. Short answer: yes, many miners trade on the fundamental, and that's fine, because it's public. It is published for every book on the dashboards, and from 0.6.4 (on testnet now, mainnet on Friday 16 October) every miner also receives it in its state update each round, so everyone gets it at the same moment, without having to fetch it separately.

What no one can do is work it out from the seed. We tested that directly on the current mainnet run: for 60 steps we tried every seed from a window of 20,000 recorded BTC prices around each step, so feed timing doesn't come into it, and none reproduced a single step.

The fundamental is also not a perfect predictor of the price, and the background market will follow it less closely as the simulation adds more exogenous signals and rare shocks (e.g. "black swans"). If you have a reconstruction that matches a past book and time, please DM it and we'll check it against the logs. (edited)

[2026-10-20T09:53:52.296Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1562041153417912373
@lemcrarz you read it right, thanks. The validator's clock for each miner starts before its request is prepared and signed, and a round's requests are prepared in uid order, so low uids are recorded slow for the validator's reasons, not yours. The effect is small but systematic: about 4 ms of simulated delay between those two groups, so a low uid's instructions reach the book a little later than they should.

The next validator update randomises the order the miners are queried in each round, which restores fairness without touching the communication path, since that needs significant careful testing. The release after it fixes the underlying delays. 0.6.5 is expected on testnet later this week and on mainnet after a few days of observation; 0.6.6 follows once the data from running 0.6.5 is in.

On roles: yes, intended. Pay is split half and half: the making half pays for quoting both sides of the book, so only makers can earn it; the skill half pays any miner, maker or taker, for the alpha in its trades once the price drift is removed. Takers are not behind there: today they hold just over half of the skill half with fewer uids than the makers. A maker with skill earns in both halves because it does both jobs the market needs. We do not plan to fix roles per hotkey. The makers' figure you saw climbing is a total that counts up from zero over each simulation run and resets when the next run starts, so it rises through the day. The share of pay going to making stays at one half; what you saw was the total growing, not makers getting a bigger share.

https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1562069523371270206

[2026-10-20T12:05:42.493Z] 6/.
https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1353733356470276096/1562074331188568105
The pay is split half making, half skill, and the split is fixed. Takers are paid from the skill half for trades that go with the next move; a taker that trades against it earns nothing and drops off, which is intended. Today most of the skill half goes to takers.

The top of the board is makers because a maker that also reads the market earns from both halves.

If everyone quoted, the making half would be shared ever thinner while the skill half paid the few remaining takers very well, which pulls miners back. So no, we are not worried, but we watch for it, and the weight between the halves is a dial we can move.
